> ## Agent Instructions
> Prefer the qBraid CLI for programmatic platform actions: pip install 'qbraid-cli>=0.12', then run `qbraid configure` once with an API key from https://account.qbraid.com/account/api-keys.
> When writing Python, prefer the qBraid SDK: `from qbraid.runtime import QbraidProvider` wraps devices, job submission (`device.run()`), and batch groups (`GroupJobSession`).
> Always install the latest packages (pip install -U qbraid qbraid-cli); do not pin versions from memory. qbraid-cli below 0.12.0 is incompatible with the current API.
> Device IDs use the QRN format vendor:provider:type:name (e.g. qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv, rigetti:rigetti:qpu:cepheus-1-108q). Legacy underscore IDs are deprecated.
> The REST API base URL is https://api-v2.qbraid.com/api/v1, authenticated with an X-API-Key header.
> For endpoints without a dedicated wrapper, use `QbraidSessionV1` from `qbraid_core` — an authenticated session (`.get()`/`.post()`) that sets the X-API-Key header. Full spec: https://docs.qbraid.com/openapi-v2.json
> Free simulators cost no credits; QPU and GPU jobs consume credits. Surface the estimated cost to the user before submitting a paid job.
> For account signup, API keys, credits, and end-to-end action recipes, see https://qbraid.com/llms.txt.

# On-demand pricing
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/pricing

Understand credits, resource billing units, AI token rates, and subscription allowances.

## Credits

The standard exchange rate is **100 qBraid credits = $1 USD**. A job priced at $3.80 uses 380 credits. [Buy credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits) from your wallet, then check the selected workspace's balance before you run paid resources.

Credit purchases, personal plans, and team plans are separate purchases. A plan provides resource allowances. Credits pay for eligible usage outside those allowances or for resources billed on demand. Review the rate and total shown in the application before checkout or launch.

## Subscription plans

| Plan     | Monthly | Annual | CPU hours per month | Storage | AI allowance per quota period |
| -------- | ------: | -----: | ------------------: | ------: | ----------------------------: |
| Free     |      $0 |     $0 |                 100 |   15 GB |                            $5 |
| Standard |     $20 |   $192 |                 400 |   50 GB |                           $15 |
| Pro      |    $100 |   $960 |               2,000 |  150 GB |                           $50 |

Annual subscriptions are billed yearly, equivalent to $16 per month for Standard and $80 per month for Pro. Team plans use the same per-seat prices with a minimum of two seats. Enterprise plans use custom terms.

See [Personal subscriptions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/subscriptions) or [Team subscriptions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/subscriptions) for benefits and management instructions. Use **Account > Usage** to check your effective allowance and renewal date.

## Quantum computers

Open [Devices](https://account.qbraid.com/devices) and inspect the selected QPU's pricing. Device availability and rates can change. A QPU can use a per-task fee, per-shot fee, execution-time fee, or a combination.

A shot is one execution of a quantum program. A task submits a program with a chosen shot count. For a device with task and shot pricing, estimate credits as:

```text
per-task credits + number of shots × per-shot credits
```

For time-based devices, the execution-time charge depends on the device's billing rules. Review the job's estimate and final charge. Do not apply one provider's minimum duration or rounding rules to another provider.

If you connect your own provider account, review that provider's billing terms as well. See [Open Quantum](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/integrations/openquantum) for its account and credit setup.

## Quantum circuit simulators

Use the [device catalog](https://account.qbraid.com/devices) for current simulator availability and rates. Some simulators have no qBraid usage charge, while others charge for execution. A simulator's price and daily job quota are separate constraints.

For qBraid-managed daily simulator quotas, Free allows 100 jobs per simulator per UTC day and Standard allows 500. Pro has no daily job-count limit for these managed simulators. This does not make a paid simulator free or remove provider-specific limits. The GPU simulators are the exception, described below.

### GPU simulators

The [GPU simulators](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/gpu-simulators), `qbraid:qbraid:sim:gpu-sv` and `qbraid:qbraid:sim:gpu-tn`, each have a smaller daily allowance of circuits, and jobs inside it are free. A single job is one circuit, and a batch counts one per circuit:

| Plan       | Free circuits per GPU simulator per UTC day |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------: |
| Free       |                                          25 |
| Standard   |                                         125 |
| Pro        |                                   Unlimited |
| Enterprise |                                   Unlimited |

Once you have used the day's allowance, further jobs on that simulator are refused until 00:00 UTC unless you turn on **Usage-based billing for GPU simulators** in [Account > Usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage#simulator-usage). With it on, each further job is charged from your credits at the simulator's per-minute price, 5 credits ($0.05) per minute of execution, with a minimum of 3 seconds (0.25 credits) per single-circuit job. A 14.3-second job costs about 1.19 credits. A job that fails is not charged, and a batch where some circuits fail is charged for its full execution time. The setting is off unless you turn it on.

## CPUs and GPUs

qBraid offers subscription compute that consumes CPU hours and on-demand compute that consumes credits. See [Usage limits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/usage-limits) for CPU-hour accounting and credit overflow settings.

### Subscription instances

CPU hours count allocated vCPUs multiplied by elapsed hours. A two-vCPU instance running for three hours consumes six CPU hours. When an instance uses your remaining plan allowance, that usage does not deduct on-demand credits.

If you enable **Auto-switch to Credits**, eligible usage beyond the compute allowance can spend wallet credits. Check the instance's credit rate before you enable this setting. AI's auto-switch policy is a separate setting.

### On-demand instances

Inspect the current compute profile for its CPU or GPU configuration and effective rate before you launch. Profile catalogs and prices can change, so the launch screen is the reference for available configurations.

The personal plan cards advertise on-demand compute discounts of 10% for Standard and 18% for Pro. The billed compute rate uses the configured tier discount, so compare the effective rate shown for your selected workspace. Storage charges are separate and do not use the compute discount.

See [On-demand instances](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/on-demand-instances) for lifecycle and billing details, or [GPUs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/gpus) for GPU access.

#### GPU instances

Select a GPU profile by GPU model, count, memory, and availability in the compute catalog. Check the displayed rate and any separate storage cost.

#### CPU instances

Select a CPU profile by vCPU count and memory. For CLI workflows, use the current profile's identifier with [qBraid compute](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid_compute).

## AI models

The model picker displays separate input and output rates in **credits per million tokens**. [Models and pricing](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/models) includes the current documented model-rate reference and instructions for querying the live catalog.

AI usage draws from your plan's allowance first. Usage beyond the allowance can spend credits when your effective auto-switch policy permits it. See [AI usage quotas](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/user-guide/usage-quotas).

## Review charges

Use [Wallet payment history](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/payment-history) for your workspace's credit activity and personal Stripe invoices. Organization administrators use [Billing transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) and the separate **Invoices** tab for organization purchases.


# Learn with qBook
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/learning

Find courses in Account and open chapters and sections in qBook.

The **Learn** page in qBraid Account lists the courses available to you. Course materials open in [qBook](https://qbook.qbraid.com).

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50npvaG1hMYdeImDjWbCTznZ2Xo6wkuK0Ec1JiU"
    alt="Learn page with course level shortcuts and available course cards"
  />
</Frame>

Use All Courses to search the available learning material.

## Open a course

1. Open [Learn](https://account.qbraid.com/learn).
2. Search by a word in the course title or description.
3. Open the course details to inspect its chapters, sections, instructor, and progress.
4. Select **Launch in qBook** to open the course in a new tab.

You can also open an available chapter or section directly from the course contents. A launch control is unavailable when that content does not have a valid launch target.

Course links carry the course's organization context so qBook can open the material in the correct organization. Use the same qBraid account that has access to the course.

## Resume your work

The course detail page shows progress returned by the course service. **Launch in qBook** opens a chapter with recorded progress when one is available, or the first chapter otherwise.

If the course list is empty, clear the search and check your account and organization access. If a request fails, use **Retry**. If a course cannot launch, return to its details or open qBook directly.

For standalone notebooks and experiments, see [qBraid Lab](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/getting-started). For recommended quantum learning resources, use [AI Chat](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/user-guide/ai-chat).


# Migration Guide
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/migration

qBraid is migrating to a new Generation-2 platform. Below is what you need to know and what to do before and after the migration.

## Migration window

- **When:** Sunday, February 8th, 10:00 AM–2:00 PM CT (4 hours)
- **Impact:** The platform and all associated services will be unavailable during this window.

## What carries over

- **Files** — All of your files from the legacy platform will be migrated.
- **Credits** — All qBraid credits will carry over **except** promotional credits (e.g., credits from access codes). Only credits purchased with a credit card or transferred to you within an organization will be migrated.
- **Organizations** — Organizations will carry over with no service interruption.

## What does not carry over (and what to do)

### Quantum jobs

Quantum jobs data will **not** be migrated. On the new account **Jobs** page you will see a download option to export all legacy quantum jobs data as a JSON file. You can then load and work with that data (results and metadata) using the qBraid-SDK as usual.

For detailed instructions on retrieving and working with your legacy jobs, see the [Legacy Jobs Retrieval](https://docs.qbraid.com/home/legacy-jobs) guide.

### Transactions

Transactions will **not** be migrated. You can download your legacy transactions as a JSON file from **Account** > **Wallet** on the new platform.

### Submitting jobs after migration

To submit quantum jobs on the new platform, use either the updated [quantum jobs and devices API endpoints](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/user-guide/overview) or:

- **qBraid-SDK** version 0.11.0 or higher
- **qBraid-CORE** version 0.2.0 or higher

Older versions of the SDK and CORE are not compatible with the new API.

## Subscribers (Standard and Pro)

You will need to renew your qBraid subscription to keep access to Standard or Pro.

1. Log in to the new [account page](https://account.qbraid.com/).
2. Go to **Account** > **Wallet**.
3. Select your previous subscription tier and complete checkout.

Previous subscribers will receive an email with a promotional code for **1 month free** when they resubscribe.

## Beta users (V2 early access)

If you participated in the qBraid V2 beta: **all data on the current beta platform will be wiped** at migration (jobs, transactions, credits, and files). None of it will persist.

- Download any data you need before the migration.
- Use any remaining credits, or they will be lost.

## Questions

For questions about the migration or any of the above, contact [contact@qbraid.com](mailto:contact@qbraid.com).


# Legacy Jobs Retrieval
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/legacy-jobs

Following the migration to qBraid's V2 platform, quantum jobs from the legacy platform are no longer directly accessible through the new API. However, you can download and work with your legacy jobs data using the instructions below.

<Warning>
**Schema Changes**

Legacy jobs will **not** match the schema of the new runtime jobs in API V2. If you're working with both legacy and new jobs, be aware that their data structures and field names will differ.

For more details, see the [API Reference for V2 Jobs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/rest/get-quantum-jobs).

</Warning>

## Downloading legacy jobs data

1. Log in to your qBraid account at [account.qbraid.com](https://account.qbraid.com/)
2. Navigate to the **Jobs** page
3. Look for the **Download Old Jobs** option
4. Click to export all your legacy quantum jobs as a JSON file
5. Save the JSON file to your local machine

## Displaying legacy jobs with qBraid-SDK

Once you've downloaded your legacy jobs JSON file, you can view the jobs data using the qBraid-SDK.

### Prerequisites

Ensure you have qBraid-SDK version `0.10.2` installed:

```bash
pip install 'qbraid==0.10.2'
```

### Loading the data

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Retrieving jobs">
```python
from qbraid.runtime import QbraidProvider

# Path to the legacy jobs JSON file

legacy_jobs_path = 'legacy_jobs.json'

# Initialize the provider with the legacy jobs path

provider = QbraidProvider(legacy_jobs_path=legacy_jobs_path)

# Display the first 5 jobs

print(provider.display_jobs(max_results=5))

````
</Tab>
<Tab title="Output">
```python
Displaying 5/5 jobs matching query:

Job ID    | Submitted                 | Status
--------- | ------------------------- | ---------------
<job_id_1> | 2025-12-31 T17:52:46.850Z | COMPLETED
<job_id_2> | 2025-11-06 T13:29:16.031Z | FAILED
<job_id_3> | 2025-10-31 T17:52:44.674Z | CANCELLED
<job_id_4> | 2025-10-31 T17:52:42.551Z | COMPLETED
<job_id_5> | 2025-10-28 T09:32:11.508Z | COMPLETED
````

</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Functionality and limitations

Once the `QbraidProvider` is initialized with the legacy jobs JSON path, you can only use the `display_jobs()` method to display the jobs.

Methods that interface with the API, such as `get_device()`, will **not** work when using legacy jobs. This is because device information is not available through the old API endpoints.

<Note>
  For full functionality including device access and job submission, upgrade to
  qBraid-SDK version **0.11.0 or greater** and use the new V2 API endpoints. See
  the [V2 SDK documentation](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/overview) for details.
</Note>

## Retrieving job details with qbraid-core

For more detailed information about individual jobs, you can use the **qbraid-core** library, which provides direct access to job metadata and results.

### Prerequisites

Install qbraid-core version`0.1.50`:

```bash
pip install 'qbraid-core==0.1.50'
```

### Using QuantumClient

The `QuantumClient` accepts the same legacy jobs JSON path parameter and provides methods for retrieving detailed job information:

```python
from qbraid_core.services.quantum import QuantumClient

# Initialize the client with the legacy jobs JSON path
legacy_jobs_path = 'legacy_jobs.json'
client = QuantumClient(legacy_jobs_path=legacy_jobs_path)

# List all jobs
jobs_list = client.search_jobs()

# display the first 5 jobs
print(jobs_list[:5])

# Get detailed information for a specific job
job_id = jobs_list[0]['qbraidJobId']
job_details = client.get_job(job_id)
print(job_details)
```

### Available methods

- **`search_jobs()`** - Returns a list of all legacy jobs
- **`get_job(job_id)`** - Retrieves detailed metadata for a specific job
- **`get_job_result(job_id)`** - Fetches the results and measurements for a completed job

## Need help?

If you encounter any issues retrieving or working with your legacy jobs data, contact [contact@qbraid.com](mailto:contact@qbraid.com).

## Related

- [Migration Guide](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/migration) - Learn about the platform migration
- [V2 Documentation](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/introduction) - Get started with the new platform
- [qBraid-SDK Documentation](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk) - Full SDK reference


# FAQ
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/faq

Frequently asked questions about the V2 platform.

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Where did my credits go?">
Only credits purchased with a credit card or transferred to you within an organization were migrated from the legacy platform. Promotional credits (e.g., those redeemed via access codes) did not carry over and have expired.

If your credits lived in an organization (purchased or transferred there), check that you're viewing that organization. "qBraid Default" in the upper left means you're in your default workspace. Click the organization name to open the dropdown, switch to the correct organization, and the balance will update.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Where did my quantum jobs go?">
  Quantum jobs data was not migrated from the legacy platform. To get your old
  jobs data, go to **Jobs** on your [account page](https://account.qbraid.com/)
  and click **Download Old Jobs Data**. You can work with that data using the
  qBraid-SDK. See [Legacy Jobs Retrieval](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/legacy-jobs) for details.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Where did my files go?">
  Lab uses a [file sync](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/file-sync) mechanism, so your files
  can take a few minutes to appear after you launch. Once you're in Lab, check
  the file sync indicator in the bottom toolbar to see progress. You can keep
  working while files populate in the background; after a few minutes, your
  files should be fully restored.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What are CPU hours?">
  CPU hours measure usage as (number of vCPUs) × (hours used). For example, a
  2-vCPU instance for 3 hours uses 6 CPU hours; an 8-vCPU instance for 2 hours
  uses 16 CPU hours. See [Usage Limits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/usage-limits) for
  more.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Why does launching Lab fail with 'Compute hours exhausted and insufficient credits'?">
  You've used all the compute hours included with your plan for this month, and
  you don't have credits set up to cover the session instead. Either [upgrade
  your subscription](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/subscriptions#subscribe-or-upgrade) for a larger
  monthly allocation, or [buy
  credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits#how-to-buy) and turn on [auto-switch
  to credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/usage-limits#auto-switch-to-credits). Both
  steps are needed, since credits only cover CPU sessions when auto-switch is
  on. See the full walkthrough in
  [Troubleshooting](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/troubleshooting#launch-failed-compute-hours-exhausted).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What is auto-switch to credits?">
  Your qBraid account has usage limits for AI chat and CPU hours. If you reach a
  limit, you can "switch to credits" and keep using that service. Usage is then
  billed in qBraid credits instead of counting against the quota. Those charges
  appear on your account under **Transactions**. The GPU simulators have a
  similar setting, **Usage-based billing for GPU simulators**, for jobs past
  their free daily allowance. See [Simulator
  usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage#turn-on-usage-based-billing-for-gpu-simulators).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Why don't my environments show up in Lab? It says 'Workspace Empty'.">
  After you launch Lab, [files can take a few minutes to sync](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/file-sync). When sync finishes, refresh the Environment Manager in the sidebar and your environments should appear.

If sync has completed and you've refreshed Environment Manager but it still says "Workspace Empty," you don't have any environments installed yet. Click **Add** in the Environment Manager, then [install an environment](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/environments#install-environment) to get started.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What does 'No Capacity' mean next to a GPU instance?">
  It means all GPU instances of that type are currently in use due to high
  demand. Try again later or choose another instance type.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What is 'qBraid Default' in the upper left of my account page?">
  On qBraid, you can belong to multiple organizations (e.g., courses, teams, or your own qBraid Default workspace). Credits and context are per-organization. The name in the upper left shows which organization you're in, and switching it changes which credits and resources you see.

**qBraid Default** is your own workspace: your own credits and work, separate from any course or other org you've joined. Credits here are yours (purchased or held in your name), and you have full control with no shared management.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Why do I need to generate API keys to launch lab?">
  API keys authenticate you with qBraid services. When you launch Lab, we check
  for credentials in `~/.qbraid/qbraidrc`. If none are found, we prompt you to
  create an API key and save it there so Lab, extensions, and the qBraid-SDK
  work without extra setup. For more on creating and managing keys, see [API
  Keys](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/api-keys).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="I ran out of CPU hours and can't access my files. What do I do?">
  When you exhaust your CPU hours, "Launch Lab" is blocked. Your files remain
  available without launching Lab. Go to **Dashboard** on your [account
  page](https://account.qbraid.com/), scroll to **Usage Overview** at the
  bottom, and click **Download Files**. See [Download your
  files](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage#download-your-files). To start launching again,
  either upgrade your plan or set up credits, as described in
  [Troubleshooting](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/troubleshooting#launch-failed-compute-hours-exhausted).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I submit quantum jobs to IBM devices through qBraid?">
  No. To run jobs on IBM devices you must use your own IBM credentials. qBraid
  does support direct access to other QPUs, including Rigetti, IQM, AQT,
  IonQ, Pasqal, QuEra, and more. See the [full list of
  devices](https://account.qbraid.com/devices) on your account page.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

For account creation, email codes, Google sign-in, and passkeys, see [Sign in](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/sign-in).

qBraid Default is your individual workspace. Organizations have their own members, credits, subscriptions, and permissions. Your profile is personal, while resource and billing pages use the selected workspace.

# Sign in
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/sign-in

Create an account and sign in with Google, a password, an email code, or a passkey.

Open [qBraid Account](https://account.qbraid.com/signin). Choose the sign-in method available for your account.

## Use your email

Enter your email address and continue. If a registered passkey is available, your device can prompt you to use it. Otherwise, select an available method, such as your password or **Email a code**.

For an email code, check your inbox and enter the code in the sign-in form. Accounts that use Google sign-in do not use this email-code flow. Return to **Sign in with Google** for those accounts.

Use [Reset your password](#reset-your-password) if you need to recover an email-and-password account.

## Reset your password

1. Open [Reset Password](https://account.qbraid.com/forgot-password).
2. Enter your account email and select **Send Reset Code**.
3. Enter the six-digit code from your email.
4. Enter and confirm a new password. It must contain at least eight characters, including a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, a number, and a special character.
5. Select **Reset Password**. After success, the page returns you to sign-in.

Select **Use a different email** if you entered the wrong address. If the reset fails, review the error before trying again. Accounts registered through Google should use **Sign in with Google**.

## Use Google

Select **Sign in with Google** and choose the Google account associated with your qBraid account.

## Create an account

Open [Sign up](https://account.qbraid.com/signup). Register with Google or complete the email registration form, including the password requirements shown there. Complete email verification if prompted.

If you arrived through an organization invitation, finish registration and return to the invitation to accept it. See [Join an organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invitations).

## Complete first-login setup

If cookie preferences appear, make your choice first. New accounts then complete four setup steps:

1. **Your role**: choose your role.
2. **What you'll do here**: select at least one intended use.
3. **Where we found each other**: choose how you heard about qBraid.
4. **About you**: provide a username, first name, and last name. A profile photo is optional.

Select **Next** between steps, then **Enter qBraid** to finish. If you select **Other**, fill in the accompanying explanation.

The **Getting Started** tour opens with **Welcome to qBraid** after setup. Follow it to explore the dashboard and run a simulator circuit, or select **Skip for now**, then confirm **Skip tour**. Restart it later from **? > Tour menu** in the top bar.

## Add a passkey

After signing in, open [Profile](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/profile#manage-passkeys) to register a passkey. Passkeys let you use a device's fingerprint, face, or security key for later sign-ins.


# Dashboard and instances
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/dashboard

Launch qBraid Lab, manage running and stopped instances, and download your files.

## Launch Lab

1. Open the [Dashboard](https://account.qbraid.com/dashboard).
2. Select the workspace that should own the session and pay for its usage.
3. In **Launch qBraid Lab**, choose an available compute profile.
4. Review the profile's resources and pricing, then select **Launch**.
5. Follow the launch progress and open Lab when the instance is ready.

Use **Browse All Instances** for the full compute selection. The dashboard also shows quantum job summaries, quick actions, and **Usage Overview**.

Subscription CPU compute draws from your compute-hours allowance. On-demand instances use wallet credits and can charge for storage while stopped. See [Usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage) before choosing a profile.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nhrtLHIYzQV0XrqfCJBvN1OSoxHFbk2IpcTiG"
    alt="Dashboard with on-demand compute profiles, credit rates, and Launch buttons"
  />
</Frame>

Review the on-demand profile's credit rate and the wallet balance required before launch.

## Manage an instance

Open **My Instances** or select an instance to inspect its details. Available actions depend on the instance's type and status. A running instance can provide Lab, VS Code, and a terminal. Instance details also provide SSH access when supported.

If the instance supports stop and resume, select **Stop** to preserve it for later. Start the stopped instance to resume work. Stopping it preserves its disk and can continue to incur storage charges. Some providers support only termination, so check the available actions before relying on stop and resume.

<Warning>
  **Terminate** permanently deletes an on-demand instance and its disk data.
  Download files you need before you confirm termination.
</Warning>

If instance details fail to load, retry the page before launching another instance. A failed page load does not mean that the instance stopped.

### Rename an instance

For an on-demand instance, select its name where **Click to rename** is available. Enter a label and press **Enter** or select **Save label**. Press **Escape** to cancel. The label helps you distinguish instances. It does not change the compute profile.

### Connect through SSH

SSH access is available for running subscription Lab instances whose image supports SSH. On-demand instance details do not provide this SSH panel.

1. Open the subscription instance details and select **SSH** to show the **SSH access** panel.
2. Paste your SSH **public** key, such as the contents of `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`. Keep the private key on your computer.
3. Select **Install key** and check that it appears in the installed-key list.
4. Install the [qBraid CLI](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/user-guide/overview) on your computer if needed.
5. Copy and run the command under **Write your SSH config** on your computer.
6. Copy and run the displayed `ssh` command to connect. You can also use the configured host with VS Code Remote-SSH or `scp`.

If you do not have an SSH key, the panel shows `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` as a way to create one locally. Use the panel's remove control to remove an installed key from that instance when it is no longer needed.

For a subscription instance whose image does not support SSH, choose a subscription profile with an SSH-capable image. If the key list fails to load, select **Retry**. A failed load does not mean that no keys are installed.

## Download Lab files

You can retrieve your Lab files without starting a Lab session.

1. Open the [Dashboard](https://account.qbraid.com/dashboard).
2. Find **Usage Overview**.
3. Select **Download Files**.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/download-files-account.png"
    alt="Download Files in the dashboard Usage Overview section"
  />
</Frame>

This download is useful when your subscription compute quota is exhausted. It does not replace a backup of an on-demand instance before termination.

## Custom compute profiles

Open [Compute Profiles](https://account.qbraid.com/dashboard/compute-profiles) and select **New Profile**. Enter a base Docker image, then choose an IDE and optional features. Advanced controls let you set resource requests and limits.

Choose the mode that fits your workflow:

- **Quick Start (Try)** applies the environment overlay at startup. The profile is ready to launch after creation.
- **Saved Build (Save)** starts an image build. Wait for the build to finish before launching it.

**My Profiles** shows your personal profiles. Organization administrators also have an **Organization** tab for shared profiles. Review each profile's resources, availability, and rate before launch. Deleting a profile requires confirmation.


# Devices and quantum jobs
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/quantum-jobs

Find quantum hardware and simulators, then inspect and manage your submitted jobs.

## Find a device

Open [Devices](https://account.qbraid.com/devices). Search by device, provider, vendor, or technology. Switch between **Grid view** and **List view**, or sort providers alphabetically.

Open a provider to browse its devices, then select a device for its details. Check the current device status, available access route, and pricing before submitting work. Device counts can group multiple access routes to the same physical device.

Use [Circuit Composer](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/composer), [qBraid Runtime](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/runtime/components), or [Quantum Jobs in Lab](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/quantum-jobs) to submit work.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nt6jwUOuZ8DOL4b5JqnarGRyvEUQuehoxYSXt"
    alt="Devices catalog with provider cards, search, view controls, and current device summaries"
  />
</Frame>

Search the device catalog or open a provider to inspect its available devices.

## Inspect jobs

1. Select the workspace where you submitted the job.
2. Open [Quantum Jobs](https://account.qbraid.com/quantum-jobs).
3. Use **Overview** for summaries or **All Jobs** for individual jobs.
4. Filter by status or provider and open a job to inspect its details.
5. Select **Refresh** to retrieve current job data.

The jobs table shows identifiers, names, devices, providers, statuses, and queue information when available. Grouped jobs can be expanded to inspect their individual jobs. Results and error details depend on the job's status and provider.

## Cancel or delete jobs

Use **Cancel job** for an eligible job, then confirm. Cancellation attempts to stop execution at the provider. It does not guarantee that a job already in progress will stop.

Use **Delete job** only when the action is available and you no longer need the record. Deletion requires confirmation and cannot be undone. You can also select eligible rows to cancel or delete several jobs together.

## Review organization activity

Organization administrators can open [organization Usage](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/usage). The **Credits** and **Jobs** tabs show activity across the organization, rather than only the personal view in Account.

See [Usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage) for simulator allowances and other resource consumption.


# Circuit Composer
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/composer

Build circuits visually, edit QASM, inspect probabilities, and run on quantum devices.

## Build a circuit

1. Open [Circuit Composer](https://account.qbraid.com/composer).
2. Select **Load example circuit** and choose **Bell State**, or drag gates from the palette onto the circuit.
3. Use the toolbar to add or remove qubits and classical bits.
4. Edit gate parameters when the gate requires them.
5. Inspect the QASM editor and the **Probabilities** panel as you change the circuit.

The visual circuit and QASM editor stay in sync for supported circuits. Resolve parsing errors before using the circuit. Use **Undo** or **Redo** to revise an edit. **Clear circuit** asks for confirmation before it resets the circuit.

For circuits with conditional gates, the probability panel warns that its simulation shows unconditional results only.

The toolbar shows the circuit's gate count and depth. The probability preview is a simulator result, separate from a submitted hardware job.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nTP2Mr2BzKxtpj4PhQiLd2sBSeu9lqEgIfkyF"
    alt="Bell-state circuit, synchronized OpenQASM, and equal probabilities for 00 and 11"
  />
</Frame>

The Bell State example shows the circuit, QASM, and simulated probabilities together.

## Run on a device

1. Select **Run**.
2. Optionally enter a job name.
3. Set the number of **Shots**.
4. Search for a device and review its provider, qubit count, type, and status.
5. Review the displayed cost estimate or usage-based pricing notice.
6. Select **Run on** for the chosen device.
7. After submission, select **View in Quantum Jobs** to follow the job.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50n2qycUCtpwDJH6pQVRd7zcgMWnKXTGBAIP1j2"
    alt="Run on quantum hardware dialog with job name, shots, searchable devices, and no selected device"
  />
</Frame>

Review shots and device availability before selecting a device and submitting a job.

The device picker lists QASM-compatible devices and disables selections the circuit cannot use. A device may be unavailable because it has too few qubits or does not accept submissions in its current state.

<Note>
  Open Quantum devices require a linked account. Use **Connect your account** in
  the run dialog and follow the [Open Quantum setup
  guide](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/integrations/openquantum).
</Note>

For devices with usage-based pricing, the final cost is calculated after the job runs. A probability preview does not submit a hardware job or guarantee its result.

Use the Composer **Feedback** button to open a support request with the Circuit Composer subject prefilled.

# Chat and Agent
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/chat

Use AI chat for quantum computing questions or attach Agent to a compute instance.

## Start a chat

1. Open [Chat](https://account.qbraid.com/chat) in the intended workspace.
2. Choose an available model in the message composer.
3. Enter your question and send the message.
4. Review any tool approval request before you approve or deny the action.

Model availability depends on your account's access. If the model list fails to load, retry it before sending. See [AI models](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/models) for model selection and [AI usage quotas](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/user-guide/usage-quotas) for allowances and charges.

When image attachments are available, use the attachment control to include images with your question. If an attachment fails validation, remove it or choose a supported image before retrying.

## Return to a conversation

Use the conversation history to reopen a saved chat. A conversation link reopens that thread in the same workspace when you have access. Start a new chat when you need a separate conversation.

The conversation controls let you export or delete the current conversation. The usage panel shows token and model usage for the thread. [Account Usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage) shows your monthly allowance and the separate AI **Auto-switch to Credits** setting.

If a message fails to send, check the draft and its attachments before retrying. An error while loading history does not mean that your saved conversation has been deleted.

## Use Agent on a compute instance

Open [Agent](https://account.qbraid.com/agent) to run a codeq session inside a compute instance. Attach to an available running instance, resume a stopped one, or launch an available profile.

Agent opens a terminal session on the selected instance. Launch and running costs follow the instance's compute profile. Use the instance controls to stop compute when you are finished.

If the terminal session ends, use **Reconnect**. See [Dashboard and instances](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/dashboard) for the difference between stopping and terminating compute.


# Models and pricing
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/models

Find available AI models, compare token rates, and understand plan allowances and credits.

qBraid Account's AI model picker lists OpenAI and Claude models with their current input and output rates. Your subscription allowance pays for AI usage first. If **Auto-switch to Credits** is enabled, additional usage can draw from your workspace's credit balance.

## Choose a model

1. Open AI chat in your selected workspace.
2. Select the model name beside the message composer.
3. Search by model name or ID.
4. Compare the input and output rates, then select a model.

The picker groups models under **OpenAI** and **Claude**. Capability labels include **Coding**, **Vision**, and **Economy** where applicable. A **Vision** label indicates image-input support. **Economy** identifies a model with a lower output-token rate.

Rates appear as **credits per 1M tokens**, with input first and output second. For example, `200 / 1k` means 200 credits per million input tokens and 1,000 credits per million output tokens. These are rates, not a charge for each message.

All current subscription tiers can use the models in the catalog. If an access policy changes, unavailable models appear under **Requires an upgrade**. The catalog can change as models are added or removed. If loading fails, select **Models unavailable. Retry**.

  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nA1sFxePFLTOKHSVhQoix0NRqJsd4ynPDlm6B"
    alt="AI model picker showing search, Vision and Economy labels, and input and output credit rates"
  />
</Frame>

The picker shows input and output credits per million tokens beside each model.

## Model rate reference

The following rates were checked against qBraid's released API rate card and the live Account model picker on October 5, 2026. Prices are in **qBraid credits per million tokens**. The picker and [AI Gateway model catalog](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/integrations/ai-gateway#available-models) provide the current rates and availability.

| Model ID            | Input | Output |
| ------------------- | ----: | -----: |
| `gpt-6-astra`       |  1000 |   5000 |
| `gpt-6-sol`         |   200 |   1000 |
| `gpt-6-luna`        |    10 |     50 |
| `gpt-6.1-sol`       |   200 |   1000 |
| `gpt-5.6-sol`       |   500 |   3000 |
| `gpt-5.6-luna`      |   100 |    600 |
| `gpt-5.6-terra`     |   250 |   1500 |
| `gpt-5.5`           |   500 |   3000 |
| `gpt-5.4`           |   250 |   1500 |
| `gpt-5.4-mini`      |    75 |    450 |
| `gpt-5.4-nano`      |    20 |    125 |
| `gpt-5.3-codex`     |   175 |   1400 |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6` |   300 |   1500 |
| `claude-haiku-4-5`  |   100 |    500 |
| `claude-opus-4-8`   |   500 |   2500 |
| `claude-opus-5`     |   500 |   2500 |
| `claude-opus-5-5`   |   400 |   2000 |
| `claude-sonnet-5`   |   200 |   1000 |
| `claude-fable-5-1`  |  1000 |   5000 |

At the standard conversion, 100 credits equals $1 USD. Cached-input rates can change a request's charge. Use token estimates to plan usage, then check the recorded charge. Review **Account > Usage** and wallet transactions for recorded usage.

## Plans, allowances, and credits

| Resource                  | How to check the price or limit                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Personal subscription     | [Personal plans](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/subscriptions) and the wallet's plan cards           |
| Organization subscription | [Team subscriptions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/subscriptions), priced per purchased seat |
| AI usage                  | Model picker rates and [AI usage quotas](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/user-guide/usage-quotas)                 |
| Quantum jobs              | The selected device's pricing and job estimate                                           |
| On-demand compute         | The selected profile's effective rate before launch                                      |
| Credit purchases          | The wallet's exchange rate and checkout total                                            |

Plan allowances are separate from your wallet balance. CPU hours are not AI tokens, simulator job counts are not currency, and a seat allocation does not create additional purchased credits. Check the selected workspace before comparing balances or usage.

See [On-demand pricing](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/pricing) for resource billing units and [Buy credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits) to fund usage beyond your plan allowances.


# Profile
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/profile

Edit your profile, manage passkeys and notification preferences, and request account deletion.

Open [Account > Profile](https://account.qbraid.com/account/profile) to manage your personal account.

## Edit your profile

Select **Edit profile** to change your first name, last name, or username, then select **Save changes**. Use **Change profile photo** to choose an image for your avatar.

Your email address is read-only. Contact [Support](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/support) if you need help changing it.

## Manage passkeys

The **Passkeys** card lets you sign in with your fingerprint, face, or a security key.

1. Select **Add passkey**.
2. Follow your browser or device's registration prompt.
3. Check that the new passkey appears in the list.

To remove a passkey, select its remove control and confirm **Remove**. That passkey can no longer sign you in.

If the browser does not support passkeys, use a supported browser on a device with a screen lock. The card displays a separate message when passkeys are unavailable for your account.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nQVfO8de4nyjX09uLKfUqpP6JtibwDAks5Mzl"
    alt="Passkeys card showing the Add passkey control and an empty passkey list"
  />
</Frame>

Select Add passkey to start your browser or device registration prompt.

## Switch or leave organizations

The **Organizations** section lists your memberships and roles. Select another organization to switch the active workspace. Use the search field when it appears to find an organization by name.

To leave, select **Leave organization** for that membership and confirm. You lose access to its resources. Stop active Lab sessions before leaving. Your assigned seat is revoked, and any remaining organization wallet credits are queued for return to the organization. You cannot leave qBraid Default. Owners must [transfer ownership](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/members#transfer-ownership) before leaving.

To accept an email invitation or join with a code, see [Join an organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invitations).

## Connect Open Quantum

Use the **Integrations** section to link an Open Quantum account. See the [Open Quantum setup guide](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/integrations/openquantum).

## Set notification and cookie preferences

**Notification Preferences** provides separate email and in-app controls for each category, plus an overall enable control. Changes save when you toggle them. If email delivery is suspended, the card directs you to support.

Use **Cookie Preferences** to review your optional cookie choices.

## Request account deletion

1. Switch to **qBraid Default**.
2. Open **Profile** and find **Delete Account**.
3. Optionally enter a reason, up to 500 characters.
4. Confirm that you understand the action cannot be undone.
5. Submit the deletion request.

The request enters **Pending Review**. The page states that the team reviews requests within 2 to 3 business days. While the request is pending, select **Cancel Request** to withdraw it. If a request is rejected, review the displayed admin notes and use **Re-submit Request** if you want to apply again.

<Warning>
  Account deletion is permanent after processing. Approval cancels active
  subscriptions and signs you out. Save the data you need before requesting
  deletion.
</Warning>

  />
