Review the deletion notice before submitting a request.

## Refresh account changes

If membership, role, or balance changes have not appeared, select **Refresh account data** beside settings in the sidebar profile row. See [Refresh account data](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/refresh) for instructions and workspace recovery.


# Refresh account data
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/refresh

Update your organizations, roles, credits, and account access without signing out.

Use **Refresh account data** when an organization, role, credit balance, or subscription change has not appeared in Account. You can refresh your account without signing out or leaving the page.

## Refresh your account

1. Open the sidebar. If it is collapsed, select **Toggle Sidebar**.
2. Find your profile row near the bottom, above **Log out**.
3. Select the circular-arrow button beside **Account settings**. Its label is **Refresh account data**.
4. Wait for **Refreshing account…** to change to **Account refreshed**.
5. Check the workspace switcher and the page affected by the change.

The icon spins while the refresh runs. The control is temporarily unavailable during a refresh or an organization switch.

<Frame caption="Select the circular-arrow button beside Account settings to refresh your account.">
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nLh0015VeqSNuhfJndBxKE61UVciHAgWY4srZ"
    alt="Refresh account data button circled beside Account settings in the sidebar profile row"
    width="256"
  />
</Frame>

<Frame caption="Account refresh at 2× speed. Wait for Account refreshed before checking the updated data.">
  <video
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nOQpiONERqbTUIK1z5VaNLSmw6khtlWYseFvd"
    controls
    muted
    playsInline
    preload="metadata"
    aria-label="Refreshing account data and seeing the Account refreshed message at twice normal speed"
  />
</Frame>

[Open the refresh recording](https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nOQpiONERqbTUIK1z5VaNLSmw6khtlWYseFvd).

## What refresh updates

Refresh reloads your account information, including organization memberships, roles, and credits, and updates the related organization and billing data. Use it after an administrator changes your access or after a credit or subscription change is missing from the UI.

It does not accept a pending invitation or grant a role, seat, or credits. Complete the [email invitation](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invitations) or [invite-code flow](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invite-codes#join-with-a-code) to join first. A successful code join refreshes your membership and opens the organization's dashboard automatically.

Account refresh is separate from refreshing a job list, device catalog, or compute environment. Use the relevant page's controls to check those resources.

## Select the right workspace

Use the workspace switcher to choose **qBraid Default** or your organization. Account shows **Switching to [organization name]…** while the change completes, then loads that workspace's data. If the name is not available, the message is **Switching organization…**.

An account refresh keeps your current workspace if you still belong to it. If your membership has been removed, Account switches to your default workspace and displays **You were removed from your organization. Switched to your default workspace.**

If an organization is still missing after refreshing, check that you signed in with the account that joined it. Ask the organization administrator to check your membership. Refresh cannot restore removed or suspended access.

## Troubleshoot refresh

| Message or behavior                                                     | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Couldn't refresh — please try again.**                                | You remain signed in on the current page. Try the refresh again. If it keeps failing, contact [Support](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/support).                                                                                                    |
| **Your session expired. Redirecting to sign in…**                       | Sign in again to continue.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The refresh control is unavailable                                      | Wait for the current refresh or organization switch to finish.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| The workspace is correct but your access or balance is still unexpected | Ask the organization administrator to check your role, seat, or credit allocation. See [Members](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/members), [Seats](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/seats), and [Credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credits). |


# API keys
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/api-keys

Create, inspect, rotate, and revoke API keys for the selected workspace.

Use API keys with [qBraid Runtime](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/runtime/components), the [REST API](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/user-guide/overview), and the [CLI](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid).

## Create a key

1. Select the intended workspace.
2. Open [Account > API Keys](https://account.qbraid.com/account/api-keys).
3. Select **Create API Key**.
4. Enter a name and, optionally, a description.
5. Choose 30, 60, or 90 days, **Never expire**, or a custom number of days.
6. Create the key and copy its secret value into your password manager or secrets store.

<Warning>
  The secret value appears only after creation or regeneration. If you lose it,
  regenerate the key or create a replacement.
</Warning>

The creation form does not provide a scope selector. Use the key details to inspect the permissions associated with a key.

## Inspect a key

Select a key in the table to open its detail dialog. The table shows status, creation date, last use, and expiration. Details can include the last IP address, rate limit, permissions, constraints, and revocation information.

Keys belong to the selected workspace. Switch workspaces if the key you expect is not in the list.

## Rotate a key

Select the key's **Regenerate** control and confirm the dialog. Copy the new secret when it appears.

<Warning>
  Regeneration invalidates the previous secret. Update the applications that use
  it immediately. For a planned migration, create a separate replacement key,
  update and verify your applications, then revoke the old key.
</Warning>

## Revoke a key

Select the key's **Revoke** control and confirm. Revocation prevents further use of that key. Check that your applications have a working replacement before revoking a key they still need.

Keep secret values out of source control, screenshots, and support requests. Review last-used information when investigating unexpected access. Report vulnerabilities through the [qBraid security advisory form](https://github.com/qBraid/community/security/advisories).


# Usage
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage

Review compute and AI allowances, inspect session charges, and control automatic credit spending.

## Open your personal usage

1. Open [qBraid Account](https://account.qbraid.com/).
2. Select **qBraid Default** in the workspace switcher to inspect your personal usage.
3. Open **Account > Usage** in the sidebar.
4. Select **Overview** for balances and allowances, or **Session History** to investigate individual compute sessions.

The same page shows your usage within an organization when that workspace is selected. It does not show every member's consumption. Administrators can use [Organization usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/usage) for that view.

## Overview

<Frame caption="Personal Usage in the default workspace. This test account has no recorded compute usage.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nyKmm28CktzIdDcJjHfu4Ss1vTq92YARExbMg" alt="Account Usage in qBraid Default with Overview selected, allowance cards, and Compute Settings" />
</Frame>

Start with the cards near the top of **Overview**:

| Card | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| **Available Credits** | Your qBraid wallet balance in the selected workspace. |
| **Compute Hours** | Subscription compute allowance consumed, total quota, and renewal countdown. |
| **Storage** | Stored data in GB and the displayed storage quota. |
| **Credits Charged** | Recorded compute credit charges for the selected history range. |

The **Understanding Your Usage** card separates subscription compute from on-demand billing. Open the question-mark help controls beside individual metrics for their definitions.

### How compute hours and charges work

<Frame caption="The page explains the two billing types in Understanding Your Usage.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50n1CwFow5jQpcOFeGo6nwMJRrzu9S74dPxmHBk" alt="Understanding Your Usage card explaining subscription compute and on-demand billing" />
</Frame>

Subscription CPU Lab instances use your compute-hours allowance first. Compute hours are **vCPU-hours**, calculated as session duration multiplied by the number of vCPUs. One hour on a 2-vCPU instance consumes two compute hours.

**Compute Time**, session **Duration**, and **Total Compute Time** measure elapsed running time. They do not multiply duration by machine size. The Compute Hours quota also follows its renewal date, while historical totals follow the selected date range. These numbers can therefore differ without indicating a billing error.

On-demand instances use wallet credits instead of subscription compute hours. They charge for compute while running and can charge for retained storage while stopped. Terminating an on-demand instance stops its storage charges but deletes its disk. Download needed files first. See [On-demand instances](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/on-demand-instances).

### Change the history range

<Frame caption="Use the range selector beside Daily Usage to change the historical totals.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nvFqje2NrFtAsIMBLpamlTiN9XkzhQqO38P0w" alt="Subscription and On-Demand session summaries above the Daily Usage chart and range selector" />
</Frame>

1. Scroll to **Daily Usage**.
2. Open its range selector.
3. Choose **7 days**, **14 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, **1 year**, or **All time**.
4. Compare the chart, session breakdown, **Credits Charged**, and **Summary** for that range.

The default range is 30 days. It changes the historical totals, not the wallet balance or monthly allowance.

The chart shows **Subscription Hours**, **On-Demand Hours**, and **Credits Charged**. Read hours on the left axis and credits on the right. Hover over a point for its daily values.

The **Subscription Sessions** and **On-Demand Sessions** cards show session counts and running time. The on-demand card also separates **Compute Credits** from **Storage Credits**. **Summary** shows total running time, the subscription and on-demand session counts, and total credits charged.

A pending-settlement notice means recorded charges can still update. If on-demand usage is temporarily unavailable, the displayed totals may be incomplete. Refresh after the service recovers before treating them as final.

## Turn on automatic credits for compute

<Frame caption="The compute switch is on in this example. It is separate from the AI switch.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50naPQUn5Rr7oSEJ8tPxqzhVQ6NL4HkIgB3U9WX" alt="Compute Settings with Auto-switch to Credits enabled for subscription CPU usage" />
</Frame>

Enable this setting if you want subscription CPU sessions to use wallet credits after the compute-hours allowance runs out. Check **Available Credits** first. Enabling the setting does not purchase credits.

1. Open **Account > Usage > Overview** in the intended workspace.
2. Find **Compute Settings**.
3. Turn on **Auto-switch to Credits**.
4. Wait for **Auto-switch to credits enabled**.
5. Review your wallet balance and session charges as you continue using compute.

Changes save when you toggle the switch; there is no separate Save button. The switch is unavailable while the update runs. If **Failed to update settings** appears, the update failed and the switch returns to its previous setting. Retry and check the success message.

To turn automatic credit spending off, use the same switch and wait for **Auto-switch to credits disabled**. With fallback disabled, subscription CPU sessions are terminated when compute hours run out, and new subscription launches are blocked until the allowance renews or fallback is enabled. Save your work before exhausting the allowance.

This setting applies to subscription CPU fallback. On-demand instances already use credits, and AI has its own setting below. See [Lab usage limits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/usage-limits) for allowances.

## Session history

<Frame caption="Session History lists subscription and on-demand sessions with duration, credit charges, status, and pagination.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nMADv5Vqw1Hg4qdUN9TOkaRKJzcr8XuvABI50" alt="Session History showing ten of twenty sessions, subscription and on-demand filters, credit charges, and Completed and Terminated statuses" />
</Frame>

Use this tab to identify a long-running session, compare subscription and on-demand work, or investigate a charge.

1. Open **Session History**.
2. Select **All**, **Subscription**, or **On-Demand** to filter by billing tier.
3. Use **All Status** to select a status, such as **Running**, **Stopped**, **Completed**, or **Error**.
4. Read the matching rows, then use **Previous** and **Next** for additional pages.
5. Select a row to open its billing details. Keyboard users can focus a row and press **Enter** or **Space**.

The table shows 10 sessions per page. Changing a filter returns to page one. These filters are separate from the Overview chart's date range.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Start** and **End** | Recorded session times. An unfinished row can show **Running…** instead of an end time. Check its Status too. |
| **Tier** | Subscription or On-Demand billing. |
| **Profile** | The compute profile or instance label, with supporting vCPU or instance information. |
| **Duration** | Elapsed running time, rather than vCPU-hours. |
| **Credits** | Recorded credit charges. A dash means no positive charge is shown. |
| **Status** | The recorded session state. |

An **Unpaid charges** indicator means usage could not be covered by the available credits. **Settlement pending** means billing is still processing. These indicators describe different conditions.

### Inspect a session's billing details


<Frame caption="An on-demand session with expanded billing events. Charged and Total show the session charge; the event rows do not add up to that total.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nXltUFf1Y0NrDQVkz4KvJ8dMFcgwyp93EAeOf" alt="Terminated on-demand session showing 0.17 credits charged, 3 minutes 38 seconds of runtime, and two expanded compute billing events" />
</Frame>

In this example:

- **On-Demand** identifies wallet-credit billing. **Terminated** is the recorded instance status.
- **Charged: 0.17 Cr** is the recorded charge for the session. The **Compute** line and bottom **Total** also show 0.17 credits.
- **Ran for: 3m 38s** is the elapsed runtime. The two event windows, **3m 9s** and **29s**, account for that runtime.
- **Events: 2** counts the recorded billing events. It does not mean two separate final wallet charges.
- **PREPAID · PER-MIN** describes the compute billing model. The expanded rows show recorded event times, types, windows, and credit values.

The event rows show **1.14** and **0.17** credits, but adding them does not give the final session charge. On-demand compute is charged in advance, with unused time refunded. Use **Charged**, the compute/storage line items, and **Total** to read the recorded charge. This screenshot alone does not show the full refund or settlement history needed to reconstruct each event's credit value.


The dialog identifies the session and shows **Charged** and **Ran for**. Subscription sessions also show **Compute**, the vCPU-time drawn from the allowance. On-demand sessions show **Events** and a compute/storage breakdown when available.

Read **Billing events** for the recorded usage windows. On-demand sessions provide **Show all [number] events** and **Hide events** controls. The detailed events are meter readings; they are not necessarily individual wallet charges. Use the **Charged** total and compute/storage line items to reconcile charges, rather than summing meter readings yourself.

If the dialog reports that it is showing only the latest events, the displayed timeline is incomplete even though the charge total covers the session. **No billing events yet.** is different from **Couldn't load billing events.** Use **Retry** for a loading error.

Select **Report Issue** to open a support request with the session identifier and billing details already supplied. Add what you expected and what looks wrong before submitting.

## Outstanding balances

An **Outstanding Balance** alert appears when there are unpaid compute charges. It can include subscription debt and on-demand debt together. The amount owed is different from the available wallet balance and from charges still awaiting settlement.

Add credits through the [Wallet](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits), then wait for settlement before retrying a blocked launch. The alert warns that sessions can be terminated or new sessions blocked while debt remains. If the balance still looks wrong after settlement, inspect the session's billing details and use **Report Issue**.

## AI chat usage

<Frame caption="The AI switch is off in this example; the compute setting does not change it.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50n2qCGRe1pwDJH6pQVRd7zcgMWnKXTGBAIP1j2" alt="AI Chat Usage showing quota, status, renewal, Can Send, and its separate Auto-switch to Credits control" />
</Frame>

Scroll to **AI Chat Usage** in **Overview**. It shows the monthly quota percentage, **Status**, **Renews**, and **Can Send**.

- **Using Quota** means usage is drawing from the included allowance.
- **Using Credits** means usage is drawing from wallet credits.
- **Quota Exhausted** means the included allowance has run out.
- **Can Send** reports whether requests can currently proceed.

### Turn on automatic credits for AI

1. Check that the intended workspace has enough wallet credits.
2. Find **AI Chat Usage**, below the simulator section.
3. Turn on that card's **Auto-switch to Credits** control.
4. Wait for **AI chat auto-switch to credits enabled**.

To stop automatic AI fallback, turn the same control off and wait for **AI chat auto-switch to credits disabled**. If **Failed to update AI chat settings** appears, retry the update. The compute switch does not change this setting.

Review [AI usage quotas](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/user-guide/usage-quotas) and [AI models](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/models) for model eligibility, token rates, and allowance limits. An enabled switch alone does not guarantee that every model is available or affordable.

## Simulator usage

<Frame caption="Check the selected simulator and its daily allowance before running jobs.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50n8Ty0BDigItG9vq5RLXdYNFeOKZTHSxVDmP7f" alt="Simulator Usage with simulator and range selectors, jobs used today, remaining jobs, and UTC reset time" />
</Frame>

The **Simulator Usage** card tracks your daily job allowance for each simulator.

1. Choose a device with the **Simulator** selector.
2. Check jobs used today, percentage used, and jobs remaining.
3. Use **Range** to choose 7, 14, 30, or 90 days of simulator history.

Daily limits reset at **00:00 UTC**. Plans without a daily cap show **Unlimited** instead of a metered allowance. The simulator date selector is separate from the compute chart's selector. Check the device's displayed limits before submitting more jobs.

For the [GPU simulators](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/gpu-simulators), the daily allowance is a number of free circuits: a single job is one circuit, and a batch counts one per circuit. Their rows read, for example, **3 / 25 free circuits today** and **22 free circuits remaining**.

### Turn on usage-based billing for GPU simulators

The GPU simulators, `qbraid:qbraid:sim:gpu-sv` and `qbraid:qbraid:sim:gpu-tn`, each give you a free daily allowance: 25 circuits on Free and 125 on Standard. Once it is used, further jobs on that simulator are refused until the reset, unless you turn on usage-based billing. With it on, they run and are charged from your credits at the simulator's per-minute price. See [Pricing](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/pricing#gpu-simulators) for the rate.

1. Check **Available Credits** in the intended workspace. Enabling the setting does not purchase credits.
2. Open **Account > Usage > Overview** and scroll to **Simulator Usage**.
3. At the bottom of the card, below **Jobs run over time**, turn on **Usage-based billing for GPU simulators**.
4. Wait for **Usage-based billing for GPU simulators enabled**.

The switch's description reads: "After your free daily circuits, further jobs on the GPU simulators run and are charged from your credits for each minute of execution, at the simulator's per-minute price. When off, jobs that need more circuits than you have left are refused."

Changes save when you toggle the switch; there is no separate Save button. The switch is unavailable while the update runs. If **Failed to update simulator billing settings** appears, the update failed and the switch returns to its previous setting. Retry and check the success message. To stop charging further jobs, turn the same switch off and wait for **Usage-based billing for GPU simulators disabled**.

The switch appears only when a GPU simulator has a limited daily allowance on your plan, so Pro and Enterprise members, whose allowance is unlimited, do not see it. It also appears on each GPU simulator's device page. The setting is yours in the selected workspace and is separate from the compute and AI switches.

If [Circuit Composer](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/composer) refuses a GPU simulator job because the day's allowance is used, its error offers **Turn on usage-based billing**, which turns the setting on without leaving the composer, and a **Review on the Usage page** link. The job is not resubmitted for you: after **Usage-based billing for GPU simulators enabled. Run the job again to submit it.** appears, run the job again.

To read or change the setting through the REST API, use [Get Simulator Usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/rest/get-simulator-usage), whose GPU simulator entries carry `creditFallover: true` and your `autoSwitchToCredits` setting, and [Update Simulator Usage Settings](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/rest/update-simulator-usage-settings).

## Refresh or recover missing data

Use **Refresh** at the top of Usage to reload the overview, AI allowance, and simulator data. If **Error loading usage data** or **Couldn't load your sessions** appears, select the associated **Retry** button.

For **No sessions found**, select **All** and **All Status** before concluding that the workspace has no history. Check that you selected the workspace where you ran the sessions. A failed query is not an empty history.

## Download your files

You can download Lab files without starting a session from **Dashboard > Usage Overview > Download Files**. Follow [Download Lab files](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/dashboard#download-lab-files). The exhausted-compute help control can also offer a file download when a new session is blocked.


# Support
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/support

Submit support requests, track their status, and reply to the qBraid team.

1. Open [Support](https://account.qbraid.com/support).
2. Select **New Request**.
3. Describe the problem, including the affected feature and steps to reproduce it.
4. Submit the request.
5. Open the request in the list to read the response and comments.

Use the status filters to find an existing request. When a request accepts replies, type into **Write a reply** and select **Send reply**. You can also press **Ctrl+Enter** to send. Closed requests show that the conversation is closed.

Use the request reference when following up. Do not include API keys, payment details, or other credentials in your request.

The Composer **Feedback** button also opens the support form. Send feedback through Support. The standalone Feedback page does not yet have a submission form.


# Open Quantum
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/integrations/openquantum

Create and connect an Open Quantum account, review its credits, and run jobs through qBraid.

The Open Quantum integration lets you submit jobs through qBraid and pay with your connected [Open Quantum](https://www.openquantum.com/) account's credits.

<Warning>
  A job that costs no qBraid credits can still consume Open Quantum credits.
  Buying qBraid credits does not fund your Open Quantum balance. Check the
  provider's balance and pricing before submitting work.
</Warning>

## Create your Open Quantum account

1. Open [Open Quantum](https://www.openquantum.com/) and start sign-up.
2. Complete the provider's registration and any remaining onboarding steps.
3. Sign in and review the account's available credits before connecting it to qBraid.

If Open Quantum displays a welcome-credit offer, follow its claim instructions and confirm that the credits appear in your provider balance. Offer availability and eligibility are controlled by Open Quantum. Welcome credits are not a guaranteed allocation from qBraid.


## Connect Open Quantum to qBraid

1. Sign in to [qBraid Account](https://account.qbraid.com/).
2. Open [Account > Profile](https://account.qbraid.com/account/profile).
3. Find **Integrations** and locate **Open Quantum**.
4. Select **Connect**. Your browser navigates to the Open Quantum authorization flow.
5. Sign in to the Open Quantum account you want to use and complete authorization.
6. Wait to return to qBraid Profile, then check the connection as described below.


You can also reach Profile's connection setup from the connection prompt in [Circuit Composer](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/composer).

## Confirm the connection

On success, qBraid displays **Open Quantum connected**. The Open Quantum entry shows a green status dot, **Connected as** followed by the linked account, and a **Disconnect** button. Check that this is the account whose credits you intend to use.


## Run a job through qBraid

1. Open [Devices](https://account.qbraid.com/devices) and find the Open Quantum device you want to use.
2. Check its availability and provider pricing.
3. Use [Circuit Composer](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/composer) or the [qBraid Runtime](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/runtime/components) to submit your circuit to that device.
4. Open [Quantum Jobs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/quantum-jobs) to inspect the job's status, results, or error.

For a local Python environment, install the qBraid SDK and configure your [qBraid API key](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/api-keys). Open Quantum's [installation guide](https://docs.openquantum.com/qbraid/installation/) explains local and Lab authentication. Its [backend guide](https://docs.openquantum.com/qbraid/backends-targets/) lists Open Quantum device identifiers, and its [examples](https://docs.openquantum.com/qbraid/examples/) provide complete circuits.

## Review provider credits

Open the [Open Quantum billing page](https://www.openquantum.com/settings/billing) to check the linked account's balance and transactions. Review consumption and expiration entries if the balance is lower than expected.

Open Quantum distinguishes two credit types:

| Type | Source and use | Provider's documented expiration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Spark** | Free or promotional credits for Public execution plans. | 90 days after grant. |
| **Full** | Purchased credits for Public or Private execution plans. | 12 months. |

For Public plans, Open Quantum spends Spark credits before Full credits. Private plans require Full credits. Check the provider's [credit documentation](https://docs.openquantum.com/concepts/credits/) for current terms and its [pricing page](https://www.openquantum.com/pricing) for rates.

To buy provider credits, open the Open Quantum portal's credit purchase flow, select an amount, complete Stripe checkout, and confirm the updated provider balance. These credits remain separate from your qBraid wallet.

## Disconnect or change accounts

1. Open **Account > Profile > Integrations**.
2. Select **Disconnect** beside Open Quantum.
3. Wait for the entry to return to **Connect**.
4. To use another Open Quantum account, select **Connect**, authorize that account, and verify **Connected as** afterward.

Link an account again before submitting another Open Quantum job through qBraid.

## Troubleshoot the connection or a failed job

- If the connection status cannot load, select **Retry**. A status-loading error does not establish that the account is disconnected.
- If authorization fails, return to Profile, select **Connect**, and complete the flow while signed in to the intended qBraid account.
- If jobs fail after connection, confirm the **Connected as** account, check its Open Quantum balance and credit expiration, and inspect the target device's availability and job error.
- If Spark credits are available but the selected execution plan requires Full credits, review the provider's supported plans before retrying.

If the error continues, open [Support](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/support) with the job identifier and error message. Do not include credentials.

## Related links

- [qBraid on Open Quantum](https://www.openquantum.com/frameworks/qbraid)
- [Open Quantum's qBraid documentation](https://docs.openquantum.com/qbraid/overview/)
- [Open Quantum credits and pricing](https://docs.openquantum.com/concepts/credits/)


# Overview
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/overview

What you see when you open your wallet: subscription, prepaid credits, transactions, and invoices.

Use your wallet to manage credits, your subscription, and payment history.

Open it from the sidebar under **Account > Wallet**, or visit [account.qbraid.com/account/wallet](https://account.qbraid.com/account/wallet).

<Note>
  The wallet changes with the selected workspace. In **qBraid Default** you see
  your personal subscription, **Buy credits**, and an **Invoices & receipts**
  tab. In an **organization** workspace you see a **Your seat** card, a
  **Request credits** button, and transactions only. See [workspace
  selection](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/overview#choose-a-workspace) for details.
</Note>

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-paid-plan.webp"
    alt="Wallet in qBraid Default showing an active Standard Monthly subscription card, a Compare plans row, and the Prepaid credits card"
  />
</Frame>

## What each part does

- **Payment link.** The **Manage payment & invoices** button. Opens the Stripe customer portal for payment methods and invoices. Personal workspace only.
- **Subscription.** Shows your personal plan. In an organization this section becomes **Your seat**.
- **Prepaid credits.** Shows the balance, recent use, and the **Buy credits** controls. Called **Your credits** in an organization.
- **Transactions.** Lists credit activity for the selected workspace. Adds the **Invoices & receipts** tab in qBraid Default.

## Subscription

In **qBraid Default**, the subscription card shows your tier, billing interval, and status. A paid plan shows the renewal date and charge. If a discount applies, the card strikes through the list price and shows the percent off next to the next charge. **Change plan** and **Cancel subscription** open in-app dialogs. A scheduled change or pending cancellation appears as a row inside the card.

On the **Free** plan, **Upgrade your plan** follows the card with the Standard and Pro cards. Standard has a **Most popular** badge. Use the **Monthly** and **Annual** toggle to switch prices. On a paid plan the cards collapse into a **Compare plans** row. Links to `/account/wallet#available-plans` open it automatically.

See [Personal subscriptions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/subscriptions) for buy, change, and cancel steps.

## Team member view

In an **organization** workspace, the wallet shows your seat instead of a personal subscription. Owners and admins assign seats in **Organizations > Billing**.

### With a seat

A member with a seat sees the seat tier, an **Active** badge, and the seat text. The **Your credits** card sits below it.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-team-seat.webp"
    alt="Wallet in an organization workspace for a member with a Standard seat, showing Your seat as Standard with an Active badge, a Plan managed by your organization badge, and the Your credits card with a 1,000 credit balance"
  />
</Frame>

On a phone, the cards stack in one column.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-team-seat-mobile.webp"
    alt="Wallet on a phone for a member with a Standard seat, showing the seat card above the Your credits card"
  />
</Frame>

- **Your seat.** Names the tier of the seat you hold, such as **Standard**.
- **Active badge.** Shows the seat status.
- **Seat text.** Reads **Your seat includes _tier_ features**. Says what the seat gives you. Credits for compute and QPU jobs come from your balance below.
- **Managed badge.** Reads **Plan managed by your organization**. Replaces the personal plan actions. You cannot buy, change, or cancel a plan here.
- **Your credits.** Shows your balance in this organization. Admins add credits from the organization pool when they approve your request.
- **Pending request.** Reads **Request for _N_ credits is pending**. Appears after you send a request. It shows the send date and your reason. **View request** opens it.

Assigning a seat moves credits from the organization wallet to your balance. The admin sees the amount before they confirm.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-assign-seat.webp"
    alt="Assign Seat dialog showing a Standard seat, 3 of 3 available seats, 1,000 credits to transfer, the current organization balance, and the new organization balance"
  />
</Frame>

### Without a seat

A member without a seat sees **Free** and **No seat assigned in** _organization_. The **Need more credits?** panel holds **Request credits**.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-team-no-seat.webp"
    alt="Wallet in an organization workspace for a member without a seat, showing Your seat as Free with No seat assigned, the Your credits card, and a Request credits button"
  />
</Frame>

Select **Request credits** to ask the organization admins for credits. A pending request replaces the **Need more credits?** panel. See [Credit requests](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests).

## Prepaid credits

The credits card shows your **Available balance** first, with its dollar value at the current rate. A seven-day usage chart appears next to the balance. With no recent use, the card shows **No recent activity** instead.

- **Burn rate.** Credits used in the last 30 days, shown per day.
- **Runway.** How long the balance lasts at that rate: **≈ N days left**, **No usage yet**, or **> 1 year**. Red under 14 days.
- **Added · 30 days.** Credits added in the last 30 days.
- **All time.** Expands to the lifetime totals added, deducted, and the net change.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-prepaid-credits.webp"
    alt="Prepaid credits card with the balance, burn rate, runway, added credits, and the Buy credits presets"
  />
</Frame>

The wallet computes these figures from the most recent transactions it loads, so they can leave out older activity. The transactions list below shows the underlying rows.

In qBraid Default, **Buy credits** offers preset and custom amounts. See [Buy credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits). In an organization, **Request credits** asks org admins for credits. A pending request shows **Request for N credits is pending** with a **View request** button. See [Credit requests](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests).

## Transactions

The **Transactions** section lists credit activity for the selected workspace. In qBraid Default it opens on **Credit transactions** next to the **Invoices & receipts** tab. On narrow screens the tabs shorten to **Transactions** and **Invoices**, and rows display as cards.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-mobile-transactions.webp"
    alt="Wallet on a phone showing transactions as stacked cards under the search and filter controls"
  />
</Frame>

Select a row to open its receipt or details. See [Payment history](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/payment-history).

## Outstanding balance

An **Outstanding Balance** banner shows unpaid compute charges separately from the wallet balance. A later credit purchase or transfer settles this debt automatically. Check the debt and the available balance before retrying a blocked launch.

## Where to next

- Add funds: [Buy credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits).
- Pick a plan: [Personal subscriptions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/subscriptions).
- Ask your organization for credits: [Credit requests](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests).
- Audit your charges: [Payment history](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/payment-history).
- Find invoices: [Payment history](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/payment-history#invoices).


# Buy credits
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits

Top up your credit balance with a preset or custom amount, and apply a promo code at checkout.

You can buy credits without a subscription. The standard rate is $1 = 100 credits for supported qBraid-billed resources. Provider-funded jobs, such as Open Quantum, use the linked provider account's credits.

<Warning>
  Buying credits is only available in your **qBraid Default** workspace (the
  default). In an organization workspace, the Buy credits controls are hidden
  and you see a [Request
  credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests) button instead.
  Organization administrators buy credits for the team from [Organizations >
  Credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credits#buy-credits-for-the-org).
</Warning>

## What each part does

- **Preset amounts.** Five cards: $5, $10, $20, $50, and $100, each with its credit count.
- **Custom.** A dollar amount you type. The credit count updates as you type.
- **Add promo code.** Opens the promo code field. Stripe applies the code at checkout.
- **Buy button.** Reads **Buy N credits · $X**. The purchase button. It shows the credit count and price for your selection and opens Stripe Checkout.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-buy-credits.webp"
    alt="Prepaid credits card showing Buy credits with the $10 preset selected, the promo code field open, and the Buy 1,000 credits button"
  />
</Frame>

## How to buy

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to qBraid Default">
    Open the workspace switcher in the top-left of the dashboard and select
    **qBraid Default**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Wallet">
    Click **Account > Wallet** in the sidebar, or open
    [account.qbraid.com/account/wallet](https://account.qbraid.com/account/wallet)
    directly.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Find Buy credits">
    The section sits inside **Prepaid credits**, below the balance and usage
    stats.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick an amount">
    Click a preset card, or type a dollar amount in **Custom**. The button label
    updates with the credit count and total.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add a promo code (optional)">
    Select **Add promo code** and type the code.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select Buy">
    Click **Buy N credits · $X**. The wallet opens Stripe Checkout.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Check>
  After payment, return to the wallet and wait for checkout confirmation.
  Refresh the wallet if the balance has not updated.
</Check>

<Tip>
  The current exchange rate appears under **Available balance**. The standard
  rate is $1 = 100 credits. The custom amount field enforces the allowed
  purchase range.
</Tip>

## Add a promo code on the wallet

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to qBraid Default">
    Open the workspace switcher and select **qBraid Default**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Wallet">Click **Account > Wallet** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Pick an amount">
    In **Buy credits**, select a preset or enter a custom amount.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Type the code">
    Select **Add promo code** and enter the code in the field.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select Buy">
    Click **Buy N credits · $X**. Stripe applies the discount at checkout. An
    invalid code shows an error in the field instead of opening checkout.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Apply a promo code on Stripe Checkout

<Steps>
  <Step title="Start a purchase">
    Follow the steps above without entering a promo code on the wallet.
  </Step>
  <Step title="On Stripe Checkout, click Add promotion code">
    A small text field appears.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Paste the code and click Apply">
    The discount appears on the order summary.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Complete the order">Click **Complete Order**.</Step>
</Steps>

Review the final amount in Stripe before completing checkout.

## If you can't see the Buy button

In an organization workspace, your wallet shows **Request credits** instead of the purchase controls. Organization administrators buy for the team from **Billing**. See [Credit Requests](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests).

## Outstanding balance

An **Outstanding Balance** banner shows unpaid compute charges separately from the wallet balance. Credit purchases and transfers can settle that debt. After checkout, check both the debt and the available wallet balance.


# Personal subscriptions
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/subscriptions

Compare personal plans, change your plan, and manage billing.

A personal subscription covers your account in **qBraid Default**. Switch to that workspace, then open [Account > Wallet](https://account.qbraid.com/account/wallet).

## Plans

| Plan     | Monthly      | Annual                    | CPU hours / month | Storage | Simulator jobs / day | AI allowance |
| -------- | ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- | ------- | -------------------- | ------------ |
| Free     | $0           | $0                        | 100               | 15 GB   | 100                  | $5           |
| Standard | $20 / month  | $192 / year ($16 / month) | 400               | 50 GB   | 500                  | $15          |
| Pro      | $100 / month | $960 / year ($80 / month) | 2,000             | 150 GB  | Unlimited            | $50          |

Simulator jobs are per managed simulator. The [GPU simulators](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/pricing#gpu-simulators) have a smaller free allowance instead: 25 circuits a day on Free, 125 on Standard, and unlimited on Pro. A batch counts one per circuit.

You pay annual prices once a year. Review the checkout total before you subscribe. CPU hours, simulator job limits, and AI allowances are separate limits, not credits deposited in your wallet. Check **Account > Usage** for your remaining allowance and renewal date.

Standard includes full Qubes and Quantum Software Engineering course access and priority support. Pro includes dedicated support. The plan cards also list the on-demand compute discount: 10% for Standard and 18% for Pro. Check the effective resource price before you launch.

All current plans can use the AI model catalog. Plans differ in their AI allowance. See [Models and pricing](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/models) and [AI usage quotas](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/user-guide/usage-quotas).

## What each part does

- **Subscription card.** Shows your tier, a Monthly or Annual badge, a status badge, and the renewal line with your price.
- **Discounted price.** When a discount applies, the card strikes through the list price and shows a **% off** badge.
- **Change plan.** Opens the plan dialog. Pick a tier and interval, preview the price, and confirm.
- **Cancel subscription.** Opens the cancellation dialog. It shortens to **Cancel** on narrow screens.
- **Scheduled change row.** A **Switches to _plan_ on _date_** row inside the card. Select **Undo** to cancel it.
- **Cancellation row.** A notice that the plan will not renew. Select **Keep my plan** to resume.
- **Compare plans.** On paid plans, a collapsed row that expands to the plan cards. Opens automatically at `/account/wallet#available-plans`.
- **Upgrade your plan.** On Free, the visible plan grid with a Monthly/Annual toggle and a savings badge.
- **Payment link.** The **Manage payment & invoices** button. Opens the Stripe customer portal for payment methods and invoices.

Plan cards show the price, key features, and the on-demand compute discount. They do not show quota meters.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-free-plan.webp"
    alt="Free plan wallet showing the Standard and Pro upgrade cards with Annual billing selected"
  />
</Frame>

Annual billing shows the monthly equivalent and the full yearly total.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-mobile.webp"
    alt="Wallet on a phone showing the Free subscription card and the Standard upgrade card below it"
  />
</Frame>

On narrow screens the plan cards stack in one column and **Cancel subscription** shortens to **Cancel**.

## Buy a plan

Use these steps on the **Free** plan.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open your wallet">
    Switch to **qBraid Default**. Open **Account > Wallet**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick a billing interval">
    In **Upgrade your plan**, choose **Monthly** or **Annual**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select a plan">
    Select **Upgrade to Standard** or **Upgrade to Pro**. A **Confirm Subscription** dialog opens. It lists the plan, the billing interval, and the total.

    <Frame>
      <img
        src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-confirm-subscription.webp"
        alt="Confirm Subscription dialog showing the Standard plan, Monthly billing, and a $20 per month total with Cancel and Proceed to Payment buttons"
      />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pay on Stripe">
    Select **Proceed to Payment**. Stripe opens. Stripe adds any taxes at checkout. Enter a promo code on the Stripe page.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Return to the wallet">
    Complete the payment and return to the wallet. Wait for the subscription card to show your plan before you use the new allowance.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Your paid plan

A paid plan replaces the Free card with a subscription card. The card shows the tier, the billing interval, and an **Active** badge. It also shows the renewal date and the price.

On a phone, the card puts **Change plan** first. **Cancel subscription** shortens to **Cancel**.

</Frame>

Select **Compare plans** to see all three plans. Your current plan has a **Current Plan** badge. Use the **Monthly** and **Annual** toggle to switch prices.

## Change plan

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the plan dialog">
    Open **Account > Wallet** in **qBraid Default**. Select **Change plan** on the subscription card.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick a tier and interval">
    Choose **Standard** or **Pro**. Choose **Monthly** or **Annual**. Enter a promo code if you have one.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Read the preview">
    The preview shows the cost before you confirm. **Due today** lists a credit for the unused time on your current plan. It also lists a charge for the time left on the new plan. **Total due today** adds them up. **From** and a date show your **Renewal total**. A note below says when the change starts.

    <Frame>
      <img
        src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-change-plan.webp"

      />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm the change">
    Select **Confirm change**. The note reads **Takes effect now** when the change starts at once. Otherwise it gives the date your plan changes. You keep your current plan until then.
  </Step>
</Steps>

A scheduled change shows a **Switches to _plan_ on _date_** row inside the card. Select **Undo** to cancel it.

## Manage payment and invoices

Select **Manage payment & invoices** at the top of the wallet to open the Stripe customer portal. Use the portal to manage your payment method and download invoices.

The wallet also has an **Invoices & receipts** tab. See [Payment history and invoices](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/payment-history#invoices).

## Cancel

<Steps>
  <Step title="Start the cancellation">
    Open **Account > Wallet** in **qBraid Default**. Select **Cancel subscription**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick a reason">
    The dialog asks **Why are you canceling?** Choose one reason. **Continue** stays off until you choose. Some reasons add an optional note box.

    <Frame>
      <img
        src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-cancel-reason.webp"
        alt="Cancel dialog step 1 of 2 asking why you are canceling, with five reasons and Keep my plan and Continue buttons"
      />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Consider an offer">
    For some reasons, the dialog shows an offer. The offer is a discount or a lower plan. Accept it to keep a subscription. Select **Cancel anyway** to continue.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm the cancellation">
    The last step reads **Cancel _plan_ at the end of your term?** It gives the end date. It lists the limits that drop to Free. It confirms that credits you bought stay in your wallet. Select **Cancel at end of term**.

    <Frame>
      <img
        src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-cancel-confirm.webp"
        alt="Cancel Pro at the end of your term dialog listing CPU hours, storage, and simulator job limits that drop, and that purchased credits stay, with Keep my plan and Cancel at end of term buttons"
      />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
</Steps>

An **Ends _date_** badge appears on the plan card. The card shows **No further charges** and a notice that your plan will not renew. You keep the paid benefits until the end date. Then your account returns to Free.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-cancelled.webp"
    alt="Pro Monthly card with an Ends Nov 10, 2026 badge, the notice Your plan won't renew, and a Keep my plan button"
  />

While a cancellation is scheduled, the card hides **Change plan** and **Cancel subscription**.

## Keep my plan

Use **Keep my plan** to undo a cancellation before the end date.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open your wallet">
    Open **Account > Wallet** in **qBraid Default**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Resume the subscription">
    In the notice that says **Your plan won't renew**, select **Keep my plan**. The notice goes away. Your plan renews as before.
  </Step>
</Steps>

You can also select **Keep my plan** inside the cancel dialog. That closes the dialog and changes nothing.

## Personal vs team

|                 | Personal                         | [Team](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/subscriptions) |
| --------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Billing scope   | Your personal account            | The organization                                |
| Price           | Per account                      | Per seat, minimum two seats                     |
| Benefits        | Your account                     | Members assigned a seat                         |
| Where to manage | Wallet and the in-app dialogs    | Organization Billing                            |
| Add capacity    | Change plan or upgrade your plan | Add seats and assign them                       |

In an organization workspace, the wallet shows **Your seat** instead of the personal subscription card. A member with a seat sees the seat tier. A member without one sees **Free** with **No seat assigned** and **Plan managed by your organization**. There are no buy, plan, or cancel actions on this view.

Select the correct workspace before you review a balance or change a subscription. An organization's wallet, member allocations, and team subscription are separate from your qBraid Default wallet.


# Payment history
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/payment-history

See every transaction on your account, filter by type or category, search, and export to CSV.

The **Transactions** section at the bottom of the wallet lists every credit transaction in this workspace. That includes purchases, transfers in and out, deductions, promo credits, and refunds.

In **qBraid Default**, two tabs sit under the section title: **Credit transactions** and **Invoices & receipts**. An organization workspace shows transactions only.

## What each part does

- **Search transactions.** Filters the rows on the current page by description text.
- **All Types.** Filters by transaction type, such as Purchase, Compute, AI Chat, Received, Sent, or Refund.
- **All Categories.** Filters by category: Purchases, Subscriptions, Transfers, Usage, or AI Chat.
- **Refresh.** Reloads the transactions without reloading the page.
- **Export CSV.** Downloads the current page of sorted and filtered rows.
- **Old Transactions.** Downloads legacy records. It appears only when your account has transactions from before the current billing system.
- **Column headers.** **Date**, **Type**, **Amount**, and **Balance** sort the page. **Description** does not sort.
- **Rows.** Open a detail dialog with the amount, balance after, and per-type details.

Active filters appear as removable badges under the toolbar. A **Clear all** button clears them together.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-transactions.webp"
    alt="Credit transactions table with the search field, type and category filters, and sortable Date, Type, Amount, and Balance columns"
  />
</Frame>

<Note>
  There is no date-range filter today. Use search or the Type and Category
  dropdowns to narrow what you see.
</Note>

## Filter and search

1. Type in **Search transactions...** to match descriptions on the current page.
2. Open **All Types** and pick a type, such as **Compute** or **Purchase**.
3. Open **All Categories** to narrow further to a business category.
4. Remove a single filter from its badge, or select **Clear all**.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-transactions-filter.webp"
    alt="The Type filter open, listing types such as Purchase, Bonus, Job, Compute, AI Chat, Received, Sent, Refund, Credit, and Deduction"
  />
</Frame>

## Read a row

Each row shows the date and time, a type badge, a description, the signed amount, and the balance after. A dash means the row carries no positive amount or no recorded balance.

Select a row to open its details. Depending on the transaction you can see:

- Payment details and a **View Receipt** link when available.
- The related user for transfers.
- The reason or note attached at the time.
- The transaction ID and a **Report Issue** link.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-transaction-details.webp"
    alt="Transaction details dialog for a subscription payment showing the amount, balance after, plan, status, transaction ID, and Report Issue"
  />
</Frame>

## Grouped compute rows

Repeated charges for the same compute resource fold into a grouped row under the default date sort. The group shows the UTC day and the count, such as **8 charges · UTC day**. Expand the group to inspect the individual billing periods.

Sorting by a value column such as Amount or Balance shows every row separately, so each transaction keeps its sorted position.

## Pages

The table shows 20 rows per page. Use **Previous** and **Next** to move between pages. The footer shows the current range and the total count.

On narrow screens the table becomes a list of cards with the same information.

## Export transactions

1. Filter or sort the table as needed.
2. Select **Export CSV**.
3. The file `transactions-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv` downloads with the current page of sorted and filtered rows. Columns: Date, Type, Category, Description, Amount, Balance.

<Tip>
  The export contains one page of transactions. To download more, move through
  the table and export each page you need.
</Tip>

## Legacy transactions

If you have transactions from before the current billing system, an **Old Transactions** button appears alongside the regular export. It downloads those older records in their original format.

<Note>
  Legacy and current transactions do not combine in the same file. Download
  both if you need a complete history.
</Note>

## Invoices

Open the **Invoices & receipts** tab in **qBraid Default** for your personal Stripe invoices. The table lists the date and invoice number, billing period, amount, and status. Select **Receipt** to open the hosted invoice or **PDF** to download it when those links are available.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-invoices.webp"
    alt="Invoices and receipts tab listing Stripe invoices with date, period, amount, paid status, and Receipt and PDF links"
  />
</Frame>

### Find invoices

1. Open **Account > Wallet** in **qBraid Default**.
2. Scroll to **Transactions**.
3. Select the **Invoices & receipts** tab. On a narrow screen the tab reads **Invoices**.
4. Select **Receipt** or **PDF** on the invoice's row.

Invoices are different from credit transactions. A credit deduction does not necessarily have a Stripe invoice. For a team purchase, open **Organizations > Billing > Invoices** in the organization workspace.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/overview

Share resources, manage members, and centralize team billing in a qBraid organization.

A qBraid organization is a workspace with its own members, subscriptions, and credits. Select the organization in the workspace switcher before using its resources or changing its settings.

Your qBraid Default workspace remains available for personal work. Team subscription seats and organization credit allocations are managed separately from a personal subscription.

## Membership and access

- [Create an organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/creating-an-organization) by submitting a request for review.
- [Join an organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invitations) with an email invitation or invite code.
- [Invite codes](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invite-codes) covers shareable codes, join links, QR images, redemption, and limits.
- [Members and invitations](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/members) covers email invitations, roles, member access, and ownership transfer.
- [Settings](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/settings) controls organization details and new-member defaults.

Organizations have Admin, Manager, and Member roles, plus one Owner. Available actions depend on your role. The owner can transfer ownership to another active member through **Members > Edit Role**.

## Billing and usage

- [Seats](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/seats) grant team subscription benefits to individual members.
- [Credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credits) covers the organization wallet and transfers to members.
- [Credit requests](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests) lets members request an allocation.
- [Subscriptions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/subscriptions) covers team plans.
- [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) records credit movements.
- [Organization usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/usage) shows member consumption and quantum jobs for administrators.

## Your organization profile

[My Profile](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/profile) shows your membership roles and status in the selected organization. Its **Usage** and **API Keys** tabs provide resource and credential views for that workspace. Organization administrators use the separate organization Usage page for activity across all members.


# Create an organization
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/creating-an-organization

Request a team workspace and track or cancel your pending request.

1. Sign in to [qBraid Account](https://account.qbraid.com/).
2. Open [Request an Organization](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/new).
3. Enter the organization name.
4. Enter a description of 10 to 500 characters.
5. Optionally enter a website and address. The website must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL.
6. Explain why you need the organization in 10 to 500 characters.
7. Select **Submit Request**.

After submission, the page shows **Request Submitted**. The page states that the team reviews requests within 2 to 3 business days and emails the decision.

## Review a pending request

Return to the request page to see the submitted details and **Pending Review** status. You can have one pending request at a time. Select **Cancel Request** if you need to withdraw it.

## Switch to the new organization

After approval, switch from your personal workspace to the organization before managing its resources.

1. Open the workspace switcher at the top-left of the dashboard sidebar.
2. Select the approved organization from the list. If you belong to more than five workspaces, use the search field to filter by part of its name.
3. Wait for the switching screen to finish.
4. Check that the switcher now shows the organization you selected.

</Frame>

To return to your personal workspace, open the same switcher and select **qBraid Default**. You can switch to any organization in the list without signing out.

If an approved organization is missing, use [Refresh account data](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/refresh), then reopen the switcher. Contact [Support](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/support) if it still does not appear.

<Warning>
  Check the selected workspace before inviting members, transferring credits,
  or changing billing. These actions apply to that workspace.
</Warning>

Once you have selected the organization, [invite members](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/members), review [Settings](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/settings), or set up its [subscription](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/subscriptions).

If you already have an invitation, follow [Join an organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invitations) instead of requesting another workspace.


# Members and invitations
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/members

Invite members, manage roles and access, create invite codes, and transfer ownership.

Select your organization and open [Members](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/members). Access and available actions depend on your role. Search by name or email, then filter by role or status, including active, pending, suspended, and inactive.

## Roles

| Role    | Purpose                                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Owner   | Controls the organization and can transfer ownership.                    |
| Admin   | Manages members, resources, settings, and billing.                       |
| Manager | Invites and manages members within the permissions granted to that role. |
| Member  | Uses the organization's resources.                                       |

Invitation roles are limited by your own role. Owner is not an invitation role. The organization has one owner, and ownership changes through the transfer flow below.

## Invite a person

1. Select **Invite Member**.
2. Enter the person's email address.
3. Select an available role.
4. Optionally enter credits to allocate and a welcome message.
5. Send the invitation.

<Frame>
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nhymrGGYzQV0XrqfCJBvN1OSoxHFbk2IpcTiG" alt="Member invitation form with email, Admin, Manager, and Member roles, optional credit allocation, and welcome message" />
</Frame>

The member remains pending until they accept. They can sign up if they do not already have a qBraid account. See [Join an organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invitations) for the recipient's steps.

Invitation credit allocations are processed when the invitation is created, so they can leave the organization pool before acceptance. Cancelling or declining an invitation queues a return of allocated credits. Check [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) for the transfer and return.

## Invite several people

Select **Bulk Invite**. Add entries manually with **Add to Queue**, or upload a CSV. Download the form's CSV template to use the supported role identifiers.

```csv
email,role,credits
alice@example.com,organization_member,500
bob@example.com,organization_admin,0
carol@example.com,organization_member,1000
```

The role identifiers for ordinary organizations are `organization_admin`, `organization_manager`, and `organization_member`. Available roles still depend on your permissions. Provider organizations use their own provider roles.

Review the queue after importing. Invalid email rows can be omitted, and an unavailable role can fall back to your default role. Do not assume that every CSV row was imported unchanged.

Send at most 100 invitations per request. The total credit allocation cannot exceed the organization wallet balance. Review the per-row result after selecting **Send Invitations**.

## Manage members

Open the actions menu on a member's row. Available actions depend on the member's status and your permissions.

- **Resend Invite** sends another email for a pending invitation.
- **Cancel Invite** opens the confirmation dialog. Select **Cancel Invitation** to withdraw the pending invitation.
- **Suspend Member** suspends a member's access.
- **Activate Member** reactivates a suspended member.
- **Remove Member** removes the membership after confirmation.
- **Edit Role** changes an assignable role.

Review the confirmation before removing or suspending a member. If a removed member needs access again, send a new invitation.

## Create an invite code

Use **Members > Invite Codes** for a shareable code, join link, or QR image. Owners, Admins, and Managers can create and disable codes. Recipients join as Members on Free.

Follow [Invite codes](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invite-codes) for creation, sharing, redemption, expiration, usage limits, and existing-membership behavior.

## Transfer ownership

Only the current owner can transfer ownership to another active member.

1. Find the recipient on **Members**.
2. Open **Edit Role**.
3. Select **Transfer ownership**.
4. Review the confirmation naming the new owner.
5. Confirm **Make [name] the owner**.

You become an admin after the transfer. Only the new owner can transfer ownership back. Pending invitees cannot receive ownership.


# Join an organization
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invitations

Accept an email invitation or redeem an organization invite code.

## Accept an email invitation

Open the invitation link to review the organization and invitee details. If you are signed out, sign up or sign in with the invited email address.

Select **Accept invitation** to join, or **Decline** to reject the invitation. Opening the link alone does not accept it.

If the page says **Wrong account**, select **Sign in with different account**. For a cancelled or invalid invitation, ask the inviter to send a new one.

You can also open [Invitations](https://account.qbraid.com/invitations) while signed in to accept or decline pending invitations sent to your email.

## Join with a code

Use **Have an invite code?** on [Invitations](https://account.qbraid.com/invitations), open the shared join link, or scan its QR image. The preview asks you to confirm **Join [organization name]** after sign-in.

Follow [Join with a code](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invite-codes#join-with-a-code) for the complete steps and [existing-membership behavior](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invite-codes#existing-memberships). Codes grant the Member role on Free, which can differ from a role offered through an email invitation.


# Invite codes
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/invite-codes

Create and share organization invite codes, join with a code, and manage limits and access.

An invite code lets several people join the same organization without individual email invitations. Share the code, its join link, or a QR image for a class, workshop, or team.

Anyone with a valid code can sign in and join as a **Member** on the **Free** tier. A code does not allocate credits or assign a paid subscription seat. Use [email invitations](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/members#invite-a-person) when you need to choose an invitee's role or include a credit allocation.

## Create a code

Organization **Owners**, **Admins**, and **Managers** can create, list, and disable codes. Members cannot manage codes. Codes are unavailable in **qBraid Default**, your personal workspace.

1. Use the workspace switcher to select your organization.
2. Open [Members](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/members).
3. Select the **Invite Codes** tab.
4. Select **Create code**.
5. Enter a **Name** to identify the code, such as the name of a class or event.
6. Set **Max uses** and **Expires on** if you want limits.
7. Select **Create code** to open the **Code created** screen.

<Frame>
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50n7NvHZZn3E50nuDkBRIcvtwyzsbLZmTOaipHe" alt="Create invite code dialog with name, use limit, expiration, and fixed Member and Free tier grants" />
</Frame>

| Field      | Requirement and default                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name       | Required, up to 100 characters. This label helps you identify the code later.                                                                                           |
| Max uses   | Optional whole number of at least 1. Leave it blank for unlimited uses.                                                                                                 |
| Expires on | Optional date. Leave it blank for no expiration. A selected date expires at the end of that day in the creator's local time zone. The expiration must be in the future. |

qBraid generates the code. The **Grants** labels show **MEMBER** and **FREE TIER**. These grants are fixed for code redemption, even if the organization has automatic seat assignment enabled for email invitations.

## Share the code, link, or QR image

On **Code created**, choose the format your recipients need:

- Copy **Code** for someone who will enter it manually.
- Copy **Join link** to send a link that opens the organization preview.
- Select **Download QR** to save a PNG image. Scanning the QR opens the same join link.

Download the QR image before selecting **Done**. Later, the **Invite Codes** table lets you copy the code or join link again.

Share only with the people you intend to invite. Codes are not restricted to an email address, and anyone who receives a forwarded code or link can use it while it remains valid.

## Join with a code

1. Open the shared join link, scan the QR image, or visit [Join with an invite code](https://account.qbraid.com/join).
2. If you are entering a code manually, paste it into **Invite code** and select **Continue**. You can also use **Have an invite code?** on [Invitations](https://account.qbraid.com/invitations).
3. Review the organization name in the preview.
4. If you are signed out, select **Sign up to join** or **I already have an account**. Finish sign-in to return to the preview.
5. Select **Join [organization name]** to confirm.

The entry form accepts lowercase letters and ignores spaces and hyphens. Enter the code itself in this field, not the full join URL. Opening the link or preview alone does not join the organization.

After a successful join, Account refreshes your membership information and opens the dashboard for that organization. Check the workspace switcher before using its resources. Ask an administrator for [credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests) or a [subscription seat](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/seats) if you need them.

## Track uses and disable a code

The **Invite Codes** table shows **Name**, **Code**, **Uses**, **Expires**, and **Status**. **Uses** compares the recorded usage count with the limit, or shows an unlimited maximum. **Expires** shows the expiration date and time in the viewer's local time zone, or **Never**.

| Status   | Meaning                                                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active   | The code is enabled, has not expired, and has remaining capacity. |
| Full     | The code has reached its maximum number of uses.                  |
| Expired  | The expiration time has passed.                                   |
| Disabled | Someone disabled the code. It cannot accept new joins.            |

To stop an active code, select its **Disable** action and confirm **Disable** in the dialog. Select **Keep it** to cancel.

Disabling a code is permanent. Create a new code if you want to invite more people afterward. Existing members keep their memberships, and the disabled code remains in the list. There is no edit or re-enable control for an existing code.

## Existing memberships

| Your current status in the organization | What happens when you use a valid code                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active                                  | The preview says **You're already a member**. Select **Open [organization name]**. Opening the organization does not use another redemption.                                             |
| Pending email invitation                | You can join with the code as a Member on Free. This does not preserve a higher role offered by the email invitation. Accept the email invitation instead if you need its assigned role. |
| Removed                                 | You can rejoin as a Member on Free. Previous roles, permission overrides, and paid-seat assignment are not restored.                                                                     |
| Suspended or inactive                   | Redemption is blocked. Contact the organization administrator to resolve your membership. A code cannot bypass this restriction.                                                         |

An active member can still open their organization from a known code's preview after that code becomes full, expired, or disabled. This does not make the code available to new members.

## Troubleshoot joining

- **This code can't be used** means the code is invalid, expired, full, or disabled. Select **Enter a different code** or ask the organization for a new one.
- **Couldn't check this code** means the preview could not be loaded. Select **Try again** before assuming the code is invalid.
- **Invite code is no longer valid** can appear if the code expires, fills, or is disabled after you open the preview. Ask for another code.
- A suspended, inactive, or changed-membership error requires help from the organization administrator. Retrying a different code does not restore suspended access.

If **Invite Codes** is missing, check the selected workspace and your role. You need a team organization and a member-management role. If the code list fails to load, use its **Try again** button.

If membership changes have not appeared, use [Refresh account data](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/refresh) before checking the workspace switcher again.


# Seats
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/seats

Assign your subscription's seats to specific members and revoke them when people move on.

An assigned seat gives a member your team subscription's benefits. Unassigned seats remain available for other members.

The Seat Management table is on the **Subscription** tab of the [Billing page](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/billing).

## Assign a seat

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher in the top-left of the dashboard and select your
    organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Stay on the Subscription tab">It's the default tab.</Step>
  <Step title="Scroll to Seat Management">
    The table sits below the subscription card.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open the assign dialog">
    Find an active member and click **Assign Seat** on their row.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review the assignment">
    Check the tier, available seats, credits to transfer, and resulting
    organization balance.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm">Click **Assign Seat**.</Step>
</Steps>

<Check>
  The member gets tier benefits right away. If you've turned on
  credits-on-assign in [Settings](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/settings), they also
  receive a credit transfer at the same time.
</Check>

<Tip>
  Turn on **Auto-assign Seats** in
  [Settings](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/settings) and new members get a seat
  automatically when they accept an email invitation, if assignment succeeds.
  Invite-code joins do not assign seats. Check Seat Management after acceptance.
</Tip>

## Revoke a seat

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
