    Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Stay on the Subscription tab">It's the default tab.</Step>
  <Step title="Scroll to Seat Management">
    The table sits below the subscription card.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Click Revoke">On the member's row.</Step>
  <Step title="Confirm">Confirm in the dialog.</Step>
</Steps>

The seat becomes available for another member. The member loses tier benefits but keeps any credits already in their wallet.

## How seats and members interact

| Action                                                       | Effect on seat                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Member accepts email invitation (with Auto-assign Seats on)  | Attempts to assign an available seat. Check capacity and credits if none is assigned. |
| Member accepts email invitation (with Auto-assign Seats off) | They join without a seat. Assign one manually if needed.                              |
| Admin removes a member                                       | Revoke the member's seat before removal if you need to free capacity.                 |
| Admin suspends a member                                      | An assigned seat can remain assigned. Use **Revoke** to return it to the pool.        |
| Subscription is canceled (period ends)                       | All assigned seats are revoked at the same time.                                      |
| Admin adds seats to the subscription                         | New seats become available to assign.                                                 |

Invite-code recipients join as Members on Free even when **Auto-assign Seats** is enabled. Assign their seats manually. Activating a membership also attempts automatic assignment when enabled.

## Need more seats?

Adding seats is a billing action, not a member action. See [Subscriptions > Add more seats](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/subscriptions#add-more-seats).

## Find a member and check eligibility

Use **Search members** in Seat Management to find a member by name or email. The table shows membership status and seat status separately. Only active members can receive a seat. An inactive or suspended member can still have an assigned seat, so revoke it explicitly when you need to free capacity.

A member with a personal paid tier and no organization seat displays that tier instead of an assignment action. A paid tier alone does not mean the organization assigned a seat.

The organization owner's seat cannot be revoked from Seat Management. If assignment includes a credit transfer, the organization must have enough credits to fund it.


# Credits
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credits

Buy credits for the organization, transfer them to members, and approve credit requests.

Administrators buy credits for the organization wallet, then transfer them to members to fund their work.

Open the [Billing page](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/billing) to see the organization balance, buy credits, or transfer them to members.

## Buy credits for the org

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher in the top-left of the dashboard and select your
    organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Click Buy Credits">In the top-right of the Billing page.</Step>
  <Step title="Enter an amount">
    Type the dollar amount you want to spend. The credit count updates as you
    type.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Purchase">
    Click **Purchase** and finish checkout on Stripe.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Check>The purchase adds credits to the organization wallet.</Check>

## Transfer credits to members

1. Switch to the organization and open **Billing**.
2. Select **Transfer** on the Balance card.
3. Use **Selected** to choose one or more active members, or **All Members** for every active member.
4. Enter the **Amount per member** and an optional reason.
5. Review the recipient count and total, then confirm the transfer.

Search the recipient list to find members. Review the selection before you use the option to add all matching members.

The organization wallet must cover the total amount. For example, 100 credits each for three members requires 300 credits. Credits go to each member's wallet within this organization. They do not become a personal qBraid Default balance.

## Approve a credit request

Owners and Admins review member requests in **Billing > Credit Requests**. Approval queues the full requested amount for transfer to the member's organization wallet. The organization pool must cover that amount.

Follow [Approve a credit request](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests#approve-a-credit-request) to review the recipient, reason, balances, and completed transfer.

## Reject a credit request

Rejection requires a reason of 10 to 500 characters and does not transfer credits. Follow [Reject a credit request](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests#reject-a-credit-request) to record the decision.

Members can [submit, track, or cancel a request](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests) from their organization Wallet.

<Tip>
  Set **Seat Assignment Credits** in [Settings > Member
  Settings](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/settings#member-settings) to transfer
  credits when a seat is assigned. Joining with an invite code does not assign
  a seat or trigger this allocation.
</Tip>

## Credit sources and allocations

Direct purchases add credits to the organization wallet. A transfer or configured seat-assignment allocation moves credits out of that pool and into a member's organization wallet. Seat assignment does not create new credits.

When a member leaves voluntarily, their remaining organization-wallet credits are queued for return to the organization. Review [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) to audit purchases, allocations, and returns.


# Credit requests
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credit-requests

Request organization credits, cancel a pending request, and approve or reject requests as an administrator.

Use **Wallet** in an organization workspace to request credits from the organization pool. Organization Owners and Admins review requests in **Billing > Credit Requests**. Managers and Members cannot approve or reject requests.

Approved credits go to your member wallet within the selected organization. Use that organization workspace when you spend them. They do not add to your personal qBraid Default balance.

<Note>
  Credit requests are available in organization workspaces. In **qBraid Default**,
  use [Buy credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/buy-credits) to fund your personal wallet.
</Note>

## Submit a request

Use these steps as a member.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Select your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher in the top-left of the dashboard. Select the
    organization that will fund your work.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Wallet">
    Select **Account > Wallet** in the sidebar. Under **Need more credits?**, select **Request credits**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enter the amount and reason">
    The **Request Credits from Organization** dialog opens. Enter a whole number of credits
    from 1 to 10,000 in **Amount**.

    **Reason** is optional. Leave it blank, or enter 10 to 500 characters
    that explain what you need the credits for. For example, name the project and
    the work you plan to run.

    <Frame>
      <img
        src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-request-credits.webp"
        alt="Request Credits from Organization dialog with 100 entered as the amount and a short reason, and the Submit Request button enabled"
      />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Submit the request">
    Select **Submit Request**. Select **Cancel** instead if you do not want to
    send it. The dialog tells you that the request goes to organization owners and admins for approval.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Check the pending state">
    The **Need more credits?** panel changes to **Request for _N_ credits is pending**. It shows the send date and your reason. **Request credits** turns off until an admin processes the request.

    <Frame>
      <img
        src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-request-pending.webp"
        alt="Your credits card showing Request for 100 credits is pending with View request and a turned-off Request credits button"
      />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
</Steps>

You can have one pending request at a time in each organization. Submitting a request does not transfer credits.

## Track the request

1. Select the same organization in the workspace switcher.
2. Open **Account > Wallet**.
3. Select **View request**.
4. Review **Amount**, **Reason**, **Status**, and **Requested** in the **Pending Credit Request** dialog.
5. Select **Close** to leave the request pending.

<Frame caption="The request stays pending until an administrator processes it or you cancel it.">
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-view-request.webp"
    alt="Pending Credit Request dialog showing 100 credits, the reason, Pending status, the request time, and Close and Cancel Request buttons"
  />
</Frame>

This dialog shows your pending request. It does not show completed requests or an administrator's rejection reason. After an administrator approves or rejects it, check your Wallet balance in the organization, or ask an administrator about the decision.

## Cancel or change a pending request

You can cancel your own pending request. To change its amount or reason, cancel it and submit a new request.

1. Open **Wallet > View request** in the same organization.
2. Select **Cancel Request**.
3. Review the amount in **Cancel Credit Request?**.
4. Select **Cancel Request** again to confirm, or **Keep Request** to leave it pending.
5. After cancellation, use **Request credits** to submit a replacement if needed.

You cannot cancel a request after an administrator approves or rejects it. If an administrator acts on the request while the dialog is open, refresh the account data before you do anything else.

## Review requests as an administrator

1. Select the organization in the workspace switcher.
2. Open [Billing](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/billing).
3. Select **Credit Requests**.
4. Find the member in **Pending Requests**.
5. Read the amount and reason. Then select **Approve** or **Reject**.

<Frame caption="The pending count appears on Credit Requests. Review the member, amount, and reason before you act.">
  <img
    src="/v2/account/_static/wallet-admin-requests.webp"
    alt="Billing page in an organization with the Credit Requests tab open, listing pending requests with member, amount, reason, date, and Approve and Reject buttons"
  />
</Frame>

Each pending row shows the member's name and email, requested amount, reason, request date, and **Approve** and **Reject** actions. The table can shorten long reasons. Open **Approve** to read the full reason before you decide, then select **Cancel** if you do not want to approve it.

### Approve a credit request

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the approval dialog">
    Select **Approve** on the member's request.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review the recipient and balance">
    In **Approve Credit Request**, verify the member, reason, **Amount to transfer**,
    **Current org balance**, and **New org balance**.

    Approval transfers the full requested amount. This dialog does not let you
    change the amount or add an approval note.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm approval">
    Select **Approve Request** and wait for the success message.
    Select **Cancel** instead to leave the request pending.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Check the result">
    The request moves to **Request History** with status **accepted**.
    Check the organization balance and [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions).
    The member sees the new balance in **Wallet** when they select
    the same organization.
  </Step>
</Steps>

If the pool cannot cover the request, the dialog shows **Insufficient organization balance. Buy more credits first.** and disables approval. [Buy credits for the organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credits#buy-credits-for-the-org), then reopen the request after the balance updates.

If a different amount is appropriate, ask the member to cancel and submit a revised request. You can also reject the request with an explanation and make a [direct transfer](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credits#transfer-credits-to-members). Resolve the original request first so it does not remain available for another approval.

### Reject a credit request

1. In **Pending Requests**, select **Reject** on the member's row.
2. In **Reject Credit Request**, enter a **Rejection Reason** of 10 to 500 characters.
3. Explain the decision and any next step, such as requesting a different amount.
4. Select **Reject Request** and wait for confirmation. To leave the request pending, select **Cancel** instead.

The request moves to **Request History** with status **rejected**. Rejection does not transfer credits. The member can submit another request after the rejection. Share the decision with the member if they need the explanation, because Wallet does not display completed request details.

## Check request history

The **Request History** table shows the member, amount, status, and original request date. **accepted** means an administrator approved the request. **rejected** means an administrator declined it. The date is the request date, not the decision date.

The tab shows up to 20 of the newest requests across pending requests and history, with only the latest request retained for each member. A replacement request can therefore remove an earlier decision from this view. Canceled requests do not appear in history.

Use [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) to check credit movements and [Audit logs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/audit-logs) to investigate recorded administrator actions. Request History is not a complete record of all past requests or proof that a queued transfer has finished.

## Resolve a request problem

- If you already have a pending request, open **View request**. Cancel it before submitting a replacement.
- If the request fails to send, check the amount and the reason. The amount must be a whole number from 1 to 10,000. A reason, if you add one, must be 10 to 500 characters.
- If a request is no longer pending, another action may have processed or canceled it. [Refresh account data](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/refresh), then check the request list.
- If approval fails or the balance has not updated, check the current request status and Transactions before retrying or making a separate transfer.
- If **Credit Requests** is unavailable, verify the selected organization and your Owner or Admin role.

For an urgent request, contact an organization administrator. Administrators can [transfer credits directly](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/credits#transfer-credits-to-members) without requiring a request.


# Team subscriptions
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/subscriptions

Buy a team plan, change tier or interval, add capacity, and handle cancellations.

A team subscription gives your organization a Standard or Pro tier and seats you assign to members. Members with a seat get the tier's benefits. Members without one stay on Free-level access.

<Note>
  Team subscriptions are different from personal ones. They're priced per seat,
  managed inside qBraid (not Stripe), and let you give benefits to specific
  members. See [Personal vs Team
  comparison](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/wallet/subscriptions#personal-vs-team).
</Note>

## Plans

| Plan     | Monthly per seat | Annual, per seat per month | Compute per seat      | Storage per seat |
| -------- | ---------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| Standard | \$20             | \$16                       | 400 CPU hrs / month   | 50 GB            |
| Pro      | \$100            | \$80                       | 2,000 CPU hrs / month | 150 GB           |

The annual column shows monthly equivalents. The yearly charge is $192 per Standard seat or $960 per Pro seat. Team subscriptions require at least two seats. Review the full checkout total before subscribing.

Standard includes full Qubes and Quantum Software Engineering course access and priority support. Pro includes higher AI usage limits and dedicated support. Each assigned Standard seat has a limit of 500 jobs per managed simulator per day, or 125 free circuits per day on each [GPU simulator](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/pricing#gpu-simulators). Pro has no daily job-count limit for those simulators. Device usage charges can still apply.

For Enterprise, use **Contact Sales** to submit an organization request for custom terms.

## Create a team subscription

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher in the top-left of the dashboard and select your
    organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Click Create Subscription">
    In the top-right of the Billing page, click **Create Subscription**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick a tier">Choose **Standard** or **Pro**.</Step>
  <Step title="Choose billing interval">
    Monthly or Annual. Annual billing saves 20% compared with twelve monthly
    payments.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enter number of seats">Minimum is 2 seats.</Step>
  <Step title="Subscribe">
    Click **Proceed to Payment** and finish checkout on Stripe.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Check>
  After checkout, wait for the Billing page to confirm the subscription.
</Check>

## Upgrade

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Stay on the Subscription tab">It's the default tab.</Step>
  <Step title="Open the manage dialog">
    Click **Manage Team Subscription** on the subscription card.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick the Plan Tier tab">
    It's the default tab in the dialog.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Upgrade">
    Click **Upgrade to Pro Now** (or Standard, if you're starting from Free).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm">
    The confirmation dialog shows the prorated cost. Click **Confirm**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Check>
  The new tier takes effect immediately. Stripe prorates the difference for the
  current period.
</Check>

## Downgrade

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Open Manage Team Subscription">
    On the Subscription tab, click **Manage Team Subscription**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Stay on the Plan Tier tab">It's the default tab.</Step>
  <Step title="Scroll to Downgrade to Standard">
    Review the benefits and effective date in the dialog.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Schedule the downgrade">
    Click **Schedule Downgrade** and confirm. You keep Pro features until the
    end of the current billing period.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  You can't change tier while a cancellation is scheduled. Reactivate the
  subscription first.
</Note>

## Switch between monthly and annual

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Open Manage Team Subscription">
    On the Subscription tab, click **Manage Team Subscription**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open the Billing Interval tab">
    Click the **Billing Interval** tab inside the dialog.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick the new interval">Switch between Monthly and Annual.</Step>
</Steps>

Both interval changes update the subscription through Stripe with proration. Review the confirmation dialog and the resulting billing dates. An annual-to-monthly change is not a scheduled tier downgrade.

## Add more seats

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">Click **Billing** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Stay on the Subscription tab">It's the default tab.</Step>
  <Step title="Click Add Seats">On the subscription card.</Step>
  <Step title="Enter the new total">
    Enter the desired total in **New Seat Count**. It must exceed the current
    total. For example, enter 6 to add 4 seats to a subscription with 2 seats.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm">
    Stripe charges a prorated amount for the rest of the period.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Check>
  The new seats are available to assign immediately. See
  [Seats](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/seats) for how to assign them.
</Check>

## Cancel

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Billing">
    Click **Billing** in the sidebar.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Manage Team Subscription">
    On the Subscription tab, click **Manage Team Subscription**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Expand Cancel Subscription">
    Scroll to the bottom of the dialog and click into the **Cancel Subscription** section.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Read what you'll lose">
    All assigned seats are revoked at the end of the current period. Members keep any credits already in their wallets.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Tick the confirmation box">
    *"I understand this will revoke all `<n>` assigned seats at end of period and cannot be undone."*
  </Step>
  <Step title="Cancel">
    Click **Cancel Team Subscription**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

The subscription enters the **canceling** state, and a banner shows the end date. Resubscribe before that date to cancel the scheduled cancellation.

<Danger>
  Once the period ends, every assigned seat is revoked and members return to
  Free-tier access. Members keep their wallet credits.
</Danger>

## Invoices and scheduled changes

Open **Billing > Invoices** for organization invoice dates, billing periods, totals, statuses, receipt links, and PDFs.

A scheduled tier downgrade prevents a billing-interval change until you cancel the scheduled downgrade. A scheduled cancellation also prevents plan changes until you reactivate. Review the effective date and proration shown in the confirmation dialog before you apply a change.

Use [Audit logs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/audit-logs) to review recorded subscription and seat changes, including who performed them and their results.


# Transactions
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions

Filter organization credit activity, export matching transactions, and inspect charges.

Switch to your organization and open [Billing](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/billing), then select **Transactions**. This log records organization credit purchases, transfers, deductions, and refunds.

## Filter transactions

Use the **Type**, **Status**, and **Date range** controls above the table. The default range is **Last 7 days**. Other ranges include **Last 30 days**, **Last 90 days**, **Last 12 months**, and **Custom**. For a custom range, enter the start and end dates.

Filters are stored in the page URL. **Reset filters** clears the selection. Status filtering applies to the fetched page, so a page can contain fewer visible rows than the page size.

## Read the table

The table shows **Date**, **Type**, **Description**, **Amount**, **Balance after**, and **Status**. Use the pagination controls to move through the history. Each page fetches up to 20 transactions.

Charges for the same compute resource and day can appear as a collapsed group. Expand the group to inspect its individual billing periods. The number of displayed rows can therefore be smaller than the number of transactions.

Select a transaction to open its details. Depending on the charge, the panel includes resource information, the billing period, balance after the transaction, and a receipt link. Select **Refresh** to retrieve recent activity.

## Export CSV

Select **Export CSV** to download transactions matching the selected type, date range, and status. Organization exports fetch all matching pages. This differs from the personal wallet export, which exports the current page.

The file is named `org-transactions-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv`. If the result exceeds the supported export size, narrow the date range or type and export again. The application reports an oversized export instead of silently downloading a partial file.

## Report a transaction problem

1. Find and open the transaction.
2. Select **Report issue**.
3. Describe the problem in the support dialog.
4. Submit the report.

The dialog includes the transaction ID and billing details so support can locate the charge.

## Invoices

Use the separate **Invoices** tab for Stripe invoices issued to the organization. It shows the invoice date, billing period, total, and status, with **Receipt** and **PDF** links when available. The personal wallet's invoice section shows your personal billing account instead.

Use [Audit logs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/audit-logs) to find who initiated a credit or billing action, inspect its result, and export the recorded activity.


# Organization usage
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/usage

Find which members consume organization credits, inspect their transactions, and review quantum job activity.

Organization Owners and Admins use **Usage** to see which members spend credits and which quantum jobs they submit. Managers and Members cannot open this organization-wide view.

## Open organization usage

1. Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
2. Open [Usage](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/usage) in the organization section of the sidebar.
3. Select **Credits** to compare member spending, or **Jobs** to review quantum job activity.

This page is different from **Account > Usage**, which shows your own allowances and sessions in the selected workspace. Organization Usage reports recorded credit and job activity. It does not show what every member is currently doing in Lab or the contents of their notebooks and AI conversations.

## Compare credit consumption

<Frame caption="The Credits view combines organization totals, category spending, and member activity. Member identities are redacted in this full-page capture.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50ngKWmtaxAwtMk8DKLhmecZl0WOz65jdsNTA2J" alt="Full organization Usage Credits page showing summary cards, consumption by category, and the member activity table with identities redacted" />
</Frame>

[Open the full-size Credits screenshot](https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50ngKWmtaxAwtMk8DKLhmecZl0WOz65jdsNTA2J).

Start in **Credits**, which opens the **Member usage** view.

1. Choose **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days**, **Last 90 days**, or **Last 12 months** from the range selector.
2. Review the four summary cards.
3. Compare **Consumption by category**.
4. Scroll to **Members** to identify who accounts for the spending.

The default range is **Last 30 days**. **Last 12 months** covers the most recent 365 days, not all-time history. The range applies to the consumption summary and member transactions. The **Trend (14d)** column always shows a recent 14-day window.

### Read the summary cards

| Card | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Total consumption** | Recorded organization credit consumption for the selected period. This is a spending total, not the available organization balance. |
| **Top spender** | The member with the highest reported period spend, their credits spent, and their share of organization consumption. |
| **Largest category** | The largest of Jobs, Compute, and AI Chat, with its credit amount and share. |
| **Active members** | Active organization memberships out of total membership records, with their percentage. |

<Note>
  The **Active members** caption currently says "consumed credits this period",
  but the count comes from membership status. Use each member's **Period spend**
  to determine whether they consumed credits during the selected range.
</Note>

### Compare categories

**Consumption by category** separates **Jobs**, **Compute**, and **AI Chat**. The stacked bar shows their relative shares. The amounts and percentages below it show the recorded credits for each category.

Use this breakdown to distinguish a rise in quantum job spending from compute or AI spending. It does not show individual chat messages, source programs, or files. For purchases, transfers, and refunds, use [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) or the member transaction view below.

### Find a member

Use **Search members** to match a name, username, or email. Clear the search to return to the loaded member list. Use the sort selector to order members by highest spend, lowest spend, most recent activity, or name.

| Column | How to read it |
| --- | --- |
| **Member** | The member's name and email. |
| **Role** | Their organization role, or **Pending** for an invitation. |
| **Breakdown** | Their Jobs, Compute, and AI Chat consumption, using the same colors as the category card. |
| **Period spend** | Their reported credits spent during the selected range and percentage of organization consumption. |
| **Trend (14d)** | Daily spending bars for the recent 14-day window, oldest on the left and newest on the right. Each member's bars use their own scale. |
| **Last activity** | The most recent recorded consumption activity in the selected period, with a relative time and date. This is not the member's last sign-in. |
| **View jobs** | A shortcut to the Jobs tab with that member selected. |

Do not compare bar heights between members to compare absolute spending. Use **Period spend** for that comparison. A taller trend bar means a busier day relative to that member's own recent spending.

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nscgZhQ4aWSITbPiM6GF9qAr2yUNdxe8BQtLO"
    alt="Organization usage filtered to Documentation QA, showing its Admin role and no activity during the selected period"
  />
</Frame>

This filtered example shows an Admin account with no consumption during the selected period. **No activity** does not mean the person has never used qBraid. The footer counts the members currently shown and those with no activity in the selected period.

Pending invitations show **Awaiting invite** and **Invite pending**. Their rows do not open transaction details. For larger organizations, the Credits member table loads up to 100 members and searches within that list. The summary cards cover organization-wide consumption, so the visible rows might not account for every member in the totals.

## Inspect a member's transactions

1. Set the date range in **Credits**.
2. Find the member in the **Members** table.
3. Select their row. Keyboard users can focus the row and press **Enter** or **Space**.
4. Read **Date**, **Type**, and **Amount** in the member's transaction table.
5. Use **Previous** and **Next** to move through pages when available.
6. Select **All members** to return to the comparison view.

The detail view loads 20 transactions per page and retains the selected date range. Its transaction count covers matching transactions, not just the visible page. Return to **All members** to change the range.

This view includes consumption and other wallet activity, such as transfers, grants, and refunds. An incoming credit transfer can therefore appear for a member whose **Period spend** is zero. Read the transaction type and signed amount before treating a movement as consumption. The rows show transaction summaries rather than the underlying program, notebook, or conversation.

If **No transactions recorded for this member in the selected range.** appears, return to **All members** and widen the date range. Check the selected organization before concluding that the member has no history.

## Review quantum job activity

<Frame caption="The Jobs view shows member activity, execution status, devices, shots, and cost. Member names and job identifiers are redacted.">
  <img src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50n9sSvSp8VS286yKEb5TWqowfmRPC1Xl3O4xzh" alt="Organization Usage Jobs tab with member and status filters, column controls, two completed jobs, and pagination; member names and job identifiers are redacted" />
</Frame>

Open **Jobs** to see who submitted jobs, where they ran, their status, and their reported cost. You can also select **View jobs** beside a member in Credits to open this tab with that member selected.

### Filter jobs

1. Open **All members** to choose a member, or leave it unchanged for the organization-wide view.
2. In the member picker, type at least two characters to search. If it shows only part of the list, narrow the search.
3. Use **All statuses** to select a job state.
4. Review the matching rows and use the page controls for more jobs.
5. To remove the filters, select **All members** and **All statuses** again.

The status selector includes **INITIALIZING**, **QUEUED**, **VALIDATING**, **RUNNING**, **CANCELLING**, **CANCELLED**, **COMPLETED**, **FAILED**, **HOLD**, and **UNKNOWN**. For example, select a member and **RUNNING** to inspect their recorded running quantum jobs.

You can also select a name in the table's **Member** column to filter to that person. Member and status filters apply across the matching history, not just the visible page. They reset pagination to the first page. The Credits date range does not filter Jobs.

The table starts with 25 jobs per page, newest submissions first. Use **Rows per page** to change the page size. **Customize Columns**, labeled **Columns** on narrower screens, controls which columns are visible.

### Read the job table

| Column | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Member** | Who submitted the job. Departed members can show **removed**, and deleted accounts show **Deleted account**. |
| **Job** | The job's qBraid Resource Name, or QRN. |
| **Status** | The recorded job state. |
| **Provider** | The service that runs the job. |
| **Device** | The device name or its QRN. |
| **Shots** | The requested measurement repetitions. |
| **Cost (cr)** | The recorded cost in credits when available. A dash means the cost is unavailable, not that the job was free. |
| **Submitted** | The recorded submission date and time. |

The organization view can include jobs from members who have since left. Their recorded job activity remains relevant to the organization's usage.

### Inspect job details

1. Select a job row outside the member-name link.
2. Review its identifier, status, and **Details** in the side panel.
3. Expand **Runtime Options** if that section is available.
4. Close the panel to return to the table.

Available details can include the provider, device, experiment type, shots, circuit count, queue position, timestamps, duration, cost, and estimated cost. Failed jobs can show a failure message. Fields depend on the recorded job data.

<Note>
  The organization job view is read-only. It hides **Program** and **Results**,
  and it does not let an administrator cancel or delete another member's job.
  Use this view to review member activity and job metadata. The job owner can
  inspect their own program and results in [Quantum Jobs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/quantum-jobs).
</Note>

## Share a view or recover missing data

The selected tab, Credits date range and member detail, and Jobs member/status filters are stored in the page URL. Share the URL with another authorized Owner or Admin, who must select the same organization. Credits search text, sort order, and page positions are not part of that saved view.

Use [Refresh account data](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/refresh) to request current data.

- If **Couldn't load usage stats** appears, select **Try again**. The member rows are not reliable evidence of zero activity while the summary has failed.
- If **No members match that search.** appears, clear the Credits search. In a large organization, the loaded Credits list may omit members beyond its limit.
- If **Could not load jobs** appears, select **Try again**. A failed query is not an empty job history.
- If **This organization is too large to list at once** appears, select a member to retrieve their jobs.
- If no jobs match, clear the member and status filters before concluding that the organization has no job history.
- If you cannot open Usage, check the selected organization and your Owner or Admin role.

Use [Account Usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage) for your own compute, storage, simulator, and AI allowances. Use [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) for organization credit movements and [Audit logs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/audit-logs) for recorded changes to settings, membership, credits, and subscriptions.


# Audit logs
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/audit-logs

Find who changed organization settings, members, credits, subscriptions, jobs, and API keys, then export the recorded activity.

Organization Owners and Admins can review the organization's recorded activity in **Billing > Audit log**. Managers and Members cannot access this page. Audit logs are not available in the personal **qBraid Default** workspace.

## Open the audit log

1. Use the workspace switcher to select your organization.
2. Open [Billing](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/billing?tab=audit-log).
3. Select **Audit log** if it is not already open.
4. Review the newest entries first. Select **Load more** to retrieve older matching entries.

The table loads 25 entries at a time. The count below it is the number currently shown, not the total number of matching events.

## Find an event

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nwjCgfuBL9Uo8LlVXWaATyftYdIq5HzxghPbQ"
    alt="Billing Audit log tab with action, member, result, date filters, Reset, and Export controls"
  />
</Frame>

Use the Audit log tab in Billing. The filters and Export button appear above the entries.

Use the filters together to narrow the history:

| Filter | What it selects |
| --- | --- |
| **All actions** | A specific action, such as **Role changed**, **Credits transferred**, **Seat assigned**, or **API key revoked**. |
| **All members** | The member who performed the action, rather than the member affected by it. |
| **All results** | **Success**, **Denied**, **Failed**, or **Error**. |
| **From date** | Events from the start of the selected day in your local time zone. |
| **To date** | Events through the end of the selected day in your local time zone. |

The initial date window starts 30 days ago and has no end date. Clear **From date** to include older retained history. Clear both date fields to remove the date limits. Choose a From date that is no later than the To date.

Changing a filter reloads the matching entries from the first page. **Reset** restores all actions, members, and results, with the original 30-day starting date. It does not select all time.

Filters are stored in the page URL. You can share the URL with another authorized administrator, who must also select the same organization. The member picker lists up to 100 members. If the person you need is missing, use **All members** and narrow by action and date instead.

## Read an entry

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Time** | When the event was recorded, displayed in your local time. |
| **Member** | Who performed the action. Recorded identity details are used when available. Older entries can show an identifier or **Deleted user**. |
| **Action** | The attempted action and a summary of recorded changes. |
| **Target** | The affected member, members, or job, when recorded. |
| **Source** | **Web**, **API key**, **Lab/Pod**, or **MCP**. Older entries can have no recorded source. |
| **Result** | Whether the request succeeded, was denied, failed, or encountered a server error. |

Select a row or **Show details** to inspect its recorded details. These can include full before-and-after values, the target's name and email, a reason, additional event information, an IP address, and a request ID. Only one entry expands at a time. Select **Hide details** to close it.

A **Denied** or **Failed** entry records an unsuccessful attempt. Its action name or listed fields do not prove that the requested change happened. Bulk actions can record partial completion, so read the target and details before assuming every requested item succeeded.

**Target** and **Source** are hidden on narrower screens. Use a wider window or export the filtered history to inspect those columns.

## Check credits and billing changes

Filter for the action you are investigating, then inspect its result and details. For example, use **Credits transferred** to investigate a member allocation, or **Subscription changed** to find a recorded plan change.

**Checkout started** records the start of checkout. It does not confirm payment. **Credits purchased** records the completed credit purchase. Use [Transactions](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/transactions) to reconcile credit movements and **Billing > Invoices** for invoices and receipts.

The log covers recorded member, invite-code, credit, subscription, seat, organization-setting, job-deletion/restoration, and API-key actions. It is not a record of every page visit or a usage report. Use [Organization usage](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/usage) for resource consumption and jobs.

## Export matching entries

1. Select the action, member, result, and date range you need.
2. Select **Export** and wait for the download.
3. Open the downloaded `audit-log-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` file.
4. Check the export notification for the number of entries and any limit warning.

Export fetches matching entries beyond the pages you have loaded in the table, up to **5,000 entries**. If more entries match, it exports the first 5,000 and asks you to narrow the date range. Export smaller date ranges to retrieve the remaining history.

The CSV includes Time, Member, Email, Action, Changes, Target, Source, Result, and Request ID. It uses the table's change summaries; it does not include every field from expanded details. CSV timestamps retain the recorded timestamp, while the table displays local time. Keep this distinction in mind when comparing dates in a spreadsheet.

## Refresh and troubleshoot

Use [Refresh account data](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/refresh) to request current organization data, including the audit log. The tab has no separate Refresh button.

- If **The audit log could not be loaded.** appears, select **Try again**. A loading failure does not mean that no activity exists.
- If **No entries match these filters.** appears, select **Reset filters** or widen the dates. Reset returns to the 30-day default.
- Even **No activity recorded yet.** is subject to the default date window. Clear From date before concluding that no older entries are available.
- If **Export failed** appears, review the error and retry. Do not treat a failed export as a complete record.
- If you cannot open the tab, check the selected organization and your Owner or Admin role.

Only recorded, retained events can appear. An empty result does not establish that an action never occurred. If you need help investigating an event, send [Support](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/support) its time, action, result, and request ID when available.


# Settings
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/settings

Set your org's name and logo, control what happens when new members join, and find owner-only actions.

Owners and Admins can use **General** and **Member Settings** on the [Settings page](https://account.qbraid.com/organizations/settings) to update organization details and member settings. Only the Owner sees **Danger Zone**.

## General

Organization details appear in invitations, the workspace switcher, and the dashboard.

| Field             | Required | Notes                                                |
| ----------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Organization Name | Yes      | What people see everywhere your org shows up.        |
| Description       | No       | A short summary of what your group does.             |
| Website           | Yes      | Must be a valid URL.                                 |
| Address           | No       | Used for invoices and contracts.                     |
| Logo (Light)      | No       | For light-themed UIs. PNG, JPG, or WEBP. Max 200 KB. |
| Logo (Dark)       | No       | For dark-themed UIs. Same formats and size limit.    |

### Update general settings

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher in the top-left of the dashboard and select your
    organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Settings">Click **Settings** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Edit the General section">
    Update any field. Required fields are marked.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save">
    Click **Save** at the bottom of the section. An "Unsaved changes" reminder
    appears next to the button until you save. Select **Cancel** to discard
    changes to this section.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
  Upload both a light and a dark logo if you have versions for each theme.
  qBraid picks the right one automatically based on the viewer's theme.
</Tip>

## Member settings

Email invitations use the role selected by the inviter. Invite codes always join people as Members on Free, regardless of the default-role and automatic-seat settings below. Change a member's role or assign a paid seat afterward when needed.

Automatic seat assignment runs when a member accepts an email invitation or an administrator activates a membership. It requires an available seat. Seat-assignment credits apply to future seat assignments, including manual assignments to existing members.

| Setting                  | What it does                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Auto-assign Default Role | Stores the default-role preference. It does not override an email invitation or invite code.                                         |
| Default Role             | Choose Member, Manager, or Admin. Use the invitation form or **Members > Edit Role** to set a member's actual role.                  |
| Auto-assign Seats        | When **Enabled**, attempts to assign an available seat on email acceptance or membership activation. Invite-code joins are excluded. |
| Seat Assignment Credits  | Credits to transfer from the org wallet whenever a seat gets assigned (manual or automatic). Max 100,000.                            |

<Frame>
  <img
    src="https://5iv4rqgitg.ufs.sh/f/75CeDcn3E50nKYgzpa2IhwkxcPtRs2nLmr4z1DGVlQTayYve"
    alt="Member Settings showing default role, automatic role and seat assignment controls, seat assignment credits, and Save"
  />
</Frame>

Member settings control automatic seat assignment and the credits allocated with a seat.

### Update member settings

<Steps>
  <Step title="Switch to your organization">
    Open the workspace switcher and select your organization.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Settings">Click **Settings** in the sidebar.</Step>
  <Step title="Scroll to Member Settings">Below the General section.</Step>
  <Step title="Edit the fields">
    Change auto-assign behavior, default role, or seat credits.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save">Click **Save**.</Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  A membership can become active even if automatic seat assignment fails. Check
  **Billing > Seat Management** after acceptance or activation. If no seat was
  assigned, check available seats and the credits needed for its allocation,
  then [assign a seat manually](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/seats#assign-a-seat).
</Note>

## Ownership and deletion

The owner-only **Danger Zone** displays disabled **Transfer** and **Delete** controls marked **Coming soon**. Organization deletion is not available there.

Ownership transfer is available from **Members > Edit Role** for another active member. Follow [Transfer ownership](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/members#transfer-ownership) to use the working flow.


# Explore catalog
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/explore-catalog

Find projects, courses, events, and challenges, or submit a project for the qBraid catalog.

For partner onboarding, custom environments, and publication review, see the [Partner guide](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/explore).

## Find a project

Open [Explore](https://account.qbraid.com/explore) and search the project catalog. Select a project to read its README, releases, repository information, and tags.

When a project offers a Lab launch, use its launch control to clone the repository and start a compute environment. Review the selected workspace and compute profile before launching. A listed project can have restricted access or show **Coming Soon** before its public release.

## Submit your project

1. Prepare a GitHub repository with the code and a README that explains how to use it.
2. Open **Explore**.
3. Select **Add your project**, then **Get Started**.
4. Enter the project title and GitHub repository URL.
5. Submit the request for review.

qBraid fetches the repository's description, README, and language information from GitHub. A successful submission displays **Request Submitted**. Submission does not publish the project immediately.

If the project needs a custom environment, follow the [Partner guide](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/explore#step-2-send-us-environment-and-project-details) to send dependencies, runtime requirements, logos, and listing details. The guide covers environment testing and publication review.

## Events and challenges

Use **Events & Hackathons** for upcoming events and archived event details. Registration, meeting, and website links depend on the event. The **Challenges** tab contains available challenges and their entry requirements.

## Learn

Open [Learn](https://account.qbraid.com/learn) to browse and search courses. Select a course for its description and available learning materials. Availability and access depend on the course. See [Learn with qBook](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/learning) for course launch and resume instructions.

The Explore page links to qBraid's Discord and GitHub communities. Use [Support](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/support) for account help. The standalone Community page is a placeholder.


# Partner guide
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/explore

Prepare a project and its environment for publication on qBraid Explore.

# Adding your project

Use this guide to contribute a solution or project to the qBraid [Explore page](https://account.qbraid.com/explore). qBraid reviews the project and prepares its environment so users can run it in Lab.

To browse projects, events, and challenges, or submit a project through Account, see [Explore catalog](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/explore-catalog).

## Step 1: Create a public GitHub repository

Create a public GitHub repository containing your project. You can include example notebooks, executable Python files, or code in other languages, such as C++ or Julia.

Include a README that describes the project and explains how to use it. Review existing Explore projects for examples, or ask your qBraid contact for guidance.

qBraid reviews your README and provides feedback. If it does not clearly describe the project, or includes setup instructions that do not apply to qBraid, we may ask for a separate Markdown file with qBraid-specific instructions. We can link the listing to that file so users see it when they open the project.

## Step 2: Send us environment and project details

Send all the details below in one email to [contact@qbraid.com](mailto:contact@qbraid.com) or your qBraid point of contact. We use these details to create the environment and prepare the project listing.

### Environment details

- Send the minimal package dependencies needed to run your code and examples, such as a `requirements.txt` or the relevant dependencies from `pyproject.toml`. Do not send a full `pip list`.
- Include square logos in both light and dark versions. qBraid uses them for the environment sidebar image and kernel logo.
- State any non-Python runtime or GPU requirements. We can arrange a custom Docker container or GPU resources and confirm the requirements with you.

### Project details

- Include a one- or two-sentence description for Explore.
- Provide tags that help users find the project.
- Include the public GitHub repository URL from Step 1.

If you have already submitted the project through **Add your project** in Account, mention that request in the email so we can match it to the environment details. The in-app form does not replace the environment requirements above.

## Step 3: What happens next

1. qBraid creates the environment and shares it with your qBraid account.
2. Find it under **Shared environments** in Lab and test your code and examples.
3. Tell your qBraid contact about any changes you need.
4. Once you are satisfied with the environment, qBraid adds the project to Explore.
5. Review the published listing and request any final changes.

## Questions?

Contact [contact@qbraid.com](mailto:contact@qbraid.com) or your qBraid point of contact.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/overview

<div
  style={{ display: "flex", justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}
>
  <img
    src="/v2/lab/_static/lab_banner.png"
    alt="qBraid-Lab"
    style={{ width: "200", height: "auto", margin: "0" }}
    className="block dark:hidden"
  />
  <img
    src="/v2/lab/_static/lab_banner_dark.png"
    alt="qBraid-Lab"
    style={{ width: "200", height: "auto", margin: "0" }}
    className="hidden dark:block"
  />
</div>

<div style={{ textAlign: "center", marginTop: "-8px" }}>
  _A web-based IDE optimized for quantum computing._
</div>

[qBraid Lab](https://lab.qbraid.com/) is a web-based IDE providing curated software tools for researchers and developers in quantum computing.

- Hosts **30+** configurable virtual environments spanning quantum machine learning, quantum chemistry, quantum error correction, and more.
- Integrates with **GitHub**, **Slack**, and AI coding assistants like **Claude Code** and **Codex**.
- **Collaborative tools** enable sharing custom environments.
- Provides direct access to a robust suite of computing resources, encompassing scalable **CPUs**, **GPUs**, and **QPUs**.

## Operating System

qBraid offers several specialized Lab instances tailored to various applications and use cases. However, the
standard and most widely used qBraid Lab instance is built on [Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)](https://releases.ubuntu.com/22.04/)
and utilizes an [x86_64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X86-64) architecture.

To discuss projects with specific system requirements, please [contact us](https://www.qbraid.com/contact).


# Getting Started
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/getting-started

This section will walk you through the basics of using the Lab interface and managing your server instance.

## Launch Lab

### Starting an Instance

From your [account page](https://account.qbraid.com/), select a compute profile and click **Launch** to start your quantum environment.

qBraid Lab offers two types of instances:

- **Subscription instances** (CPU): Included with your plan, billed against your monthly compute hours. Available in Small (2 vCPU), Medium (4 vCPU), and Large (8 vCPU) configurations. Your files are automatically synced from cloud storage on each launch.
- **On-demand instances** (GPU + high-spec CPU): Pay-as-you-go with [qBraid credits](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/home/pricing#credits), billed per minute. Includes 20+ GPU configurations and high-spec CPU instances. See [On-Demand Instances](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/on-demand-instances) for the full lifecycle guide.

[Paid subscription tiers](https://www.qbraid.com/pricing) provide additional benefits including higher disk storage limits and compute hours.

<div
  style={{ display: "flex", justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}
>
  <img
    src="https://storage.googleapis.com/qbraid-static-assets/qbraid-docs/lab/launch-lab-part-1.gif"
    alt="launch_lab_new_account"
    width="150%"
  ></img>
</div>

Depending on its size, pulling an image may take up to 2 minutes for the first time. The next time you launch Lab, it will load much more quickly.

<Note>
  If launching fails with `Compute hours exhausted and insufficient credits`,
  you've used your monthly compute hour allocation. See
  [Troubleshooting](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/troubleshooting#launch-failed-compute-hours-exhausted)
  for how to upgrade your plan or switch the session over to credits.
</Note>

### Stopping Lab

To stop your running Lab instance:

1. Navigate to your [account dashboard](https://account.qbraid.com/)
2. Click **Stop Running Server** to stop the running instance

<div
  style={{ display: "flex", justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}
>
  <img
    src="https://storage.googleapis.com/qbraid-static-assets/qbraid-docs/lab/stop-lab.gif"
    alt="stop_lab_new_account"
    width="150%"
  ></img>
</div>

Stopping your server will not delete your data, but will stop it from running and consuming compute hours.

<Note>
  On-demand instances (GPUs, high-spec CPUs) have an additional **Terminate**
  action that permanently deletes the instance and its disk. See [On-Demand
  Instances](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/on-demand-instances#stop-vs-terminate) for
  details on the stop vs terminate distinction.
</Note>

## Lab interface

Once your image is pulled, you will be taken to the qBraid Lab interface. Here are a few helpful resources to get started:

- **Interactive tour**: Click **Start Tour** (pop-up at first launch, or **Help** drop-down) to begin a guided tour of all of the Lab extensions and their key features.
- **Help drop-down**: The top-bar menu **Help** drop-down contains links to qBraid user guides, demos, and other reference materials.


# Files
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/files

Open, create, rename, delete, and download files in the qBraid Lab file browser, and see how file sync differs on subscription and on-demand instances.

## File browser

The file browser and Files menu enable you to work with files and directories on your system. This includes opening, creating,
deleting, renaming, downloading, and copying files and directories. To open the file browser, click on the "Folder"
icon in the left sidebar (or use shortcut `Cmd+Shift+F`).

Navigate by double-clicking folders in the listing or clicking folders at the top of the directory listing. To open any file, double-click on its name, or drag the file into the main work area to create a new tab.

### Show hidden files

Hidden files are those whose names start with a "`.`" (e.g., `.bashrc`, `.gitignore`). These are hidden by default in the file browser to reduce clutter.

From the top-bar menu, click on **View**, and then select **Show Hidden Files** to toggle the visibility of hidden files in
the file browser.

<img src="/v2/lab/_static/hidden-files.png" alt="Show Hidden Files in the Lab View menu" width="95%" />

### Download files

To download a file, open the file browser, right click on the file, and select **Download** from the context menu.

<Note>
  If you can't launch Lab, you can still [download your files from the account
  dashboard](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/usage#download-your-files) without starting a session.
</Note>

<div
  style={{ display: "flex", justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}
>
  <img src="/v2/lab/_static/download-file.png" alt="Download action in the file context menu" width="95%" />
</div>

### Delete files and directories

To delete a file or directory, open the file browser, right-click on the item, and select **Delete** from the context menu.

You can also delete files and directories from the terminal using the `rm` command:

```bash
rm -rf [file_or_directory]
```

<Warning>
  qBraid Lab has no trash or recovery folder. Files deleted from the file browser or with `rm -rf` are removed immediately and cannot be restored. Double-check the item before confirming a deletion or running the command.
</Warning>

If you need to keep a recoverable copy, download the file first (see [Download files](#download-files)) or push it to a remote Git repository before deleting.

If you are deleting files to free up disk space, see [Disk Usage Management](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/usage-limits#disk-usage-management) for how to find large files and directories with `gdu` and how uninstalling unused environments can reclaim the most space.

### Download directories

The JupyterLab file browser does not support directory downloads. Use the terminal to zip a directory, then download the zip file.

First, open terminal in JupyterLab by opening a Launcher tab and selecting **Terminal** under the **Other** section.

<div
  style={{ display: "flex", justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}
>
  <img src="/v2/lab/_static/terminal.png" alt="Terminal launcher in JupyterLab" width="95%" />
</div>

Compress the directory with `zip`. Specify the output file name and directory path. The `-r` option includes subdirectories and their contents:

```bash
$ zip -r output_filename.zip /path/to/directory
```

Finally, download the zip file using the file browser. See [Download files](#download-files).

## File sync (subscription instances)

If your subscription Lab instance has been inactive for a few days, your files will be restored from cloud storage when you start a new session. A progress indicator appears above the file browser in the left sidebar while the sync is in progress.

<Note>
  Sync time depends on the size of your directory. Once the sync is complete, refresh
  the **Environments** sidebar to see all of your environments again.
</Note>

## Files on on-demand instances

On-demand instances (GPUs and high-spec CPUs) handle file persistence differently from subscription instances:

- On-demand instances do not sync files from cloud storage at launch. Each instance has its own disk.
- Use the **Files** tab to download files from cloud storage into an instance. Changes do not sync back to cloud storage.
- If the provider supports stopping, your disk and files remain available when you resume. Some instance types only support termination.
- Terminating permanently deletes the disk and all its files.

<Warning>
  Before terminating an on-demand instance, download any important files to your
  local machine or push them to a remote repository. See [On-Demand
  Instances](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/on-demand-instances#file-persistence) for more
  details.
</Warning>


# Notebooks
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/notebooks

Jupyter Notebooks (`.ipynb` files) are a community standard for communicating and performing interactive computing. They are documents that combine live runnable code with narrative text (Markdown), equations (LaTeX), images, interactive visualizations and other rich output.

qBraid Lab provides an interface to create and interact with Jupyter Notebooks, and includes a number of additional key features and integrations to enhance the quantum developer's experience.

## Create notebook

Create a notebook by clicking the `+` button in the file browser and then selecting a kernel in the new Launcher tab. In the Launcher tab, under **Notebooks**, clicking on an ipykernel associated with an activated environment will automatically launch a Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb` file) using that kernel.

<Info>
  The notebook document format used in qBraid Lab is the same as in the classic
  Jupyter Notebook. For more on how to use Jupyter Notebooks, see [Jupyter
  Notebooks](https://jupyter-notebook.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) and [Jupyter
  Lab:
  Notebooks](https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/notebook.html).
</Info>

## Switch notebook kernel

In the upper-right of any open notebook, you can see which kernel is in use. Clicking on the name of the current kernel, will open the kernel selector, and allow you switch to any other active kernel.

<Frame>
  <video
    src="https://storage.googleapis.com/qbraid-static-assets/qbraid-docs/lab/switch-kernel.mp4"
    autoPlay
    muted
    loop
    playsInline
    width="100%"
  />
</Frame>

## Pip (magic) commands

From inside a notebook, you must run all pip commands using the “magic” `%` operator.
For example, to install a new package from within a notebook cell, use:

```python
[ ] %pip install <my-package>
```

<Warning>
  WARNING: **Do not** use the `!` operator for pip install commands within
  Jupyter notebooks on qBraid. Doing so will install packages at the
  system-level, where they will _not_ be discoverable by your current notebook
  environment/kernel.
</Warning>

After installing any new packages directly from a notebook, you _must_ restart the kernel to see the changes take effect.


# Kernels
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/kernels

## Add and remove kernels

The IPython kernel is the Python execution backend for Jupyter.

Under **Environments**, choose an environment, and expand its panel. Click **Add kernel** to create an ipykernel for the environment.
This is a necessary step before running code in a Jupyter Notebook using a given environment.

Once "active", click **Remove kernel** to remove the environment's ipykernel from the launcher.
