# Usage Examples
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/algorithms/user-guide/examples

## Key Features: Load algorithms as PyQASM modules and QASM files

qBraid Algorithms provides a collection of quantum algorithms that can be loaded
as [PyQASM](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/pyqasm/user-guide/overview) modules, or
you can generate .qasm files to use them as subroutines in your own circuits.

### Loading Algorithms as PyQASM Modules

To load an algorithm as a [PyQASM module](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/pyqasm/user-guide/overview#the-qasmmodule-object), use the `load_algorithm` function from the `qbraid_algorithms` package, passing algorithm-specific parameters. For example, to load the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) algorithm:

```python
from qbraid_algorithms import qft

qft_module = qft.load_algorithm(3) # Load QFT for 3 qubits
```

Now, you can perform operations with the PyQASM module, such as [unrolling](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/pyqasm/user-guide/examples#inlining-and-unrolling), and
converting back to a QASM string:

```python
qft_module.unroll()
qasm_str = pyqasm.dumps(qft_module)
```

### Loading Algorithms as `.qasm` Files

In order to utilize algorithms as subroutines in your own circuits, use the
`generate_subroutine` function for your desired algorithm. By passing algorithm-specific parameters, and optionally a desired output path, you can
generate a .qasm file containing a subroutine for the parameterized circuit. For
example, to generate a QFT subroutine for 4 qubits:

```python
from qbraid_algorithms import qft, iqft
path = "path/to/output" # Specify your desired output path
qft.generate_subroutine(4) # Generate 4-qubit QFT in the current directory
iqft.generate_subroutine(4, path=path) # Generate 4-qubit IQFT in specified path

```

To utilize the generated subroutine in your own circuit, include the generated
.qasm file, and call the subroutine on a qubit register of the size specified
when generating the subroutine. For example, after running

```python
qft.generate_subroutine(4)
```

you can append `include "qft.qasm";` to your OpenQASM file, and call the
subroutine. For example:

```qasm
OPENQASM 3.0;
include "qft.qasm";

qubit[4] q;
bit[4] c;

qft(q);
measure q -> c;
```


# CLI
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/algorithms/user-guide/cli

## CLI Usage

qBraid Algorithms includes a command-line interface (CLI) for generating quantum algorithm subroutines.
These subroutines can either be saved in `.qasm` files or displayed directly in the terminal, providing
users with a convenient way to access and utilize quantum algorithms.

### Installation

To use the CLI, install with CLI dependencies:

```bash
pip install "qbraid-algorithms[cli]"
```

Or install from source:

```bash
pip install -e ".[cli]"
```

### Generate Subroutines

Generate quantum algorithm subroutines that can be included in other circuits:

- Generate QFT subroutine for 4 qubits

<CodeGroup>
```bash Command
qbraid-algorithms generate qft --qubits 4 --show
```

```output Output
QFT subroutine for 4 qubits generated successfully.
Output: /path/to/qft.qasm
Generated QASM:
--------------------------------------------------
OPENQASM 3.0;
include "stdgates.inc";


def qft(qubit[4] q) {
  int n = 4;
  for int[16] i in [0:n - 1] {
    h q[i];
    for int[16] j in [i + 1:n - 1] {
      int[16] k = j - i;
      cp(2 * pi / (1 << (k + 1))) q[j], q[i];
    }
  }

  for int[16] i in [0:(n >> 1) - 1] {
    swap q[i], q[n - i - 1];
  }
}
--------------------------------------------------
```

</CodeGroup>

- Generate IQFT subroutine for 3 qubits with custom name and show the circuit

<CodeGroup>
```bash Command 
qbraid-algorithms generate iqft -q 3 -o my_iqft.qasm --gate-name my_iqft --show
```

```output Output
QASM:
--------------------------------------------------
OPENQASM 3.0;
include "stdgates.inc";

def my_iqft(qubit[3] q) {
    int n = 3;

    for int[16] i in [0:n-1] {
        int[16] target = n - i - 1;
        for int[16] j in [0:(n - target - 2)] {
            int[16] control = n - j - 1;
            int[16] k = control - target;
            cp(-2 * pi / (1 << (k + 1))) q[control], q[target];
        }
        h q[target];
    }

    for int[16] i in [0:(n >> 1) - 1] {
        swap q[i], q[n - i - 1];
    }
}
--------------------------------------------------
```

</CodeGroup>

- Generate only the oracle for Bernstein-Vazirani

<CodeGroup>

```bash Command
qbraid-algorithms generate bernvaz -s "1001" --oracle-only --show
```

```output Output
Generating Bernstein-Vazirani oracle for secret '1001'...
Bernstein-Vazirani oracle generated successfully.
Output: /path/to/oracle.qasm
Secret string: 1001
Qubits needed: 4 + 1 ancilla
Generated QASM:
--------------------------------------------------
OPENQASM 3.0;
include "stdgates.inc";

def oracle(qubit[4] q, qubit[1] ancilla) {
    int[32] s = 9;
    int[16] n = 4;
    for int i in [0:n - 1] {
        if ((s >> i) & 1) {
            cx q[i], ancilla[0];
        }
    }
}

--------------------------------------------------
```

</CodeGroup>

- Generate a QPE subroutine for phase estimation:

<CodeGroup>
```bash Command 
qbraid-algorithms generate qpe --unitary-file gate.qasm --qubits 3 --show
```

```output Output
QPE subroutine for 3 qubits generated successfully.
Unitary file: /path/to/gate.qasm
Output: /path/to/qpe.qasm
Generated QASM:
--------------------------------------------------
OPENQASM 3.0;
include "stdgates.inc";
include "iqft.qasm";

gate custom_t q {
  p(pi / 4) q;
}

gate CU a, b {
  ctrl @ custom_t a, b;
}


def qpe(qubit[3] q, qubit[1] psi) {
    int n = 3;
    for int i in [0:n-1] {
        h q[i];
    }
    for int j in [0:n-1] {
        int[16] k = 1 << j;
        for int m in [0:k-1] {
            CU q[j], psi[0];
        }
    }
    iqft(q);

}
--------------------------------------------------
```

</CodeGroup>

### Examples


<div style={{ textAlign: "center", marginTop: "-8px" }}>
  _Universal command line interface for interacting with all parts of the qBraid
  platform._
</div>

The qBraid CLI manages cloud compute, quantum jobs, environments, and AI agents from your terminal. It can also route AI coding tools through qBraid as their provider, and send you Slack or email updates from long-running work.

## Getting started

The qBraid-CLI comes pre-installed and pre-configured in qBraid Lab:

- [Launch qBraid Lab &rarr;](https://lab.qbraid.com/)
- [Make an account &rarr;](https://account.qbraid.com/)

For help, see qBraid Lab User Guide: [Getting Started](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/getting-started).

### Local setup

If you prefer to use qBraid-CLI on your local machine, you can install it from PyPI with:

```bash
pip install qbraid-cli
```

<Warning>
qbraid-cli versions &lt;0.12 are *not* compatible with qBraid API V2. See [migration guide](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/rest/migration).

Use qbraid-cli &ge; 0.12.0 with API V2.

</Warning>

To manage qBraid [environments](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/environments) using the CLI, you must also install the `envs` extra:

```bash
pip install 'qbraid-cli[envs]'
```

To SSH into qBraid [compute instances](#manage-compute-instances) from your local machine, install the `compute` extra:

```bash
pip install 'qbraid-cli[compute]'
```

After installation, you must configure your account credentials to use the CLI locally:

1. Create a qBraid account or log in to your existing account by visiting
   [account.qbraid.com](https://account.qbraid.com/)
2. Open [API Keys](https://account.qbraid.com/account/api-keys) and create a key. See [API key management](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/api-keys) for scope and rotation details.
3. Save your API key from step 2 in local configuration file `~/.qbraid/qbraidrc` using:

```bash
$ qbraid configure
```

### Add the CLI to PATH on Windows

If you encounter a warning like:

```bash
WARNING: The script qbraid.exe is installed in 'C:\Users\<YourUsername>\AppData\Local\Packages\PythonSoftwareFoundation.Python.<version>\LocalCache\local-packages\Python<version>\Scripts' which is not on PATH.
```

You need to add the directory containing qbraid.exe to your system's PATH.

1. Copy the directory path provided in the warning.
2. Follow these steps:

- Open the Start Menu, search for "Environment Variables," and select "Edit the system environment variables."
- In the System Properties window, click the Environment Variables button.
- Under "User variables," locate the Path variable, click Edit, and add the copied directory.

3. Save the changes and restart your terminal.

# Configuration Files
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/user-guide/config-files

Manage your qBraid account credentials and settings

qBraid uses configuration files to store your account credentials and settings. The main configuration file is called `qbraidrc`.

## The qbraidrc file

The `qbraidrc` file is an INI-format configuration file that stores your qBraid account credentials and settings. It is located in your home directory at:

- Linux/macOS: `~/.qbraid/qbraidrc`
- Windows: `C:\Users\<username>\.qbraid\qbraidrc`

These qBraid tools use the configuration file:

- qBraid-SDK
- qBraid-CLI
- qBraid Jupyter Lab extensions
- qBraid VS Code extensions

### File structure

A typical `qbraidrc` file contains the following:

```ini
[default]
url = https://api-v2.qbraid.com/api/v1
api-key = <your-api-key>
```

### Creating new configuration file

To create a new `qbraidrc` file:

```
qbraid configure
```

This interactive command:

1. Prompts you to enter your API key
2. Sets the qBraid API URL
3. Creates the configuration file in the correct location

### Updating configuration values

To update a specific configuration value:

```
qbraid configure set <field> <value>
```

For example, to update your API key:

```
qbraid configure set api-key your-new-api-key
```

### Viewing configuration values

To view a specific configuration value:

```
qbraid configure get <field>
```

For example:

```
qbraid configure get api-key
```

To view all configuration values in your default profile:

```
qbraid configure list
```

### Finding your configuration file

To locate your `qbraidrc` file programmatically:

```python
from pathlib import Path

config_path = Path.home() / ".qbraid" / "qbraidrc"

print(config_path)
```

## Security note

Your API key provides access to your qBraid account. Keep it secure and never share it with others. If you believe your API key has been compromised, you can generate a new one from your qBraid account settings and update it using the CLI commands above.

See [API key security](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/api-keys#rotate-a-key) for more information.


# Environments
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/user-guide/environments

qBraid environments are simply [Python virtual environments](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html) in disguise.
The qBraid CLI provides convenient short-cuts to activate and install packages into your qBraid environments, however all
of the traditional commands to activate and manipulate Python venvs still apply. For example, you can activate an
environment using the [source command](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html#how-venvs-work):

```bash
$ source ~/.qbraid/environments/<slug>/pyenv/bin/activate
```

If you're working in terminal, you don't specifically need to activate a qBraid environment, as you can just specify the full path
to that environment's Python interpreter when invoking Python, e.g. `/<path-to-venv>/bin/python`. The same is true for `pip` commands.
So if you are attempting to install new packages into a qBraid environment from terminal or inside a notebook, make sure to use the full
pip path.

Simply running `pip install ...` will default to `/opt/conda/bin/pip`, which will cause dependency conflicts, and the installed packages
will be overridden the next time you launch lab.

### Install package

From Launcher, under “Other”, click on Terminal. By default, your qBraid terminal opens using Python (and pip) from
`/opt/conda/bin`. Packages that are installed directly at this top-level will _not_ persist between sessions. Instead,
use the qBraid CLI to list your environments,

```bash
$ qbraid envs list
# qbraid environments:
#

default                        /opt/.qbraid/environments/qbraid_000000
qsharp                         /opt/.qbraid/environments/qsharp_b54crn
qbraid_sdk                     /home/jovyan/.qbraid/environments/qbraid_sdk_9j9sjy
qiskit                         /home/jovyan/.qbraid/environments/qiskit_9y9siy
```

activate an environment, and perform your pip installs from there. For example, installing pytket into the qiskit environment:

```bash
$ qbraid envs activate qiskit
$ python -m pip install pytket
$ deactivate
```


# Magic Commands
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/user-guide/magic-commands

You can access the CLI directly from within [Notebooks](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/lab/user-guide/notebooks)
using IPython [magic commands](https://ipython.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactive/magics.html). First, configure
the qBraid magic command extension using:

```shell
$ qbraid configure magic
```

The above command can also be executed from within a Jupyter notebook using the `!` operator. Then, from within a
notebook cell, load the qBraid magic IPython extension using:

```python
In [1]: %load_ext qbraid_magic
```

Now you can continue to use the qBraid-CLI as normal from within your Jupyter notebook using the magic `%` operator, e.g.

```python
In [2]: %qbraid

In [3]: %qbraid --version
```


# qbraid
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid

The qBraid CLI — A unified interface for AI agents, quantum computing, Python environments, and cloud compute.

Version: [0.16.16](https://pypi.org/project/qbraid-cli/0.16.16)

Whether you're running AI coding agents locally or on cloud servers,
managing quantum experiments across providers, or setting up reproducible
Python environments — qBraid brings it all into one CLI.


**Options**:

- `-v, --version`: Show the version and exit.
- `--install-completion`: Install completion for the current shell.
- `--show-completion`: Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `lab`: Launch qBraid Lab (JupyterLab).
- `admin`: CI/CD commands for qBraid maintainers.
- `agents`: Manage AI coding agent sessions.
- `ai`: Use qBraid as your AI provider.
- `compute`: Manage cloud compute and SSH.
- `comms`: Send updates and read replies.
- `configure`: Configure CLI settings.
- `account`: Manage qBraid account.
- `devices`: Browse quantum devices.
- `jobs`: Submit and track quantum computing jobs.
- `projects`: Browse and install qBraid Hub projects.
- `skills`: Create, install, and share AI coding skills.
- `troubleshoot`: Diagnose qBraid platform issues.
- `envs`: Manage Python environments.
- `kernels`: Add, remove, and repair Jupyter kernels.
- `pip`: Run pip command in active qBraid environment.

# qbraid agents
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid_agents

Manage AI coding agent sessions.

Launch, monitor, and control AI coding agents.
Run Claude Code, OpenCode, or Codex in managed tmux sessions. Send
instructions, stream transcripts, handle permissions, and orchestrate
multiple agents — all from one place. Works locally and on remote
compute servers via SSH.

Use this when you want to:

- Spin up agents on specific repos or projects
- Watch what agents are doing in real-time
- Approve or deny tool-use permissions remotely
- Manage agents running on cloud compute machines
- Resume previous coding sessions

Getting started:

```bash
qbraid agents launch                    # Interactive launch
qbraid agents list                      # Show active sessions
qbraid agents watch <name>              # Stream live activity
qbraid agents send <name> --text "..."  # Send instructions
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `interrupt`: Interrupt one verified active turn.
- `jobs`: Inspect agent schedules and jobs.
- `register`: Register an agent session.
- `deregister`: Deregister an agent session.
- `list`: List agent sessions.
- `discover`: Discover new agent sessions.
- `status`: Show detailed status for an agent session.
- `update`: Update metadata fields on an agent session.
- `kill`: Stop an agent by name, session ID, or PID.
- `readiness`: Check this destination before launch.
- `machine`: Serve the fleet machine protocol.
- `settings`: Inspect or configure agent execution.
- `launch`: Launch an AI coding agent.
- `resume`: Resume a previous agent session.
- `send`: Send text to a running agent's terminal.
- `read`: Read recent terminal output from an agent.
- `notifier`: Wake idle agents when inbox mail arrives.
- `approve`: Approve a tool-use prompt.
- `watch`: Stream agent transcript.
- `attach`: Attach to an agent's terminal.
- `clean`: Clean up orphaned sessions.
- `send-to`: Send a message to another agent's inbox.
- `broadcast`: Broadcast to multiple agent inboxes.
- `team`: Show a team roster with unread counts.
- `hooks`: Manage agent lifecycle hooks.
- `keep-alive`: Opt-in local managed agent recovery.
- `queue`: Queue follow-ups for a managed runtime.
- `inbox`: Read messages sent to this agent's inbox.

## qbraid agents interrupt

Interrupt one verified active turn.

Request one Escape and pause queued input, without ending the agent process.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents interrupt [OPTIONS] {session_id}
```

**Arguments**:

- `session_id`: Exact destination session ID. [required]

**Options**:

- `--preflight`: Inspect availability and turn without sending Escape.
- `--compute <str>`
- `--request-id <str>`
- `--json`
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents jobs

Inspect agent schedules and jobs.

This observes provider-owned work. It never creates a schedule, wakes an
agent, or treats missing telemetry as an empty list. Manage tasks through
the agent's own terminal. Claude reports snapshots after completing turns;
other providers report unsupported until they expose an inventory.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents jobs [OPTIONS] {session_id}
```

**Arguments**:

- `session_id`: Exact qBraid session ID from agents list. [required]

**Options**:

- `-c, --compute <str>`: SSH alias for the owning machine.
- `--json`: Emit one JSON object; errors go to stderr.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents list

List agent sessions.

Use --compute to list on a remote server.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents list [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-t, --tool <str>`: Filter by tool (claude, codeq, codex)
- `--status <str>`: Filter by status
- `--tag <str>`: Filter by tag (repeatable)
- `--since <str>`: Time window (e.g., '1h', '30m', '2d')
- `-c, --compute <str>`: SSH alias for remote compute (runs list on remote)
- `-s, --search <str>`: Text search across name/cwd/tags
- `-a, --all`: Include stopped sessions
- `-l, --limit <int range>`: Entries per page [default: 25; x&gt;=1]
- `-p, --page <int range>`: Page number (non-interactive mode) [default: 1; x&gt;=1]
- `--sort <str>`: Sort by: recent, oldest, name, tool, status, cwd, model [default: recent]
- `--no-interactive`: Disable interactive pagination
- `--json`: Output as JSON array (for programmatic use)
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents status

Show detailed status for an agent session.

Without `--compute` this reads the local registry, which is per-host: an
agent on another machine is simply absent and reports as not found.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents status [OPTIONS] {session_id}
```

**Arguments**:

- `session_id`: Session ID (full or prefix) [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents update

Update metadata fields on an agent session.

--type, --team and --parent let agents started from a terminal join a
team after launch, so they can message each other. From your own shell
any change is allowed. Inside an agent, it may only place teamless
sessions or its teammates into a team it leads, never as or out of
leader. These are coordination guardrails, not a security boundary.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents update [OPTIONS] {session_id}
```

- `session_id`: Session ID (full or prefix) [required]

**Options**:

- `--name <str>`: Set terminal name for the session
- `--model <str>`: Set model name (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-20250514)
- `--cwd <str>`: Set working directory for the session
- `--status <str>`: Set session status (working, waiting, idle, error, stopped)
- `--type <str>`: Set the agent type (leader, worker, observer, reviewer); '' clears it.
- `--team <str>`: Join a team by id; '' leaves it.
- `--parent <str>`: Set the parent session (id, prefix or name); '' clears it.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents launch

Launch an AI coding agent.

Uses the owning Lab terminal when available; otherwise starts in tmux.

Detached agents may wait for approval until you open their terminal or dashboard.
Approval and execution mode are independent and remembered for resume.
--approval auto disables approval prompts; --execution-mode container
explicitly uses the current user's access without an extra Codex sandbox.
Choose it only where you trust the surrounding machine/container isolation.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents launch [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `--backend <auto|jupyter|tmux>`: auto: prefer the owning Lab terminal; jupyter: require Lab; tmux: run independently. [default: auto]
- `-t, --tool <str>`: Agent tool (claude, codeq, codex; claude-auto = claude --approval auto)
- `--cwd <str>`: Working directory
- `-n, --name <str>`: Agent name
- `-i, --instructions <str>`: Initial instructions
- `-r, --repo <str>`: GitHub repo URL, org/repo, or issue/PR URL
- `--type <str>`: Agent type: leader, worker, observer, reviewer
- `--parent <str>`: Parent session ID
- `--team <str>`: Team ID
- `--tag <str>`: Tags (repeatable)
- `-c, --compute <str>`: SSH alias for remote compute server
- `--request-id <str>`: Remote launch UUID retained for reconciling an interrupted request.
- `--execution-mode <native|workspace|container>`: Codex only: native uses Codex defaults; workspace adds its workspace sandbox; container uses current user access without an extra Codex sandbox (no sudo). Omitted preserves existing behavior. Independent of --approval.
- `--approval <ask|auto|manual|auto-review|yolo>`: manual: the agent asks you. auto-review: the tool's own automatic reviewer decides. yolo: no permission checks. ask/auto: legacy modes, unchanged.
- `--trust-hooks`: Codex only, DANGEROUS: run ALL enabled hooks (yours, the project's and plugins') without Codex's hook review, for this launch only. Not retained on resume. Refused with --repo. Independent of --approval and --yolo.
- `--trust-folder / --no-trust-folder`: Answer the agent's 'trust this folder?' prompt now (Claude, Codex), so a detached agent does not stop at it. The answer is remembered for later launches and resumes. Trusting a folder lets its own settings, hooks and MCP servers run. Default: Claude trusts the folder, except a fresh --repo clone; Codex asks.
- `--skip-bypass-confirmation`: Claude with --yolo: skip its bypass-permissions confirmation, for this launch only.
- `--yolo`: Claude: skip permissions. Codex: bypass approvals and its sandbox.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents resume

Resume a previous agent session.

Resumes with the selected terminal backend. With `--compute` the session is resumed
on that machine, and a session id is required -- the interactive picker
reads the local registry and cannot see another host's sessions.

`--confirm-owner-gone` is for a session whose old Lab (in another PID
namespace, after a restart) cannot be verified gone. Core's preflight runs
first; when it allows a confirmation, its reason and the risk are shown and
the person is asked (default No). Without a terminal it refuses unless
`--yes` is given. An agent must never pass `--yes` on its own judgement:
only after the person has confirmed that the old Lab is closed or restarted.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents resume [OPTIONS] [session_id]
```

**Arguments**:

- `session_id`: Session ID, prefix, or name. Omit for interactive picker.

**Options**:

- `--backend <auto|jupyter|tmux>`: auto: prefer the owning Lab terminal; jupyter: require Lab; tmux: run independently. [default: auto]
- `-n, --name <str>`: Agent name for the resumed session
- `--execution-mode <native|workspace|container>`: Override the recorded Codex execution mode for this resume.
- `--approval <ask|auto|manual|auto-review|yolo>`: Override recorded permissions for this resume. Omit to preserve them.
- `--trust-hooks`: Codex only, DANGEROUS: run ALL enabled hooks without Codex's hook review, for this resume only. Hooks are reviewed again on every run that omits it.
- `--trust-folder / --no-trust-folder`: Answer 'trust this folder?' for the folder it resumes in (remembered). Default: keep the answer given at launch.
- `--confirm-owner-gone`: For a session from a restarted Lab that cannot be verified: confirm its old Lab is closed or restarted, and resume anyway. Asks first; confirming while that Lab still runs starts a second copy of the agent.
- `-y, --yes`: With --confirm-owner-gone: do not ask. Agents must not pass this unless the person has confirmed the old Lab is gone.
- `-c, --compute <str>`: SSH alias for remote compute
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents send-to

Send a message to another agent's inbox.

For multi-recipient / team broadcast, use `qbraid agents broadcast`.

Same-host only: an inbox is a JSONL file under `~/.qbraid/inboxes/` on
the machine that owns it, so there is no `--compute`. Cross-host
messaging is not supported yet.

Delivery is a JSONL append at ~/.qbraid/inboxes/&lt;to-session-id&gt;.jsonl
(local host only — cross-host messaging isn't yet supported and will raise
a clear error). Permission rules (leader/worker/observer/reviewer) are
enforced by default.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents send-to [OPTIONS] {to} {text}
```

**Arguments**:

- `to`: Target session id (full or prefix), tmux window name, or terminal name. [required]
- `text`: Message body. [required]

**Options**:

- `--from <str>`: Sender session id. Defaults to $QBRAID_SESSION_ID (set by the qBraid launcher for every managed agent shell).
- `--type <str>`: One of: message, task_assignment, status_update, shutdown_request. Controls how the recipient's UI/hooks categorize it. [default: message]
- `--no-permission-check`: Skip the sender→target permission check (agent-type rules from qbraid_core.services.agents.types.can_message). Use for testing.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents broadcast

Broadcast to multiple agent inboxes.

Same-host only: an inbox is a JSONL file under `~/.qbraid/inboxes/` on
the machine that owns it, so there is no `--compute`. Cross-host
messaging is not supported yet.

Two selectors — pick exactly one:

- `--team &lt;team_id&gt;` — every session with that team_id (except sender)
- `--to A,B,C` — explicit id/prefix/name list

Delivery is all-or-nothing on target resolution: if any target can't be
resolved, NOTHING is sent (avoids partial-delivery surprises). Once
resolved, per-target send failures are reported individually; a partial
delivery exits with code 3.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents broadcast [OPTIONS] {text}
```

**Arguments**:

- `text`: Message body — delivered to every target. [required]

**Options**:

- `--team <str>`: Deliver to every session with this team_id (excluding the sender). Use one of --team or --to.
- `--to <str>`: Comma-separated list of target session ids/prefixes/names for multi-recipient send. Use one of --team or --to.
- `--from <str>`: Sender session id. Defaults to $QBRAID_SESSION_ID.
- `--type <str>`: One of: message, task_assignment, status_update, shutdown_request. Controls how the recipient's UI/hooks categorize it. [default: message]
- `--no-permission-check`: Skip the sender→target permission check. Use for testing.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents team

Show a team roster with unread counts.

Same-host only: an inbox is a JSONL file under `~/.qbraid/inboxes/` on
the machine that owns it, so there is no `--compute`. Cross-host
messaging is not supported yet.

Answers the leader-orchestrator question &quot;who is on my team, how many
unread messages do they have, and what was the last thing they heard from
anyone?&quot; — which today requires peeking each worker's inbox individually.

Rows are sorted with the current session first (identified via
$QBRAID_SESSION_ID), then by agent_type (leader → worker → observer →
reviewer), then by session_id.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid agents team [OPTIONS] {team_id}
```

**Arguments**:

- `team_id`: Team identifier (matches AgentSession.team_id). [required]

**Options**:

- `-w, --wide`: Show full session ids instead of the 12-char prefix.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents keep-alive

Opt-in local managed agent recovery.

Restore enrolled local conversations after an instance restart. A process exit in the same instance pauses recovery for attention. Off by default. Explicit Stop disables recovery. A compatible running host is required; these commands do not install a daemon or support remote compute.

```console
$ qbraid agents keep-alive [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `enable`: Enable recovery for one exact session.
- `disable`: Disable recovery; leave the agent running.
- `forget`: Remove an already disabled policy.
- `run`: Run the local recovery host.

Does not enroll or launch anything.


**Options**:

- `--json`: Print policy data as JSON.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Preserves the live conversation's recorded permissions.

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Disable recovery; leave the agent running.

### qbraid agents keep-alive run

Run the local recovery host.

Ctrl-C exits without disabling policies.

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid agents inbox

Follow, filter unread, and mark-read messages sent to this agent

- `-f, --follow`: Stream new messages as they arrive.
- `-u, --unread`: Show only unread messages.
- `-n, --limit <int>`: Max messages to show (most recent). [default: 50]
- `--mark-read / --no-mark-read`: Mark shown messages as read after display. Default on. [default: mark-read]
- `-w, --wide`: Show full session ids in the From column and title (not the 12-char prefix). Use when multiple senders share a prefix.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.


# qbraid compute
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid_compute

Manage cloud compute and SSH.

Manage cloud compute servers, profiles, and SSH access.
Start GPU or CPU servers on qBraid infrastructure. SSH in from any
terminal, connect your IDE (VS Code, Cursor), or launch AI agents
on remote hardware. Persistent storage across sessions.

Use this when you want to:

- Run heavy workloads on cloud GPUs without local setup
- SSH into a cloud dev environment from your terminal
- Connect VS Code or Cursor to a remote server
- Launch AI agents on more powerful hardware

Quick start:

```bash
qbraid compute up <profile>          # Launch an instance + configure SSH
qbraid compute status                # List your instances
qbraid compute instances ...         # launch/start/stop/terminate/ssh/...
qbraid compute down                  # Stop an instance
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `up`: Launch an instance and configure SSH.
- `down`: Stop an instance.
- `status`: List your instances.
- `list`: List compute profiles.
- `sessions`: List compute sessions.
- `usage`: Show compute usage summary.
- `instances`: Manage compute instances.
- `profiles`: Manage compute profiles.
- `server`: (deprecated) Use `qbraid compute instances`.
- `ssh`: SSH access to compute servers.

## qbraid compute up

Launch an instance and configure SSH.

Alias for `qbraid compute instances launch &lt;profile&gt; --ssh`. On-demand
profiles always launch a new instance; the subscription server attaches
if it's already running.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute up gpu-l4
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute up [OPTIONS] {profile_slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `profile_slug`: Profile slug to launch [required]

**Options**:

- `-c, --cluster <str>`: Subscription cluster ID
- `-t, --timeout <int>`: Seconds to wait (default 600 on-demand, 120 subscription)
- `--no-ssh`: Skip SSH configuration
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

- `--cleanup-ssh`: Remove the subscription SSH config

## qbraid compute instances

Manage compute instances.

One list for both tiers: on-demand instances (billed from your wallet, several at once) and the subscription server (one at a time).

Quick start:

```bash
qbraid compute instances launch <profile>   # new instance, waits, prints URL
qbraid compute instances list               # both tiers, rates, uptime
qbraid compute instances stop <target>      # keeps the disk; bills storage
qbraid compute instances terminate <target> # the only zero-cost state
```

&lt;target&gt; is an instance id, its hash, a label, a profile slug, or 'subscription'.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `list`: List your instances across both tiers.
- `show`: Show one instance in detail.
- `launch`: Launch a new instance from a profile.
- `start`: Start (resume) a stopped instance.
- `stop`: Stop a running instance; the disk is kept.
- `terminate`: Terminate an instance; deletes its disk.
- `set`: Change an instance's label or auto-stop.
- `ssh`: Configure SSH for a running instance.
- `history`: List terminated instances and what they cost.
- `availability`: Show on-demand capacity and rates by profile.

### qbraid compute instances list

List your instances across both tiers.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute instances list
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances list [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-c, --cluster <str>`: Subscription cluster ID
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute instances show

Show one instance in detail.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute instances show trainer
qbraid compute instances show subscription --show-url
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances show [OPTIONS] {target}
```

**Arguments**:

- `target`: Instance id, hash, label, profile slug, or 'subscription' [required]

**Options**:

- `--show-url`: Show the full URL including the auth token
- `-c, --cluster <str>`: Subscription cluster ID
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute instances launch

Launch a new instance from a profile.

On-demand profiles always launch a new instance — the tier is
multi-instance — and you're told if you already have one up. The
subscription tier is one server at a time, so launching attaches if it's
already running.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute instances launch gpu-l4 --ssh
qbraid compute instances launch gpu-l4 --label trainer --no-wait
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances launch [OPTIONS] {profile_slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `profile_slug`: Profile slug (see `qbraid compute profiles list`) [required]

**Options**:

- `--no-wait`: Return right after the launch is accepted
- `--ssh`: Configure SSH once the instance is ready
- `-t, --timeout <int>`: Seconds to wait (default 600 on-demand, 120 subscription)
- `-l, --label <str>`: Label for the new instance (on-demand)
- `--region <str>`: Preferred region (on-demand; a preference, not a pin)
- `-c, --cluster <str>`: Subscription cluster ID
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute instances start

Start (resume) a stopped instance.

Its disk is kept, so you pick up where you left off. With a profile slug,
resumes your stopped instance of that profile — and asks which if there
are several.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute instances start trainer
qbraid compute instances start gpu-l4 --ssh
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances start [OPTIONS] [target]
```

**Arguments**:

- `target`: Stopped instance: id, hash, label, or profile slug

**Options**:

- `--no-wait`: Return right after the start is accepted
- `--ssh`: Configure SSH once the instance is ready
- `-t, --timeout <int>`: Seconds to wait (default 600)
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute instances stop

Stop a running instance; the disk is kept.

A stopped on-demand instance keeps billing a small storage rate until you
terminate it. Refuses on clouds that can't preserve the disk (stop would
destroy it) — terminate those instead.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute instances stop trainer
qbraid compute instances stop subscription
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances stop [OPTIONS] [target]
```

**Arguments**:

- `target`: Running instance: id, hash, label, profile slug, or 'subscription'

**Options**:

- `-y, --yes`: Skip the confirmation
- `-c, --cluster <str>`: Subscription cluster ID
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute instances terminate

Terminate an instance; deletes its disk.

The only zero-cost state: a stopped instance still bills storage. Works
from any state, including one that is still starting.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute instances terminate trainer
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances terminate [OPTIONS] [target]
```

**Arguments**:

- `target`: Instance: id, hash, label, or profile slug

**Options**:

- `-y, --yes`: Skip the confirmation
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute instances set

Change an instance's label or auto-stop.

Example:

```bash
qbraid compute instances set a1b2c3d4 --label trainer
qbraid compute instances set trainer --max-session 240
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute instances set [OPTIONS] {target}
```

**Arguments**:

- `target`: Instance: id, hash, label, or profile slug [required]

**Options**:

- `-l, --label <str>`: New label ('' clears it)
- `--max-session <int>`: Stop after this many minutes running (0 disables)
- `--auto-stop <int>`: Stop after this many idle minutes (0 disables)
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid compute ssh

SSH access to compute servers.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute ssh [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `setup`: Configure SSH for the server.
- `connect`: SSH into the running server.
- `token`: Get SSH session token.
- `config`: Show or edit SSH configuration.
- `remove`: Remove SSH configuration for a host.

### qbraid compute ssh setup

Configure SSH for the server.

Sets up SSH config with a ProxyCommand that tunnels SSH through
the jupyter-server-proxy WebSocket endpoint. No websocat required.

On-demand BMA instances are handled automatically: if one is running
it's configured under its own alias; pass --instance to target a specific
one. Each instance gets an independent alias so several can be reachable at
once.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute ssh setup [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-c, --cluster <str>`: Cluster ID
- `-i, --instance <str>`: On-demand instance: id, hash, label, or profile slug
- `-t, --tool <str>`: Configure for specific tool: vscode, cursor, claude-code, codex
- `-a, --alias <str>`: SSH config alias (default: qbraid-&#123;cluster&#125;)
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute ssh connect

SSH into the running server.

This opens an interactive SSH session to the server. Pass --instance to
connect to a specific on-demand instance (resolves to its per-instance
alias from 'ssh setup --instance').

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute ssh connect [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-a, --alias <str>`: SSH config alias (auto-detected if not set)
- `-i, --instance <str>`: On-demand instance: id, hash, label, or profile slug
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid compute ssh token

Get SSH session token.

Retrieves a JupyterHub session token for SSH access.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid compute ssh token [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-c, --cluster <str>`: Cluster ID

# qbraid envs
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid_envs

Manage Python environments.

Create, install, upload, and share Python environments.
Isolated Python environments with automatic Jupyter kernel integration.
Create environments locally, upload them to the cloud, share with
teammates, or install pre-built environments from the catalog. Works
identically on qBraid Lab and local machines.

Use this when you want to:

- Set up a reproducible Python environment for a project
- Share your environment with collaborators
- Install a pre-configured environment (e.g., qBraid SDK, Qiskit)
- Publish an environment to the public catalog

Quick start:

```bash
qbraid envs create             # Create new environment
qbraid envs available          # Browse installable environments
qbraid envs install <slug>     # Install from cloud
qbraid envs list               # List local environments
qbraid envs upload <name>      # Upload to cloud
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `create`: Create a new qBraid environment.
- `uninstall`: Remove a local environment.
- `delete`: (Admin) Delete a cloud environment.
- `list`: List installed qBraid environments.
- `activate`: Activate qBraid environment.
- `available`: List installable environments.
- `info`: Show environment details.
- `install`: Install an environment.
- `upload`: Upload an environment.
- `health`: Check the health of an environment.
- `repair`: Repair a broken environment.
- `pythons`: List available Python versions.
- `config`: View or update environment configuration.
- `publish`: Manage environment publishing.
- `share`: Manage environment sharing via share codes.
- `groups`: Manage environment groups.
- `registry`: Manage the local environment registry.

## qbraid envs create

Create a new qBraid environment.

Run without options for an interactive walkthrough, or provide options via flags.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs create [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-n, --name <str>`: Name of the environment to create
- `-d, --description <str>`: Short description of the environment
- `-l, --logo <str>`: Company name for logo (e.g., 'ibm', 'google')
- `-r, --requirements <str>`: Path to requirements.txt file
- `-k, --kernel-name <str>`: Display name for Jupyter kernel
- `-t, --tags <str>`: Comma-separated tags
- `-y, --yes`: Automatically answer 'yes' to all prompts
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid envs uninstall

Remove a local environment.

By default this removes only the local copy — the cloud environment is
preserved so you can reinstall it later. Pass `--delete-cloud` to also
retire the cloud environment (requires ownership).

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs uninstall [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-n, --name <str>`: Name of the environment to remove [required]
- `-c, --delete-cloud`: Also delete the environment from qBraid cloud (requires ownership). By default only the local copy is removed and the cloud slug is preserved, so you can reinstall it later.
- `-y, --yes`: Automatically answer 'yes' to all prompts
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid envs delete

## qbraid envs info

Show environment details.

Get detailed information about an environment.
Accepts either a local env_id or a cloud slug. Shows information from
both local registry and cloud catalog when available.

```bash

$ qbraid envs info my_custom_abc123 # Custom environment
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs info [OPTIONS] {identifier}
```

**Arguments**:

- `identifier`: Environment identifier (env_id or slug) [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid envs install

Install an environment.

Installs a pre-built environment from cloud storage.
If the environment was built for a different platform or requires a Python
version not available on your system, you'll be offered options to either
create a similar local environment or proceed with the download anyway.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs install [OPTIONS] {env_slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `env_slug`: Environment slug to install (from 'qbraid envs available') [required]

**Options**:

- `-t, --temp`: Install as temporary environment (faster, non-persistent)
- `--target <str>`: Custom target directory (defaults to ~/.qbraid/environments)
- `-y, --yes`: Automatically proceed with default options without prompting
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid envs upload

Upload an environment.

Upload environment to qBraid cloud storage (private by default).
This uploads your local environment to make it available for sharing
with specific users. Use 'qbraid envs publish request' after upload to request
public visibility.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs upload my_custom_env
$ qbraid envs upload a1b2 --overwrite
$ qbraid envs upload my_env --group quantum_sdk
$ qbraid envs upload my_env --slug existing_slug_abc123  # Re-upload
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs upload [OPTIONS] {identifier}
```

**Arguments**:

- `identifier`: Environment name (if unique) or env_id to upload [required]

**Options**:

- `-s, --slug <str>`: Re-upload to existing slug (replaces previous upload)
- `-g, --group <str>`: Environment group to add this environment to
- `-o, --overwrite`: Overwrite existing uploaded environment
- `-y, --yes`: Skip confirmation prompts
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid envs health

## qbraid envs config

View or update environment configuration.

Without flags, prints the current config. With flags, applies the updates
and prints the new state. Multiple update flags can be combined in one call.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs config 5dcc
$ qbraid envs config myenv --description "Quantum sim env"
$ qbraid envs config myenv --tags "quantum,sim,gpu"
$ qbraid envs config myenv --add-tag gpu --add-tag cuda
$ qbraid envs config myenv --remove-tag deprecated
$ qbraid envs config myenv --system-site-packages true
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs config [OPTIONS] {environment}
```

**Arguments**:

- `environment`: Environment name, env_id, or slug [required]

**Options**:

- `-d, --description <str>`: Update environment description
- `--tags <str>`: Replace tags (comma-separated, use '' to clear)
- `--add-tag <str>`: Append a tag (repeatable)
- `--remove-tag <str>`: Remove a tag (repeatable)
- `--kernel-name <str>`: Update Jupyter kernel display name
- `--system-site-packages <str>`: Enable/disable inheriting packages from parent Python (true/false)
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid envs publish

Manage environment publishing.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs publish [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `request`: Request to publish environment.
- `status`: Check publish status.
- `cancel`: Cancel a pending publish request.
- `review`: (Admin) Mark as under review.
- `approve`: (Admin) Approve and publish.
- `deny`: (Admin) Deny a publish request.

### qbraid envs publish request

Request to publish environment.

Submits your uploaded environment to the public catalog for admin review. Once approved,
it will be publicly visible and installable by all users.

The environment must be uploaded first with 'qbraid envs upload'.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs publish request my_env_abc123
```

**Usage**:

```console

```

**Arguments**:

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs publish status

Check publish status.

Check the publishing status of an environment.
Status values:

    - none: Not submitted for publishing
    - requested: Waiting for admin review
    - pending: Under admin review
    - approved: Published to public catalog
    - denied: Publish request was denied

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs publish status my_env_abc123
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs publish status [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: Environment slug to check [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs publish cancel

Cancel a pending publish request.

This withdraws your publish request before it's approved.
You can resubmit later with 'qbraid envs publish request'.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs publish cancel my_env_abc123
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs publish cancel [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: Environment slug [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs publish review

(Admin) Mark as under review.

Transitions the environment from 'requested' to 'pending' status,
indicating an admin is actively reviewing it.

Examples:

```bash

```

**Usage**:

```console

```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: Environment slug to review [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs publish approve

(Admin) Approve and publish.

Approve and publish an environment to the public catalog.
This makes the environment publicly visible and installable by all users.
After approval, you'll be prompted to add the environment to a group
if it's not already in one.

Examples:


**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs publish approve [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: Environment slug to approve [required]

**Options**:

- `-g, --group <str>`: Add environment to this group after approval
- `--no-group`: Skip the group assignment prompt
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs publish deny

(Admin) Deny a publish request.

The owner will be notified with the denial reason.

**Usage**:


**Arguments**:

## qbraid envs share

Manage environment sharing via share codes.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs share [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `list`: List users with access.
- `create-code`: Generate a share code.
- `delete-code`: Delete the share code for an environment.
- `redeem-code`: Redeem a share code.

### qbraid envs share list

List users with access.

Shows all users with read or write access to the specified environment.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs share list my_env_abc123
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs share list [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: Environment slug to check [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs share create-code

Generate a share code.

Creates an 8-character code that others can redeem with
'qbraid envs share redeem-code' to gain read access to your environment.
Only the owner can generate codes.

Generating a new code invalidates any previous code for this environment.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs share create-code my_env_abc123
Share code: ABC12XYZ

# Share the code with collaborators, they can redeem it with:
$ qbraid envs share redeem-code ABC12XYZ
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs share create-code [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: Environment slug to generate share code for [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs share delete-code

Delete the share code for an environment.

Removes the share code, preventing new users from redeeming it.
Users who have already redeemed the code keep their access.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs share delete-code my_env_abc123
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs share delete-code [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: Environment slug to delete share code for [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid envs share redeem-code

Redeem a share code.

Redeem a share code to gain access to an environment.
Enter a share code received from an environment owner to gain read access.
The code is case-insensitive.

Examples:

```bash
$ qbraid envs share redeem-code ABC12XYZ
Access granted to: My Environment (my_env_abc123)

# After redeeming, you can install the environment:
$ qbraid envs install my_env_abc123
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid envs share redeem-code [OPTIONS] {code}
```

**Arguments**:

- `code`: Share code to redeem [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

# qbraid jobs
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid_jobs

Submit and track quantum computing jobs.

Monitor quantum jobs across all providers from a single interface.
View job status, results, and costs.

Use this when you want to:

- Check the status of submitted quantum jobs
- View results from completed experiments
- Track costs across providers
- Bundle related jobs into groups (qbraid jobs groups)

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `submit`: Submit a quantum job.
- `list`: List quantum jobs.
- `get`: Get a qBraid Quantum Job.
- `groups`: Manage job groups.

## qbraid jobs submit

Submit a quantum job.

Submit a quantum program to a device on the qBraid platform.
The program can be provided as a file path or piped via stdin.

Examples:

```bash
qbraid jobs submit circuit.qasm -d qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv --shots 100

cat circuit.qasm | qbraid jobs submit - -d qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv -f qasm2

qbraid jobs submit program.ll -d qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv --json
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs submit [OPTIONS] {program}
```

**Arguments**:

- `program`: Path to a quantum program file, or '-' to read from stdin. [required]

**Options**:

- `-d, --device <str>`: Target device QRN (e.g. 'qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv'). [required]
- `-f, --format <qasm2|qasm3|qir.bc|qir.ll|analog|pulser.sequence|quil|ionq.circuit.v0|problem>`: Program format. Required when reading from stdin. Auto-detected from file extension when omitted. Options: qasm2, qasm3, qir.bc, qir.ll, analog, pulser.sequence, quil, ionq.circuit.v0, problem
- `-s, --shots <int range>`: Number of shots to execute. [x&gt;=1]
- `-n, --name <str>`: Job name.
- `-t, --tags <str>`: Job tags as a JSON object (e.g. '&#123;&quot;experiment&quot;:&quot;bell&quot;&#125;').
- `--options <str>`: Runtime options as a JSON object.
- `--group <str>`: Group job QRN to associate this job with.
- `--json`: Output full job response as JSON (for programmatic use).
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid jobs list

List quantum jobs.

Lists quantum jobs submitted through the qBraid platform.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs list [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-l, --limit <int>`: Limit the maximum number of results returned [default: 10]
- `-s, --status <INITIALIZING|QUEUED|VALIDATING|RUNNING|CANCELLING|CANCELLED|COMPLETED|FAILED|UNKNOWN|HOLD>`: Filter by status: INITIALIZING, QUEUED, VALIDATING, RUNNING, CANCELLING, CANCELLED, COMPLETED, FAILED, UNKNOWN, HOLD
- `-v, --vendor <aws|azure|ibm|ionq|qbraid>`: Filter by vendor: AWS, AZURE, IBM, IONQ, QBRAID
- `-p, --provider <aqt|aws|azure|equal1|ibm|iqm|ionq|nec|oqc|pasqal|quantinuum|quera|rigetti|qbraid>`: Filter by provider: AQT, AWS, AZURE, EQUAL1, IBM, IQM, IONQ, NEC, OQC, PASQAL, QUANTINUUM, QUERA, RIGETTI, QBRAID
- `--page <int>`: Page number for pagination [default: 1]
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid jobs get

Get a qBraid Quantum Job.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs get [OPTIONS] {job_id}
```

**Arguments**:

- `job_id`: The QRN or ID of the job to get. [required]

**Options**:

- `--no-fmt`: Disable rich console formatting (output raw data) [default: True]
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid jobs groups

Manage job groups.

A group bundles related jobs into one session so the runtime can
track aggregate cost and status. Submit into a group with
`qbraid jobs submit --group &lt;qrn&gt;`.

Quick start:

```bash
qbraid jobs groups create -n my-batch
qbraid jobs groups list
qbraid jobs groups info <qrn>
qbraid jobs groups jobs <qrn>
qbraid jobs groups close <qrn>     # no more submissions, jobs run
qbraid jobs groups cancel <qrn>    # cancel group + non-terminal jobs
qbraid jobs groups delete <qrn>    # remove the record
```

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `list`: List your job groups.
- `info`: Show full details for one group.
- `create`: Create a new group.
- `close`: Close a group to new submissions.
- `cancel`: Cancel a group and its non-terminal jobs.
- `jobs`: List the jobs in a group.
- `delete`: Delete a group record.

### qbraid jobs groups list

List your job groups.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups list [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-s, --status <str>`: Filter by status (OPEN/CLOSED/COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED)
- `-p, --page <int range>`: Page number [x&gt;=1]
- `-l, --limit <int range>`: Results per page [x&gt;=1]
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid jobs groups info

Show full details for one group.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups info [OPTIONS] {qrn}
```

**Arguments**:

- `qrn`: Group QRN [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid jobs groups create

Create a new group.

Returns the new group's QRN — pass it to `qbraid jobs submit --group`
to attach jobs into the group.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups create [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `-n, --name <str>`: Human-readable group name
- `-t, --tags <str>`: Comma-separated key=value tags (values stored as strings)
- `-m, --metadata <str>`: Comma-separated key=value metadata (values stored as strings)
- `--max-ttl <int range>`: Max time-to-live in seconds (1-86400) [1&lt;=x&lt;=86400]
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid jobs groups close

Close a group to new submissions.

Existing jobs continue running; only new submissions are blocked.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups close [OPTIONS] {qrn}
```

**Arguments**:

- `qrn`: Group QRN [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid jobs groups cancel

Cancel a group and its non-terminal jobs.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups cancel [OPTIONS] {qrn}
```

**Arguments**:

- `qrn`: Group QRN [required]

**Options**:

- `-f, --force`: Skip confirmation
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid jobs groups jobs

List the jobs in a group.

Requires qbraid-core &gt;= 0.3.3 (the get_group_jobs helper).

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups jobs [OPTIONS] {qrn}
```

**Arguments**:

- `qrn`: Group QRN [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### qbraid jobs groups delete

Delete a group record.

Underlying jobs are not affected — cancel the group first if you want
to stop them. Idempotent: deleting an already-deleted group is a no-op.
Requires qbraid-core &gt;= 0.3.3 (the delete_group helper).

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid jobs groups delete [OPTIONS] {qrn}
```

**Arguments**:

- `qrn`: Group QRN [required]

**Options**:

- `-f, --force`: Skip confirmation
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.


# qbraid kernels
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/cli/api-reference/qbraid_kernels

Add, remove, and repair Jupyter kernels.

can have its own kernel visible in JupyterLab's launcher.

Use this when you want to:

- Make an environment available as a Jupyter kernel
- Fix a broken kernel that points to a missing environment
- Clean up orphaned kernels from deleted environments

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid kernels [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

**Commands**:

- `list`: List all available kernels.
- `add`: Add a kernel to Jupyter.
- `remove`: Remove a kernel from Jupyter.
- `status`: Check kernel status for an environment.
- `repair`: Repair a kernel's Python path.
- `clean`: Remove orphaned kernels.

## qbraid kernels list

List all available kernels.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid kernels list [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid kernels add

Add a kernel to Jupyter.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid kernels add [OPTIONS] {environment}
```

**Arguments**:

- `environment`: Name of environment for which to add ipykernel. Values from 'qbraid envs list'. [required]

**Options**:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid kernels remove

Remove a kernel from Jupyter.

**Usage**:

# qbraid skills

Skills are reusable prompt templates and tools that give AI agents
specialized capabilities — like running quantum circuits, deploying
to specific platforms, or following team conventions.

Use this when you want to:

- Give your AI agent domain-specific knowledge

- Create custom skills for your projects


**Usage**:


- `install`: Install a skill for AI coding tools.
- `uninstall`: Uninstall a skill from AI coding tools.
- `installed`: List locally installed skills.
- `check`: Check if a skill is installed and where.
- `share`: Share a skill with another user.
- `unshare`: Revoke a user's access to a skill.
- `shared-with`: List users with access to a skill.
- `share-code`: Generate a share code for a skill.
- `redeem`: Redeem a skill share code.

- `pending-reviews`: List skills pending review (admin only).
- `approve-publish`: Approve skill publishing.

- `mark-pending`: Mark a skill as under review (admin only).
- `create`: Create a new skill.

- `delete`: Delete a skill (owner or admin only).

## qbraid skills install

Install a skill for AI coding tools.

By default, installs to Claude Code (~/.claude/skills/). Use --target all
for every supported tool; --target codex or --target pi both land in
~/.agents/skills/, which Codex and CodeQ (pi) read.

In a tool's skills directory the skill is placed under its own name (not
its slug); with --path it is placed under its slug at that path. The
download is checked against the registry's checksum, and installing an
unchanged skill again is a no-op.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid skills install [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: The skill slug to install [required]

**Options**:

- `-t, --target <claude-code|codex|pi|cursor|copilot|all>`: Target AI coding tool(s) to install for [default: claude-code]
- `-p, --path <str>`: Install into this directory instead of a tool's skills directory
- `-f, --force`: Replace the installed copy even if it is unchanged or was not installed by qbraid
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

## qbraid skills uninstall

Uninstall a skill from AI coding tools.

By default, uninstalls from all supported tools. Accepts the registry slug
or the installed directory name.

**Usage**:

```console
$ qbraid skills uninstall [OPTIONS] {slug}
```

**Arguments**:

- `slug`: The skill slug (or installed name) to uninstall [required]

**Options**:

- `-t, --target <claude-code|codex|pi|cursor|copilot|all>`: Target AI coding tool(s) to uninstall from [default: all]
- `--path <str>`: Uninstall from this directory instead of the tool directories
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

# Overview
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/user-guide/overview

Learn to work with qBraid APIs

The qBraid REST API provides authenticated endpoints for devices, jobs, credits, and usage. The reference pages document JSON request and response formats. The separate [AI Gateway](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/integrations/ai-gateway) also supports streaming responses.

<Warning>
  This API is designed for server-to-server use. Browser (cross-origin) requests
  are restricted to an allowlist of qBraid origins, so calling the API directly
  from a web page on your own domain is blocked by CORS. Call it from your
  backend instead, where your API key also stays out of client-side code.
</Warning>

## OpenAPI specification

The machine-readable definition of the documented REST endpoints is available as an
[OpenAPI 3.1 document](https://docs.qbraid.com/openapi-v2.json). Download it to generate client
libraries, import the API into tools like Postman or Insomnia, or hand it to an
AI agent as a compact description of the documented endpoints, parameters, and responses. Platform features outside this specification have separate guides, including the AI Gateway.

## Quantum job flow

The diagram shows how an application converts a quantum program to an intermediate representation (IR), submits it through the qBraid API, and receives results from a quantum backend.

<img
  src="/v2/api-reference/_static/qbraid-runtime-api.png"
  alt="qBraid Runtime API Server"
  className="block dark:hidden"
/>
<img
  src="/v2/api-reference/_static/qbraid-runtime-api_dark.png"
  alt="qBraid Runtime API Server"
  className="hidden dark:block"
/>

For a client-side view of how the qBraid-SDK integrates with the qBraid API see the [Runtime overview](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/runtime/components#runtime-overview) in the SDK docs.

## Rate limiting

The shared rate limiter uses request-method and path counters, scoped to an IP address, user, organization, or user within an organization. The default window starts with the first request and expires after 15 minutes. Individual routes and organization configurations can override these defaults.

| Tier                 | Window | Max requests |
| -------------------- | ------ | ------------ |
| Unauthenticated (IP) | 15 min | 100          |
| Authenticated user or organization | 15 min | 1,000 |

Exceeding the applicable limit returns HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). Read the response rate-limit headers and wait before retrying. Authentication does not bypass endpoint-specific limits.

<Tip>
  Higher rate limits for your [organization](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/account/organizations/overview)
  are available upon request.
</Tip>

## Using the SDK and CLI

<Tip>
  The qBraid SDK and CLI wrap most of these endpoints. They handle authentication, the `{ success, data }` response envelope,
  pagination, and retries. Use the REST API when you need
  something the client doesn't cover.
</Tip>

Install with `pip install -U qbraid qbraid-cli`, then run `qbraid configure` once
with an [API key](https://account.qbraid.com/account/api-keys).

| To do this                               | CLI                      | Python SDK                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Submit & track jobs (incl. batch groups) | `qbraid jobs`            | `QbraidProvider`, `device.run()`, `GroupJobSession` |
| Browse devices & calibrations            | `qbraid devices`         | `provider.get_devices()`, `provider.get_device()`   |
| Check credits & account                  | `qbraid account credits` | `QbraidSessionV1`                                   |

For any endpoint without a dedicated wrapper, `QbraidSessionV1` (from
`qbraid_core`) is an authenticated session. Call methods such as `.get()` and `.post()`
against the API. The session sets the `X-API-Key` header.


# Migrating from V1
Source: https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/api-reference/rest/migration

This guide covers breaking changes when migrating from the qBraid V1 API to V2.

## What's changed

### Authentication and response structure

#### Base URL

| Version | Base URL                           |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- |
| V1      | `https://api.qbraid.com/api`       |
| V2      | `https://api-v2.qbraid.com/api/v1` |

#### Authentication header

| Version | Header      |
| ------- | ----------- |
| V1      | `api-key`   |
| V2      | `X-API-KEY` |

#### Response envelope

The device and job REST responses use a standard envelope:

```json
{
  "success": boolean,
  "data": { ... }
}
```

V1 returned raw payloads without this wrapper.

### Devices

V2 device objects include `paradigm`, `modality`, and `pricingModel` fields. Device identifiers use qBraid Resource Names (QRNs).

#### Routes

| Operation    | V1 Route               | V2 Route                    |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
| List devices | `GET /quantum-devices` | `GET /devices`              |
| Get device   | —                      | `GET /devices/{device_qrn}` |

#### Identifier

| Version | Field              | Example                    |
| ------- | ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| V1      | `qbraidDeviceId`   | `qbraid_qir_simulator`     |
| V2      | `qrn` (QRN format) | `qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv` |

#### Response fields

V2 adds:

| Field           | Description                                   |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `qrn`           | QRN identifier                                |
| `paradigm`      | `gate_model`, `analog`, `annealing`, `other`  |
| `modality`      | Device modality (e.g., `sparse_simulator`)    |
| `pricingModel`  | `fixed` or `dynamic`                          |
| `pricing`       | Object with `perTask`, `perShot`, `perMinute` |
| `directAccess`  | Boolean for direct device access              |
| `runInputTypes` | Array of supported input formats              |

V2 renames:

- `type` → `deviceType` (values: `SIMULATOR`, `QPU`)

### Jobs

V2 job responses use QRNs as identifiers. Job submissions specify the program format instead of using the `openQasm` or `bitcode` fields.

#### Routes

| Operation            | V1 Route                       | V2 Route                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Create job           | `POST /quantum-jobs`           | `POST /jobs`                  |
| Get job              | `GET /quantum-jobs`            | `GET /jobs/{job_qrn}`         |
| Get result           | `GET /quantum-jobs/result/:id` | `GET /jobs/{job_qrn}/result`  |
| Get program          | —                              | `GET /jobs/{job_qrn}/program` |
| Cancel job           | `PUT /quantum-jobs/cancel/:id` | `POST /jobs/{job_qrn}/cancel` |
| Delete job           | —                              | `DELETE /jobs/{job_qrn}`      |
| Delete multiple jobs | `DELETE /quantum-jobs/:ids`    | `DELETE /jobs?qrns=[...]`     |

#### Request body

**V1:**

```json
{
  "qbraidDeviceId": "qbraid_qir_simulator",
  "openQasm": "OPENQASM 3; ...",
  "shots": 1000,
  "tags": {}
}
```

**V2:**

```json
{
  "deviceQrn": "qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv",
  "program": {
    "format": "qasm3",
    "data": "OPENQASM 3; ..."
  },
  "shots": 1000,
  "tags": {}
}
```

Key differences:

- `qbraidDeviceId` → `deviceQrn` (QRN format)
- `openQasm`/`bitcode` → `program.data` with explicit `program.format`
- `circuitNumQubits` removed (inferred from program)

#### Response fields

V2 adds these fields to job responses:

| Field            | Description                                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `jobQrn`         | QRN identifier (replaces V1's `_id`)                    |
| `batchJobQrn`    | Batch job reference                                     |
| `experimentType` | `gate_model`, `analog`, `annealing`, `other`            |
| `estimatedCost`  | Pre-execution cost estimate                             |
| `timeStamps`     | Object with `createdAt`, `endedAt`, `executionDuration` |
| `metadata`       | Extensible metadata object                              |

## What's the same

- API key authentication model (header-based)
- Core job lifecycle: create → poll status → get result
- `shots`, `tags`, `status` fields
- Job statuses: `INITIALIZING`, `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`
- Device statuses: `ONLINE`, `OFFLINE`, `UNAVAILABLE`

## Deprecated endpoints

The following V1 endpoints are **not available** in V2:

| Endpoint           | Notes                           |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| `POST /chat`       | Deprecated chat completions   |
| `GET /chat/models` | Deprecated chat model listing |

## Quick migration checklist

1. Update base URL to `https://api-v2.qbraid.com/api/v1`
2. Change auth header from `api-key` to `X-API-KEY`
3. Replace `qbraidDeviceId` with `deviceQrn` using QRN format
4. Wrap program in `{ "format": "...", "data": "..." }` object
5. Update route paths (`/quantum-jobs` → `/jobs`, `/quantum-devices` → `/devices`)
6. Handle new response envelope (`response.data` instead of raw payload)
7. Replace legacy chat integrations with the [AI Gateway](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/ai/integrations/ai-gateway). Its OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible responses use their own formats.

## OpenAPI

````yaml get /devices/{device_qrn}
openapi: 3.1.0
````

# Get Device Calibrations

## OpenAPI

````yaml get /devices/{device_qrn}/calibrations
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: qBraid Runtime API
  description: Public REST API for qBraid's quantum platform. Submit and manage quantum jobs, organize them into batch groups, and browse available devices and their calibration data. Authenticate every request with an API key (`X-API-KEY`).
  version: "2"
servers:
  - url: https://api-v2.qbraid.com/api/v1
    description: Live Server
security:
  - ApiKeyAuth: []
paths:
  /devices/{device_qrn}/calibrations:
    get:
      tags:
        - Devices
      operationId: getDeviceCalibrations
      summary: Get device calibration data
      description: "Retrieve the latest calibration snapshot for a device: qubit-level (T1, T2, frequency, readout/gate errors) and edge-level (two-qubit gate errors, gate lengths)."
      parameters:
        - name: device_qrn
          in: path
          required: true
          description: The device qrn (qBraid Resource Name).
          schema:
            type: string
            minLength: 1
            example: aws:tn1:qpu:device-name
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Success.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/GetDeviceCalibrationsResponse"
        "400":
          description: Invalid or missing QRN.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "404":
          description: Calibration data not found for this device.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
components:
  schemas:
    ErrorResponse:
      type: object
      required:
        - success
        - message
        - error
      description: Standard error envelope returned for 4xx/5xx responses.
      properties:
        success:
          type: boolean
          example: false
        message:
          type: string
          description: Human-readable error message.
        error:
          type: object
          required:
            - message
            - code
          properties:
            message:
              type: string
            code:
              description: Machine-readable error code (string) or HTTP status (integer).
              oneOf:
                - type: string
                - type: integer
          additionalProperties: true
    EdgeEntry:
      type: object
      required:
        - source
        - target
        - value
      properties:
        source:
          type: integer
        target:
          type: integer
        value:
          type: number
    QubitCalibration:
      type: object
      description: Qubit-level properties; presence depends on the provider.
      properties:
        t1:
          type: number
        t2:
          type: number
        frequency:
          type: number
        readoutError:
          type: number
        gateError:
          type: object
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          description: Per-single-qubit-gate error, keyed by gate name.
    DeviceCalibration:
      type: object
      required:
        - deviceQRNs
        - provider
        - lastCalibrated
        - fetchedAt
        - qubits
        - edges
      properties:
        _id:
          type: string
        deviceQRNs:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
        provider:
          type: string
        lastCalibrated:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        fetchedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        qubits:
          type: object
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/QubitCalibration"
          description: Qubit-level properties keyed by qubit index (string).
        edges:
          type: object
          description: Edge-level properties keyed by metric name, then by source-qubit key, to a list of edge entries.
          additionalProperties:
            type: object
            additionalProperties:
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/EdgeEntry"
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        updatedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
    GetDeviceCalibrationsResponse:
      type: object
      required:
        - success
        - data
      properties:
        success:
          type: boolean
          example: true
        data:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/DeviceCalibration"
      title: GetDeviceCalibrationsResponse
  securitySchemes:
````
